name: abc
description: ABC News (Australian Broadcasting Corporation): search news, read top stories by state edition, browse topics, sections, authors and article metadata from abc.net.au/news.

commands.name: search-news
commands.summary: Keyword search across ABC News content (articles, video, audio) via the site's Algolia index

params.name: filters
params.description: Algolia filter expression. Empty means no filter. Read (articles): 'contentType:Article OR contentType:article OR contentType:Recipe OR contentType:recipe'. Watch: 'contentType:video'. Listen: 'conten

bodyTemplate.query: {query}

commands.name: get-top-stories
commands.summary: Homepage top stories for the national edition or a state edition

params.name: view
params.description: Edition: national, or a state/territory code such as nsw, vic, qld, wa, sa, tas, act, nt (national and nsw were recorded)

commands.name: list-topic-stories
commands.summary: Paginated JSON list of stories for a topic, by the topic's internal documentId (e.g. 1450 = Climate Change)

params.name: documentId
params.description: Internal topic collection id (Climate Change = 1450). Found in the topic page's embedded data.

commands.name: list-topic-page
commands.summary: Latest stories on a topic page by topic slug (first page, server-rendered)

params.name: topic
params.description: Topic slug as in /news/topic/{slug}, e.g. climate-change

commands.name: list-section-stories
commands.summary: Story headlines from a news section page, e.g. justin (latest news), politics, world, business

params.name: section
params.description: Section slug: justin (Just In / latest), politics, world, business, health, science, environment, sport, ...

commands.name: get-article
commands.summary: Article metadata (headline, description, dates, authors, keywords) from an article URL's date, slug and id

params.name: date
params.description: Date segment of the article URL, YYYY-MM-DD

params.name: slug
params.description: Slug segment of the article URL

commands.name: list-author-stories
commands.summary: Latest stories by an ABC reporter, from their profile page

params.name: id
params.description: Numeric author id from the profile URL

commands.name: list-topics
commands.summary: A-Z topics library: topics starting with a letter (links to /news/topic/{slug})

params.name: letter
params.description: Lowercase letter a-z, or 0-9 for numeric topics

commands.name: list-location-topics
commands.summary: A-Z location topics (places) starting with a letter

notes: Public site, no login needed. Search uses ABC's public search-only Algolia key (index news_prod_all), which covers all ABC content (news, iview, listen). Use the filters param to restrict by contentType or siteTitle.
Article links from listings look like /news/YYYY-MM-DD/slug/id. Split such a link into date, slug and id for get-article.
list-topic-stories needs the topic's internal documentId (Climate Change = 1450), not the slug. For a quick first page by slug, use list-topic-page.
get-top-stories returns state editions via view=nsw|vic|qld|wa|sa|tas|act|nt. Only national and nsw were observed.
Search pages are 0-based: page=1 is the second page.
about: ABC News (Australian Broadcasting Corporation): search news, read top stories by state edition, browse topics, sections, authors and article metadata…

name: airnow
description: AirNow.gov (EPA) U.S. air quality: current and forecast AQI by location, reporting-area and monitor-site history, state tables, national top AQI list, state alerts and site search. The CLI calls airnowgovapi.com and related JSON endpoints directly.

commands.name: suggest-reporting-areas
commands.summary: Autocomplete AirNow reporting area names (e.g. 'Denver-Boulder, CO') from a city name or ZIP fragment

params.name: term
params.description: Partial city name or ZIP code

commands.name: geocode-location
commands.summary: Resolve a U.S. city, region or ZIP code to latitude/longitude (x=longitude, y=latitude) for use with get-current-aqi and get-weather

params.name: location
params.description: City name, 'City, ST' or ZIP code

commands.name: get-current-aqi
commands.summary: Get current observed AQI and today/tomorrow forecasts per pollutant for the reporting area nearest a latitude/longitude

params.name: longitude
params.description: Longitude in decimal degrees (negative for the western hemisphere)

params.name: stateCode
params.description: Two-letter U.S. state code of the location, e.g. CO

commands.name: get-reporting-area-location
commands.summary: Get the latitude/longitude of a named reporting area

params.name: reportingArea
params.description: Reporting area name, e.g. Austin or Denver-Boulder

commands.name: get-reporting-area-providers
commands.summary: Get the data and forecast provider agencies (with URLs) for a reporting area

commands.name: get-interpolated-pm25
commands.summary: Get the current interpolated PM2.5 AQI and category for a reporting area

commands.name: get-weather
commands.summary: Get current weather (temperature °F, wind, humidity, pressure) at a latitude/longitude

commands.name: get-reporting-area-hourly
commands.summary: Get the last 24 hours of hourly AQI (with dominant pollutant) for a reporting area

params.name: reportingArea
params.description: Reporting area name exactly as AirNow spells it

commands.name: get-reporting-area-daily
commands.summary: Get the last 30 days of daily AQI (with dominant pollutant) for a reporting area

params.name: reportingArea
params.description: Reporting area name exactly as AirNow spells it

commands.name: get-site-hourly
commands.summary: Get the last 24 hours of hourly AQI and concentrations per pollutant for a monitoring site

params.name: siteId
params.description: Monitor site ID (the siteID field from get-current-aqi, e.g. 9-digit AQS code 060750005 or 12-digit 840080010010)

commands.name: get-site-daily
commands.summary: Get the last 30 days of daily AQI and concentrations per pollutant for a monitoring site

commands.name: list-state-aqi
commands.summary: List current observations and forecasts for every reporting area in a state

commands.name: get-state-history
commands.summary: Get daily AQI for ozone, PM2.5 and PM10 for every reporting area in a state on a past date

params.name: state
params.description: Full state name with the first letter capitalized, e.g. Texas

commands.name: get-top-aqi
commands.summary: List the U.S. reporting areas with the highest current NowCast AQI

commands.name: list-state-alerts
commands.summary: List states that currently have an AirNow notification (e.g. Wildfires) and its alert type

commands.name: search-site
commands.summary: Keyword search of AirNow.gov pages and documents (EPA search, scoped to www.airnow.gov), 10 results per page

params.name: filter
params.description: Extra facet filter in Solr syntax, e.g. filetype_s:"PDF" or displaylanguage_s:"English"

notes: Typical flow: geocode-location (or suggest-reporting-areas) -> get-current-aqi with lat/lon (location.y = latitude, location.x = longitude) -> use the reportingArea, stateCode and siteID from that result for the history and site commands.
In AQI results dataType 'O' means an observation and 'F' means a forecast. isPrimary marks the pollutant that drives the area's AQI.
In history arrays a value of -999 means missing data. aqi, conc and param line up index-by-index with utcDateTimes.
Reporting area names must match AirNow spelling exactly (e.g. 'Denver-Boulder', 'San Francisco'). Spaces are URL-encoded in path params.
get-state-history takes the full state name (Texas). list-state-aqi takes the two-letter code (TX).
Raw search responses also include facet_counts.facet_fields (filetype_s, displaylanguage_s, ...) that list the available filter values.
about: AirNow.gov (EPA) U.S. air quality: current and forecast AQI by location, reporting-area and monitor-site history, state tables, national top AQI list, state…

name: anilist
description: AniList (anilist.co) is an anime and manga database and tracker. This CLI sends read-only queries to AniList's public GraphQL API (https://graphql.anilist.co), the same API the web app uses. It covers searching and filtering anime and manga, media details, characters, staff, relations, reviews, recommendations, stats, character, staff and studio lookups, and the genre and tag lists.

commands.name: search-media
commands.summary: Search or browse anime/manga by keyword, with filters for type, format, status, season, year, genre and tag, plus sorting. Covers trending, popular, this-season and top-100 lists via sort and season.

params.name: search
params.description: Keyword matched against titles and synonyms

params.name: type
params.description: Media type. Leave it out to get both anime and manga.

params.name: season
params.description: Anime airing season. Use it together with seasonYear.

params.name: seasonYear
params.description: Year the anime season started airing, e.g. 2006. Anime only.

params.name: genre
params.description: Genre name, exact case, e.g. Thriller, Action, Romance. list-genres returns the valid values.

params.name: tag
params.description: Tag name, e.g. Pirates, Time Skip. list-tags returns the valid values.

params.name: isAdult
params.description: true returns only adult (18+) titles, false excludes them. Leave it out for no filter.

params.name: sort
params.description: Sort order. SEARCH_MATCH ranks by relevance to the search keyword. SCORE_DESC gives the top-rated list, TRENDING_DESC trending, POPULARITY_DESC all-time popular.

bodyTemplate.query: query SearchMedia($page: Int, $perPage: Int, $search: String, $type: MediaType, $format: MediaFormat, $status: MediaStatus, $season: MediaSeason, $seasonYear: Int, $genre: String, $tag: String, $isAdult: Boolean, $sort: [MediaSort]) { Page(page: $page, perPage: $perPage) { pageInfo { total currentPage lastPage hasNextPage perPage } media(search: $search, type: $type, format: $format, status: $status, season: $season, seasonYear: $seasonYear, genre: $genre, tag: $tag, isAdult: $isAdult, sort: $sort) { id idMal type format status(version: 2) title { romaji english native } season seasonYear startDate { year month day } episodes chapters volumes averageScore popularity genres siteUrl } } }

commands.name: get-media
commands.summary: Get full details of one anime or manga by AniList id, or the best match for a title: titles, synopsis, dates, episodes/chapters, genres, tags, scores, studios, next airing episode, links.

params.name: id
params.description: AniList media id, the number in /anime/{id}/ or /manga/{id}/ URLs

params.name: search
params.description: Title to look up when the id is unknown. Returns the best match.

params.name: type
params.description: Restricts the lookup to anime or manga

bodyTemplate.query: query GetMedia($id: Int, $search: String, $type: MediaType) { Media(id: $id, search: $search, type: $type) { id idMal type format status(version: 2) title { romaji english native } synonyms description(asHtml: false) season seasonYear startDate { year month day } endDate { year month day } episodes duration chapters volumes source(version: 3) countryOfOrigin isAdult genres tags { name rank isMediaSpoiler } averageScore meanScore popularity favourites studios(isMain: true) { nodes { id name } } nextAiringEpisode { airingAt episode timeUntilAiring } coverImage { large } bannerImage trailer { site id } externalLinks { site url } siteUrl } }

commands.name: list-media-characters
commands.summary: List the characters of an anime or manga (the Characters tab), with role (MAIN/SUPPORTING/BACKGROUND) and voice actors in the chosen language.

params.name: language
params.description: Language of the voice actors returned

bodyTemplate.query: query MediaCharacters($id: Int, $page: Int, $perPage: Int, $language: StaffLanguage) { Media(id: $id) { id title { romaji } characters(page: $page, perPage: $perPage, sort: [ROLE, RELEVANCE, ID]) { pageInfo { total currentPage lastPage hasNextPage } edges { role node { id name { full native } siteUrl } voiceActors(language: $language, sort: [RELEVANCE, ID]) { id name { full native } languageV2 siteUrl } } } } }

commands.name: list-media-staff
commands.summary: List the staff of an anime or manga (the Staff tab) with their roles, e.g. Original Story, Director.

bodyTemplate.query: query MediaStaff($id: Int, $page: Int, $perPage: Int) { Media(id: $id) { id title { romaji } staff(page: $page, perPage: $perPage, sort: [RELEVANCE, ID]) { pageInfo { total currentPage lastPage hasNextPage } edges { role node { id name { full native } primaryOccupations siteUrl } } } } }

commands.name: get-media-relations
commands.summary: List the media related to an anime or manga (adaptations, sequels, prequels, side stories, spin-offs) with the relation type.

bodyTemplate.query: query MediaRelations($id: Int) { Media(id: $id) { id title { romaji } relations { edges { relationType(version: 2) node { id type format status(version: 2) title { romaji english } startDate { year } siteUrl } } } } }

commands.name: list-media-recommendations
commands.summary: List the titles users recommend for a given anime or manga, ranked by recommendation rating.

bodyTemplate.query: query MediaRecommendations($id: Int, $page: Int, $perPage: Int) { Media(id: $id) { id title { romaji } recommendations(page: $page, perPage: $perPage, sort: [RATING_DESC, ID]) { pageInfo { total currentPage lastPage hasNextPage } nodes { rating mediaRecommendation { id type format title { romaji english } averageScore siteUrl } } } } }

commands.name: list-media-reviews
commands.summary: List user reviews of an anime or manga (the Reviews tab): summary, the reviewer's score and how many users found it helpful.

params.name: sort
params.description: Sort order. RATING_DESC puts the most helpful reviews first.

bodyTemplate.query: query MediaReviews($mediaId: Int, $page: Int, $perPage: Int, $sort: [ReviewSort]) { Page(page: $page, perPage: $perPage) { pageInfo { total currentPage lastPage hasNextPage } reviews(mediaId: $mediaId, sort: $sort) { id summary score rating ratingAmount createdAt user { id name } siteUrl } } }

commands.name: get-media-stats
commands.summary: Get statistics for an anime or manga (the Stats tab): rankings, score distribution, distribution of user list statuses (completed, planning, etc.), popularity and favourites.

bodyTemplate.query: query MediaStats($id: Int) { Media(id: $id) { id title { romaji } averageScore meanScore popularity favourites trending rankings { rank type context format year season allTime } stats { scoreDistribution { score amount } statusDistribution { status amount } } } }

commands.name: get-character
commands.summary: Get a character by id, or the best match for a name: name, description, age, birthday, favourites, and the anime/manga they appear in with Japanese voice actors.

params.name: id
params.description: AniList character id, the number in /character/{id}/ URLs

params.name: search
params.description: Character name to look up when the id is unknown

params.name: page
params.description: Page of the character's media appearances

bodyTemplate.query: query GetCharacter($id: Int, $search: String, $page: Int, $perPage: Int) { Character(id: $id, search: $search) { id name { full native alternative } image { large } description(asHtml: false) gender dateOfBirth { year month day } age bloodType favourites siteUrl media(page: $page, perPage: $perPage, sort: [POPULARITY_DESC]) { pageInfo { total currentPage hasNextPage } edges { characterRole node { id type format title { romaji english } siteUrl } voiceActors(language: JAPANESE, sort: [RELEVANCE, ID]) { id name { full } } } } } }

commands.name: search-characters
commands.summary: Search characters by name and return ids, names, favourites and their most popular media.

params.name: search
params.description: Character name or part of it

bodyTemplate.query: query SearchCharacters($search: String, $sort: [CharacterSort], $page: Int, $perPage: Int) { Page(page: $page, perPage: $perPage) { pageInfo { total currentPage lastPage hasNextPage } characters(search: $search, sort: $sort) { id name { full native } favourites siteUrl media(perPage: 1, sort: [POPULARITY_DESC]) { nodes { id type title { romaji } } } } } }

commands.name: search-staff
commands.summary: Search staff and voice actors by name and return ids, occupations and language.

bodyTemplate.query: query SearchStaff($search: String, $page: Int, $perPage: Int) { Page(page: $page, perPage: $perPage) { pageInfo { total currentPage lastPage hasNextPage } staff(search: $search, sort: [SEARCH_MATCH]) { id name { full native } primaryOccupations languageV2 favourites siteUrl } } }

commands.name: get-staff
commands.summary: Get a staff member or voice actor by id, or the best match for a name: bio, occupations, birthday, the media they worked on with roles, and characters voiced.

params.name: id
params.description: AniList staff id, the number in /staff/{id}/ URLs

params.name: search
params.description: Name to look up when the id is unknown

params.name: page
params.description: Page of the staff's media and characters lists

params.name: perPage
params.description: Items per page in each list, maximum 50

bodyTemplate.query: query GetStaff($id: Int, $search: String, $page: Int, $perPage: Int) { Staff(id: $id, search: $search) { id name { full native alternative } languageV2 primaryOccupations gender dateOfBirth { year month day } age yearsActive homeTown description(asHtml: false) favourites siteUrl staffMedia(page: $page, perPage: $perPage, sort: [POPULARITY_DESC]) { pageInfo { total hasNextPage } edges { staffRole node { id type format title { romaji english } siteUrl } } } characters(page: $page, perPage: $perPage, sort: [FAVOURITES_DESC]) { pageInfo { total hasNextPage } nodes { id name { full } siteUrl } } } }

commands.name: get-studio
commands.summary: Get an animation studio or producer by id or name, with the media it produced, newest first.

params.name: id
params.description: AniList studio id, the number in /studio/{id}/ URLs, e.g. 11 for MADHOUSE

params.name: search
params.description: Studio name to look up when the id is unknown

params.name: page
params.description: Page of the studio's media list

bodyTemplate.query: query GetStudio($id: Int, $search: String, $page: Int, $perPage: Int) { Studio(id: $id, search: $search) { id name isAnimationStudio favourites siteUrl media(page: $page, perPage: $perPage, sort: [START_DATE_DESC], isMain: true) { pageInfo { total currentPage lastPage hasNextPage } nodes { id type format title { romaji english } seasonYear averageScore siteUrl } } } }

commands.name: list-genres
commands.summary: List all genre names accepted by the search-media --genre filter.

bodyTemplate.query: query Genres { GenreCollection }

commands.name: list-tags
commands.summary: List all media tags (name, category, description, adult flag) accepted by the search-media --tag filter.

bodyTemplate.query: query Tags { MediaTagCollection { id name category description isAdult } }

notes: All commands are anonymous, read-only GraphQL POSTs to https://graphql.anilist.co (JSON body {operationName, query, variables}). No login or cookies are needed.

The explorer held the site's GraphQL calls (39 held), so no GraphQL request or response was ever recorded. The queries above are written from the public schema at docs.anilist.co, not copied from traffic, and no response shape was observed. If a command returns an 'errors' array, check the field and argument names against docs.anilist.co/reference.
The commands depend on omitted optional params being dropped from 'variables' or sent as null. AniList ignores null arguments. An empty string or a literal '{param}' placeholder would break filters.
The API is rate limited: about 90 requests per minute normally, sometimes lowered to 30. A 429 response includes a Retry-After header.
Errors come back as HTTP 400 or 404 with an 'errors' array, for example a nonexistent id or an invalid enum value. Enum values are uppercase (ANIME, TV, SCORE_DESC, FALL).
Ids appear in site URLs: /anime/{id}/{slug}, /manga/{id}/{slug}, /character/{id}/{slug}, /staff/{id}/{slug}, /studio/{id}/{slug}. Anime and manga share one id space, so get-media takes either kind.
Site list pages map to search-media sorts: /search/anime/trending is TRENDING_DESC, /popular is POPULARITY_DESC, /top-100 is SCORE_DESC, /this-season is season plus seasonYear with POPULARITY_DESC.

The site's year=YYYY URL filter maps to --seasonYear, which only applies to anime. Site tags are passed through the 'genres' URL parameter, but the API separates them: use --genre for genres and --tag for tags.
Combining --type ANIME with a manga format such as MANGA, NOVEL or ONE_SHOT returns nothing.

Descriptions may contain light HTML or markdown, e.g.
, and ~!spoiler!~ markers.
Dates are fuzzy {year, month, day} objects whose parts can be null. nextAiringEpisode.airingAt is a Unix timestamp.
Server-rendered HTML pages (/anime/{id}/{slug}/, /manga/{id}/{slug}/, /search/anime/top-100) also embed schema.org JSON-LD. The GraphQL API gives the same data more completely.
about: AniList (anilist.co) is an anime and manga database and tracker.

name: arbeidsplassen-nav
description: arbeidsplassen.nav.no is NAV's Norwegian public job board. This CLI searches job ads with filters, sorting and paging, opens individual ads, and reads a few informational pages. The site is server-rendered, so most commands parse HTML.

commands.name: search-jobs
commands.summary: Search job ads (ledige stillinger) by keyword, with filters for county, publish date, category, extent, remote work, sector, experience and under-18, plus sorting and paging (25 results per page)

params.name: q
params.description: Free-text keyword (place, occupation or search term), e.g. 'utvikler'

params.name: county
params.description: County (fylke) in upper case, e.g. OSLO, ROGALAND, VESTLAND. Only one value per call has been tested.

params.name: published
params.description: Publish-date window: 'now/d' = published today, 'now-7d' = last 7 days

params.name: remote
params.description: Remote-work option, e.g. 'Hybridkontor' (seen in a recorded URL) or 'Hjemmekontor'

params.name: experience
params.description: Experience requirement, e.g. 'ingen krav til arbeidserfaring' (no experience required)

params.name: under18
params.description: Set true to show only jobs open to applicants under 18

params.name: sort
params.description: Sort order. Omit for most relevant; 'published' = newest first; 'expires' = soonest application deadline first

params.name: from
params.description: Result offset, in steps of 25 (0 = page 1, 25 = page 2, ...)

commands.name: get-job
commands.summary: Get one job ad by its UUID: title, employer, location, employment details, application deadline, apply link and full description

params.name: id
params.description: Job ad UUID (the last path segment of the url returned by search-jobs)

commands.name: get-auth-status
commands.summary: Check whether the current session is logged in to arbeidsplassen.no (returns ok and isAuthenticated)

commands.name: list-youth-shortcuts
commands.summary: List the youth landing-page shortcuts (/ung), such as jobs for under-18s and jobs that need no experience, with their search URLs

commands.name: get-import-api-info
commands.summary: Read NAV's info page about the job-ad import API (how employers and vendors can publish ads to arbeidsplassen.no)

notes: There is no JSON search API. search-jobs and get-job parse server-rendered HTML.
The job ad id is the UUID at the end of each search result's url (/stillinger/stilling/<uuid>). Pass it to get-job.
Pages hold 25 results. Use --from 25, 50, ... for later pages. A larger page size (100) exists in the UI but no URL parameter for it was tested.
Filter values are Norwegian and case-sensitive (county=OSLO, extent=Heltid, sector=Offentlig). Only one value per filter was tested, although the UI allows combining counties.
Some filters exist only in the UI, with no known URL parameter: sub-level job category, education, driving licence, work language, summer job, Superrask søknad and employment type.
Saving favourite ads and saved searches needs a logged-in NAV session. They were not recorded, so no command covers them.
The search-result card selector ('article') is inferred from the related-ad cards on the detail page. If it returns nothing, use the raw HTML.
about: arbeidsplassen.nav.no is NAV's Norwegian public job board.

name: arbeitnow
description: Arbeitnow: a job board for jobs in Germany (remote, visa sponsorship, English speaking). This CLI searches and filters jobs, lists a company's jobs, reads the free public job-feed API, opens job details and lists hiring companies.

commands.name: search-jobs
commands.summary: Search jobs by keyword, with optional tag, location/category, date-posted filter, sort order and page. Returns paging info plus the result list as rendered HTML; each <li data-slug> holds a job slug a

params.name: search
params.description: Keyword query, e.g. 'python developer'. Empty means all jobs.

params.name: tags
params.description: JSON array of tag slugs, e.g. ["remote"]. Use [] for no tag filter.

params.name: category
params.description: Location/category slug, the same as /jobs/locations/{slug}. Examples: 'remote', 'berlin', 'munich'. Empty means any.

params.name: sort_by
params.description: Sort order. 'null' is the site default; 'relevance' sorts by relevance; 'newest' puts the most recent first.

params.name: date_posted
params.description: Posting-date window. Observed values: 'all' and '7d'. The UI likely also offers '24h' and '3d'.

commands.name: list-company-jobs
commands.summary: List the open jobs of one company. Needs both the display name and the slug. Returns paging info plus the result list as rendered HTML; each <li data-slug> holds a job slug for get-job.

params.name: company_name
params.description: Company display name exactly as shown on the site, e.g. 'Duck Duck Go'.

commands.name: list-jobs-feed
commands.summary: Free public job-board API feed: newest jobs as clean JSON (slug, company, title, description, remote flag, tags, job types, location, created_at), paginated.

params.name: visa_sponsorship
params.description: Documented on /blog/job-board-api but not exercised: true returns only jobs that offer visa sponsorship.

commands.name: get-job
commands.summary: Get full details of one job posting: title, HTML description, salary, employment type, remote/location, dates and hiring company.

params.name: job_slug
params.description: Job slug ending in the numeric job id, e.g. 'remote-director-data-science-440507'. It is the 'slug' field from list-jobs-feed or the data-slug in search results.

commands.name: list-companies
commands.summary: List the companies hiring on Arbeitnow with their open-job count. The company slug is the last segment of url; use it with list-company-jobs.

notes: search-jobs and list-company-jobs return JSON whose 'data' field is a rendered HTML fragment of <li data-slug=...> items. Each item's data-link is the job URL /jobs/companies/{company_slug}/{job_slug}. Pass those two parts to get-job.
For clean structured JSON without keyword filtering, use list-jobs-feed (the public, keyless /api/job-board-api). Its 'slug' field is the job_slug for get-job; the company slug is in the 'url' field.
tags must be a JSON array string, e.g. ["remote"]. category takes a location slug from /jobs/locations/{slug}, e.g. 'remote'.
/visa-sponsorship-jobs and /remote-jobs redirect: visa sponsorship goes to the home page, remote goes to /jobs/locations/remote. Use category=remote or the feed's visa_sponsorship parameter instead.
No login needed. Every command is read-only; analytics events on stats.arbeitnow.com are skipped.
about: Arbeitnow: a job board for jobs in Germany (remote, visa sponsorship, English speaking).

name: arbetsformedlingen
description: Platsbanken (Arbetsförmedlingen, the Swedish Public Employment Service job board): search job ads by keyword and municipality, read full ad details, list popular occupations, look up location and occupation taxonomy IDs, and get search suggestions.

commands.name: search-jobs
commands.summary: Free-text search of Platsbanken job ads (title, employer, occupation, workplace, dates), sorted by relevance or date

params.name: q
params.description: Free-text query: occupation, skill, employer or place, e.g. 'systemutvecklare stockholm'

params.name: order
params.description: Sort order: relevance, or date (newest first)

params.name: source
params.description: Ad source: pb = ads published in Platsbanken, joblinks = ads collected from external job sites

params.name: startIndex
params.description: Zero-based offset of the first ad to return. The API caps offsets at 2000 (offsetLimit).

commands.name: search-jobs-in-municipality
commands.summary: Free-text job search limited to one Swedish municipality (municipality ID from get-taxonomy-tree --type LOCATION)

params.name: municipality
params.description: Municipality taxonomy ID, e.g. AvNB_uwa_6n6 = Stockholm. Look IDs up with get-taxonomy-tree --type LOCATION.

params.name: order
params.description: Sort order: relevance, or date (newest first)

params.name: source
params.description: Ad source: pb = Platsbanken ads, joblinks = ads from external sites

params.name: startIndex
params.description: Zero-based offset of the first ad to return (maximum 2000)

commands.name: get-job
commands.summary: Full details of one job ad: HTML description, employer, workplace address, employment type, working hours, salary type, how to apply

params.name: id
params.description: Job ad ID (the id field from search-jobs), e.g. 31590660

commands.name: suggest-search-terms
commands.summary: Typeahead suggestions (completions) for a partial job-search query

params.name: q
params.description: Partial search text (word prefix), e.g. 'sjuksk' or 'utveckl'

commands.name: list-popular-occupations
commands.summary: Occupations with the most open job ads right now, with ad counts

params.name: api_limit
params.description: Maximum number of occupations to return (sent to the site as "limit"; clify's own --limit only shapes the output)

commands.name: get-taxonomy-tree
commands.summary: Taxonomy tree with IDs used for search filters: LOCATION = regions (län) and their municipalities, OCCUPATION = occupation fields and groups

notes: Every command calls the public Platsbanken API at platsbanken-api.arbetsformedlingen.se. No login is needed.
Search returns numberOfAds (total matches) and offsetLimit (2000) next to the ads array. Results cannot be paged past startIndex 2000, so narrow the query to see more.
Find municipality IDs (type 'municipality', e.g. Stockholm = AvNB_uwa_6n6) in get-taxonomy-tree --type LOCATION. The web UI writes them in its URL as l=3:<id>.

Other filter IDs seen in the UI: employmentType kpPX_CNN_gDU = permanent (tillsvidare), workExtent 6YE1_gAC_R2G = full-time (heltid), workplaceModel Vbpe_rGe_vCW = hybrid. The UI sends these as extra {type, value} entries in the search filters array, and a 'published last N days' filter as fromDate. The commands here do not expose them.
The human-readable ad page is https://arbetsformedlingen.se/platsbanken/annonser/<id>.
Ad descriptions from get-job are HTML strings.
Typeahead suggestions returned an empty list for the recorded queries, so the result may be empty for full words.
about: Platsbanken (Arbetsförmedlingen, the Swedish Public Employment Service job board): search job ads by keyword and municipality, read full ad details, list…

name: archive
description: Internet Archive (archive.org): a digital library of texts, audio, video, software and web snapshots. This CLI searches items, including full-text search inside books, browses collections and user uploads, reads item metadata, file lists, reviews and OCR text, downloads files, and queries Wayback Machine snapshots.

commands.name: search-items
commands.summary: Keyword search across archive.org items, as the archive.org/search UI does it, with facet filters, sort and paging; set service_backend=fts to search inside book text

params.name: query
params.description: Search terms. Lucene-style field queries are allowed, e.g. 'grateful dead' or 'title:(moby dick)'

params.name: filter_map
params.description: JSON facet filter. Map each field to {value: op}, where op is inc, exc, gte or lte. Example: {"mediatype":{"texts":"inc"},"year":{"1900":"gte","1950":"lte"},"language":{"English":"inc"}}

params.name: sort
params.description: Sort order as field:direction. Omit for relevance.

params.name: service_backend
params.description: Search backend: 'metadata' (the default when omitted) or 'fts' for full-text search inside documents

params.name: hits_per_page
params.description: Results per page (the UI uses 50 or 100)

commands.name: list-collection-items
commands.summary: List the items in a collection (e.g. GratefulDead, texts, audio), with sort, facet filters and paging

params.name: collection
params.description: Collection identifier, e.g. GratefulDead, etree, texts, librivoxaudio

params.name: query
params.description: Optional search terms to search within the collection

commands.name: list-user-uploads
commands.summary: List the public uploads of an archive.org user account

params.name: user
params.description: Account screen name prefixed with @, e.g. @matthew_vernon

commands.name: advanced-search
commands.summary: Solr-style advanced search (advancedsearch.php) returning identifier, title, creator, mediatype, date and downloads, with sort and paging

params.name: q
params.description: Lucene query, e.g. 'grateful dead AND mediatype:audio' or 'collection:GratefulDead AND year:1977'

params.name: sort
params.description: Sort as 'field asc|desc', e.g. 'downloads desc', 'date asc', 'publicdate desc'

commands.name: scrape-items
commands.summary: Bulk-list every item matching a query with the cursor-based scrape API; suited to enumerating large collections

params.name: api_fields
params.description: Comma-separated metadata fields to return (sent to the site as "fields"; clify's own --fields only shapes the output)

params.name: cursor
params.description: Cursor from the previous response, used to fetch the next batch

commands.name: get-item-metadata
commands.summary: Get an item's descriptive metadata (title, creator, date, collection, description and more) by identifier

commands.name: list-item-files
commands.summary: List the files in an item, with name, format, size and checksums; pass a name to download-file

commands.name: get-item-reviews
commands.summary: Get the user reviews (title, body, reviewer, stars, date) posted on an item

commands.name: get-item-fulltext
commands.summary: Get the full OCR plain text of a text item (book or document)

commands.name: download-file
commands.summary: Download one file from an item (text files are returned as text)

params.name: file
params.description: File name as listed by list-item-files

commands.name: get-collection-views
commands.summary: Get view statistics for a collection over the last N days, broken down by country and region

params.name: days
params.description: Number of days to look back

commands.name: list-user-lists
commands.summary: Get a user's public item lists and the items each one contains

params.name: username
params.description: Account screen name without the leading @

commands.name: list-top-collections
commands.summary: List the top collections featured on the archive.org home page, with item counts

commands.name: get-media-counts
commands.summary: Get total item counts per media type (texts, movies, audio, software, image, etree, tv, web)

commands.name: wayback-available
commands.summary: Find the Wayback Machine snapshot of a URL closest to a given timestamp

params.name: url
params.description: URL or domain to look up, e.g. example.com

params.name: timestamp
params.description: Target time as YYYYMMDDhhmmss (a prefix is fine, e.g. 20100101). Omit to get the latest snapshot.

commands.name: list-wayback-snapshots
commands.summary: List Wayback Machine captures of a URL from the CDX index, optionally limited to a date range

params.name: url
params.description: URL to list captures for, e.g. example.com

params.name: from
params.description: Start of the range as a YYYYMMDDhhmmss prefix, e.g. 2010

params.name: to
params.description: End of the range as a YYYYMMDDhhmmss prefix, e.g. 2012

params.name: collapse
params.description: Collapse adjacent duplicate captures on a field, e.g. digest or timestamp:8 (one per day)

params.name: api_limit
params.description: Maximum number of rows (sent to the site as "limit"; clify's own --limit only shapes the output)

notes: Items are identified by their identifier, the part after /details/ in an item URL. The search commands return it as fields.identifier (page_production) or identifier (advancedsearch/scrape).
search-items with service_backend=fts searches inside the OCR text of books. Results carry highlight snippets. The UI equivalent is /search?sin=TXT.
filter_map takes a JSON string. Operators are inc and exc for facet values, and gte and lte for year ranges. Example: {"mediatype":{"texts":"inc"},"year":{"1900":"gte","1950":"lte"}}.
Facet-count aggregations are not available (aggregations=true returned UNSUPPORTED_AGGREGATION), so aggregations is fixed to false.
Top-level media categories such as texts, audio, movies, software and image can be browsed as collections with list-collection-items.
For bulk enumeration, use scrape-items and follow its cursor. advanced-search is limited in how deep it can page.
advancedsearch.php also supports output=rss (RSS export). This CLI always requests JSON.

list-wayback-snapshots returns an array of arrays: the first row is the header (urlkey, timestamp, original, mimetype, statuscode, digest, length). Replay a capture at https://web.archive.org/web/{timestamp}/{original}.
Writes (favorites, reviews, uploads) need an account and were not recorded, so they are not included.
about: Internet Archive (archive.org): a digital library of texts, audio, video, software and web snapshots.

name: arstechnica
description: Ars Technica (WordPress news site plus XenForo 'Civis' forum). The CLI reads article feeds by site, section, tag and author, fetches full articles, and reads forum threads and article comment threads.

commands.name: list-latest-articles
commands.summary: List the newest articles across the whole site from the sitewide RSS feed (title, link, date, author, excerpt).

commands.name: list-section-articles
commands.summary: List the newest articles in a site section (e.g. gadgets, security, science) from the section RSS feed.

params.name: section
params.description: Section slug as it appears in article URLs, e.g. gadgets, security, science, ai, tech-policy, space, cars, gaming, culture, health, reviews

commands.name: list-tag-articles
commands.summary: List articles with a given tag from the tag RSS feed. Items include the full article content.

params.name: tag
params.description: Tag slug, lowercase and hyphenated, e.g. quantum-computing, cryptography, laptops

commands.name: list-author-articles
commands.summary: List the newest articles by one Ars Technica author from the author RSS feed.

params.name: author
params.description: Author slug from /author/{slug}/ URLs, e.g. dan-goodin

commands.name: get-article
commands.summary: Fetch one article: title, description, author, publish date, body text and the link to its forum comment thread.

params.name: section
params.description: Section slug from the article URL, e.g. security, reviews, gadgets

params.name: month
params.description: 2-digit month from the article URL, e.g. 09

commands.name: get-thread-posts
commands.summary: Read the posts in a forum thread, including an article's comment thread, one page at a time. Can sort by vote score.

params.name: thread
params.description: Thread slug plus numeric id, in the form slug.id. Taken from /civis/threads/{slug}.{id}/ URLs, e.g. the article's commentsUrl.

params.name: order
params.description: Post order. Omit for chronological; vote_score sorts by votes.

commands.name: list-forum-threads
commands.summary: List threads in a forum, e.g. News Discussion (article comment threads): title, url, author, latest activity.

params.name: forum
params.description: Forum slug plus numeric id, in the form slug.id, e.g. news-discussion.2

commands.name: list-new-forum-posts
commands.summary: List forum threads with the most recent new posts, from Civis 'What's new > New posts'.

notes: Keyword search is not available as a replayable request. /search/ and /?s= are rendered client-side by an embedded Google Custom Search, and no first-party search endpoint exists. To find articles, use the tag, section and author feeds.
Feed commands return RSS converted to JSON. Article URLs are in 'link'. Tag feeds include full article HTML in 'content:encoded'.
To read an article's comments, take commentsUrl from get-article. The /civis/threads/{slug}.{id}/ part is the 'thread' argument of get-thread-posts.
The WordPress JSON API (/wp-json/wp/v2/posts) returns 403. robots.txt disallows forum search and member profiles.
All commands are anonymous, read-only page or feed fetches. The site is behind AWS WAF, so heavy request rates may trigger challenges.

The section, author and new-posts commands were inferred from the page list rather than recorded directly. If they fail, fall back to the recorded HTML listings: /gadgets/, /gadgets/page/2/, /author/dan-goodin/ and /civis/whats-new/posts/.
about: Ars Technica (WordPress news site plus XenForo 'Civis' forum).

name: artic
description: Art Institute of Chicago collection. The CLI queries the museum's official public JSON API (api.artic.edu) for artworks, artists, exhibitions, events, articles, category terms and IIIF manifests, and adds the website's related-artworks lookup.

commands.name: search-artworks
commands.summary: Full-text search of the collection's artworks, with optional filters (public domain, on view, department, artist id), sort by date and pagination

params.name: public_domain
params.description: Only public-domain artworks (images free to reuse)

params.name: on_view
params.description: Only artworks currently on view in the galleries

params.name: department
params.description: Exact department title, e.g. 'Painting and Sculpture of Europe', 'Arts of the Americas', 'Prints and Drawings'

params.name: artist_id
params.description: Restrict to one artist. Use the numeric id from search-artists.

params.name: sort_date
params.description: Sort by start date instead of relevance

params.name: api_fields
params.description: Comma-separated fields to return (sent to the site as "fields"; clify's own --fields only shapes the output)

params.name: api_limit
params.description: Results per page (max 100) (sent to the site as "limit"; clify's own --limit only shapes the output)

commands.name: facet-artworks
commands.summary: Get facet counts (aggregation buckets) over the whole artwork collection for a keyword field such as department, classification or artist

params.name: field

commands.name: get-artwork
commands.summary: Get full details of one artwork by numeric id (title, artist, date, medium, dimensions, credit line, gallery, description, image id)

params.name: api_fields
params.description: Optional comma-separated subset of fields to return (default: all) (sent to the site as "fields"; clify's own --fields only shapes the output)

commands.name: get-artworks
commands.summary: Fetch several artworks at once by a comma-separated list of ids

params.name: api_fields
params.description: Comma-separated fields to return (sent to the site as "fields"; clify's own --fields only shapes the output)

commands.name: get-artwork-manifest
commands.summary: Get the IIIF Presentation manifest for an artwork (image service URLs, label, metadata)

commands.name: search-artists
commands.summary: Search artists by name. The returned id works with get-artist and the artist_id filter of search-artworks.

params.name: api_fields
params.description: Comma-separated fields to return (sent to the site as "fields"; clify's own --fields only shapes the output)

params.name: api_limit
params.description: Results per page (max 100) (sent to the site as "limit"; clify's own --limit only shapes the output)

commands.name: get-artist
commands.summary: Get details of one artist by id (name, alternate names, birth and death dates, biography)

commands.name: search-exhibitions
commands.summary: Search museum exhibitions (current and past) by keyword

params.name: api_fields
params.description: Comma-separated fields to return (sent to the site as "fields"; clify's own --fields only shapes the output)

params.name: api_limit
params.description: Results per page (sent to the site as "limit"; clify's own --limit only shapes the output)

commands.name: get-exhibition
commands.summary: Get details of one exhibition by id (dates, gallery, description, artworks shown)

commands.name: search-events
commands.summary: Search museum events (tours, talks, programs) by keyword

params.name: api_fields
params.description: Comma-separated fields to return (sent to the site as "fields"; clify's own --fields only shapes the output)

params.name: api_limit
params.description: Results per page (sent to the site as "limit"; clify's own --limit only shapes the output)

commands.name: search-articles
commands.summary: Search the museum's editorial articles by keyword

params.name: api_fields
params.description: Comma-separated fields to return (sent to the site as "fields"; clify's own --fields only shapes the output)

params.name: api_limit
params.description: Results per page (sent to the site as "limit"; clify's own --limit only shapes the output)

commands.name: search-category-terms
commands.summary: Search category terms (styles, subjects, themes, classifications, materials, techniques, departments)

params.name: subtype
params.description: Restrict to one kind of term

params.name: api_fields
params.description: Comma-separated fields to return (sent to the site as "fields"; clify's own --fields only shapes the output)

params.name: api_limit
params.description: Results per page (sent to the site as "limit"; clify's own --limit only shapes the output)

notes: The www.artic.edu collection search page is behind a bot check, so these commands use the official public API at api.artic.edu (CC0 data, docs at https://api.artic.edu/docs/). It needs no auth and accepts at most 100 results per page.
Build image URLs from image_id: https://www.artic.edu/iiif/2/{image_id}/full/843,/0/default.jpg. Smaller widths such as 400, also work.
search-artworks filters use Elasticsearch bool/must terms. They combine with AND, and you can pass any subset. department must match the exact title, which you can get from facet-artworks.
Artwork, artist and exhibition ids are numeric. Website URLs follow https://www.artic.edu/artworks/{id}/{slug}; the slug is optional.
get-related-artworks returns an HTML fragment string. Artwork links inside it look like /artworks/{id}/{slug}; pass those ids to get-artwork.
For heavy use the museum asks clients to send an AIC-User-Agent header containing a contact email.
about: Art Institute of Chicago collection.

name: artifacthub
description: Artifact Hub (artifacthub.io) is the CNCF hub for cloud-native packages such as Helm charts, operators, kubectl/krew plugins and policies. This CLI searches packages and reads package details, versions, default values, templates, changelogs, security reports, views, stars, RSS feeds and site statistics through the public /api/v1 API.

commands.name: search-packages
commands.summary: Search Artifact Hub packages by keyword, with filters for kind, category, publisher, repo, org and license, plus sorting and offset paging.

params.name: query
params.description: Full-text search terms, e.g. 'nginx'. Words separated by ' or ' run an OR search, which the site uses for related packages.

params.name: kind
params.description: Package kind id: 0=Helm chart, 1=Falco rules, 2=OPA policies, 3=OLM operator, 4=Tinkerbell action, 5=kubectl/krew plugin, 6=Helm plugin, 7=Tekton task, 8=KEDA scaler, 9=CoreDNS plugin, 10=Keptn integr

params.name: category
params.description: Category id: 1=AI/Machine learning, 2=Database, 3=Integration and delivery, 4=Monitoring and logging, 5=Networking, 6=Security, 7=Storage, 8=Streaming and messaging

params.name: license
params.description: SPDX license id, e.g. Apache-2.0, MIT

params.name: repo
params.description: Repository name to restrict to, e.g. bitnami

params.name: facets
params.description: Also return facet counts (kinds, categories, orgs, repos, licenses)

params.name: api_limit
params.description: Results per page (max 60) (sent to the site as "limit"; clify's own --limit only shapes the output)

commands.name: get-package
commands.summary: Get full details of a package's latest version: readme, available versions, repository, keywords, links and data.

params.name: kind
params.description: Package kind slug as used in URLs

commands.name: get-package-version
commands.summary: Get details of a specific version of a package.

params.name: kind
params.description: Package kind slug, e.g. helm, krew, olm

commands.name: get-package-values
commands.summary: Get the default values.yaml of a Helm chart version as raw YAML text.

commands.name: get-package-templates
commands.summary: Get the template files of a Helm chart version. Each file's data field is base64-encoded.

commands.name: get-package-changelog
commands.summary: Get a package's changelog: changes per version, with timestamps and security-update flags.

commands.name: get-security-report
commands.summary: Get the Trivy vulnerability scan report for each container image of a package version.

commands.name: get-package-views
commands.summary: Get daily view counts for a package over roughly the last 30 days, grouped by version.

commands.name: get-package-stars
commands.summary: Get the number of stars a package has.

commands.name: get-package-feed
commands.summary: Get a package's release feed (RSS): versions with links and publish dates.

params.name: kind
params.description: Package kind slug, e.g. helm, krew

commands.name: random-packages
commands.summary: Get a random selection of packages, as shown on the home page.

commands.name: get-package-totals
commands.summary: Get the total number of packages and releases on Artifact Hub.

commands.name: get-site-stats
commands.summary: Get site-wide statistics: package, release, repository and organization totals and their growth over time.

commands.name: get-openapi-spec
commands.summary: Get Artifact Hub's public OpenAPI 3 specification (YAML text) describing the full /api/v1 API.

notes: All commands are public reads; no login is needed.
Commands that take package_id need the UUID from search-packages or get-package. get-package and get-package-feed take kind/repo/name instead.

repository.kind in search results is numeric. Map it to the URL kind slug: 0=helm, 1=falco, 2=opa, 3=olm, 4=tbaction, 5=krew, 6=helm-plugin, 7=tekton-task, 8=keda-scaler, 9=coredns, 10=keptn, 11=tekton-pipeline, 12=container, 13=kubewarden, 14=gatekeeper, 15=kyverno, 16=knative-client-plugin, 17=backstage, 18=argo-template, 19=kubearmor, 20=kcl, 21=headlamp.
For related packages, run search-packages with an OR query, e.g. 'ingress or nginx'.
Template data is base64-encoded. Values are returned as raw YAML text.
The POST /api/v1/packages/{id}/{version}/views calls are view-tracking telemetry that needs a CSRF token, so they are not exposed. Starring a package needs login, and that request was not captured.
about: Artifact Hub (artifacthub.io) is the CNCF hub for cloud-native packages such as Helm charts, operators, kubectl/krew plugins and policies.

name: arxiv
description: arXiv.org, the open-access preprint archive. This CLI browses category listings (new, recent, monthly), daily catch-up, archive overviews, yearly stats, the category taxonomy and RSS feeds, and fetches paper abstract pages and BibTeX citations.

commands.name: list-recent
commands.summary: List papers from the last 5 announcement days in an arXiv category or archive (e.g. cs.LG, math.NT, cs), paged. Results alternate: an {id,url} item, then that paper's {title,authors,subjects,comments}

params.name: category
params.description: Category or archive id, e.g. cs.LG, math.NT, astro-ph, cs

commands.name: list-new
commands.summary: List the latest announcement (new submissions, cross-lists, replacements) in a category, with abstracts. Results alternate: an {id,url} item, then that paper's {title,authors,subjects,abstract} item.

params.name: category
params.description: Category or archive id, e.g. cs.LG, math.NT, cs

commands.name: list-month
commands.summary: List all papers in a category or archive for a given month (YYYY-MM) or year (YYYY), paged. Results alternate: an {id,url} item, then that paper's {title,authors,subjects,comments} item.

params.name: category
params.description: Category or archive id, e.g. cs.LG, cs, math

params.name: month
params.description: Month as YYYY-MM (e.g. 2026-10), or a year as YYYY

commands.name: catchup
commands.summary: Show everything announced in an archive on a given day (new, cross-lists, replacements). Use for catching up since a date. Results alternate: an {id,url} item, then that paper's {title,authors,subject

params.name: archive
params.description: Archive id, e.g. cs, math, astro-ph

params.name: date
params.description: Day as YYYY-MM-DD. Must be a recent date.

params.name: page
params.description: Page counter the site adds when following 'Continue to the next day' links

commands.name: get-paper
commands.summary: Get a paper's abstract page: title, authors, abstract, comments, subjects, submission history and PDF/HTML links

params.name: id
params.description: arXiv id, optionally with a version suffix, e.g. 2610.21832 or 2610.22339v1

commands.name: get-bibtex
commands.summary: Export the BibTeX citation for a paper

commands.name: get-rss-feed
commands.summary: Get the raw RSS 2.0 XML feed of the latest announcement in a category: items with title, link, description, dc:creator, category and arxiv:announce_type. Empty on weekends and holidays.

params.name: category
params.description: Category or archive id; join several with '+', e.g. cs.LG or cs.LG+stat.ML

commands.name: get-archive
commands.summary: Get an archive overview (e.g. cs, math, physics): its subject categories with descriptions and browse links

params.name: archive
params.description: Archive id, e.g. cs, math, astro-ph, cond-mat, q-bio, stat, eess, econ

commands.name: get-year-stats
commands.summary: Get monthly article counts for an archive in a given year

commands.name: list-categories
commands.summary: List the full arXiv category taxonomy (category ids, names and descriptions across all groups)

notes: In list-recent, list-new, list-month and catchup, entries come back as alternating items. The first item of each pair has id and url (from the <dt>). The second has title, authors, subjects, comments and abstract (from the <dd>). Pair consecutive items to build one paper.
The listing 'id' field reads like 'arXiv:2610.22358'. Strip the 'arXiv:' prefix before passing it to get-paper or get-bibtex.
Full text is at https://arxiv.org/pdf/{id}, LaTeX source at https://arxiv.org/src/{id}, and HTML at https://arxiv.org/html/{id}v{n}. These are binary or large documents, so they are not commands.

Keyword and author search (/search/*) and the export API (/api/query) are disallowed by arXiv's robots.txt, so this CLI has no search command. Author links in results point to /search and should not be fetched.
Listings are updated once per weekday announcement. The RSS feed (get-rss-feed) is empty on weekends and holidays; use list-new or list-recent then.
The prev/next within a category link (/prevnext) timed out during exploration and is not included.
Text fields include arXiv's descriptor labels such as 'Title:', 'Authors:', 'Abstract:', 'Subjects:'. Strip them if needed.
Be polite: arXiv asks automated clients to limit request rates (about 1 request every 3 seconds).
about: arXiv.org, the open-access preprint archive.

name: aviationweather
description: AviationWeather.gov (NOAA Aviation Weather Center) public Data API. The CLI fetches METARs, TAFs, PIREPs, SIGMETs/AIRMETs, international SIGMETs, winds aloft, and airport/station info. No login is needed.

commands.name: get-metars

params.name: bbox
params.description: Bounding box as minLat,minLon,maxLat,maxLon, e.g. 39,-106,41,-104. Use it instead of ids.

params.name: hours
params.description: Hours of observations to return. 0 or omitted returns only the most recent report.

commands.name: get-tafs
commands.summary: Get TAF terminal forecasts for ICAO station ids, optionally with the latest METAR

params.name: ids
params.description: Comma-separated ICAO station ids, e.g. KSEA,KLAX

params.name: metar
params.description: Also include the latest METAR for each station

commands.name: get-airport
commands.summary: Get airport details: name, location, elevation, runways and frequencies

params.name: ids
params.description: Comma-separated airport ICAO ids, e.g. KDEN

commands.name: get-station-info
commands.summary: Get weather station metadata: ICAO/IATA/WMO ids, site name, location, and product types (METAR/TAF)

params.name: ids
params.description: Comma-separated station ICAO ids, e.g. KSEA

commands.name: search-pireps
commands.summary: Search pilot reports (PIREPs/AIREPs) near a station by distance and age, or inside a bounding box, optionally filtered by intensity

params.name: id
params.description: Center station ICAO id, e.g. KDEN. Use with distance.

params.name: distance

Winds aloft come back as raw FD text. Each column is DDSS+TT (direction, speed in knots, temperature in °C); temperatures above 24000 ft are negative.

commands.summary: Find football teams and competitions by name. Returns BBC URNs and scores-fixtures URLs (the team slug is in the URL).

commands.summary: Get structured JSON content for a BBC page path (e.g. a /reel/video/{id}/watch video): title, summary, publish times, metadata.

notes: There is no keyword/full-text search. BBC's robots.txt disallows /search, so find content through section, region and topic listings, list-live-pages, or search-football-teams.

Listing commands return relative hrefs such as /news/articles/{id}, /news/videos/{id} and /news/live/{id}. The last path segment is the id that get-article, get-video and get-live-blog take. The same story can appear more than once on a listing page.
get-article returns schema.org metadata only (headline, description, author, dates, image), not the full body text. The body is in the page's script#__NEXT_DATA__.

name: bundlephobia
description: Bundlephobia shows the bundle-size cost of npm packages. This CLI searches packages and looks up minified/gzipped size, dependency composition, version history, similar packages, exports, recent searches and download/star trends. It can also fetch a GitHub repo's package.json to scan its dependencies.

commands.name: search-packages
commands.summary: Autocomplete/search npm package names (npms.io suggestions used by the Bundlephobia search box)

params.name: q
params.description: Search text or package-name prefix; scopes allowed, e.g. '@grida'

commands.name: get-package-size
commands.summary: Get minified and gzipped bundle size, dependency count and module flags for an npm package (optionally a specific version)

params.name: package
params.description: Package name, optionally with a version: 'react', 'react@19.3.1', '@mui/material'

commands.name: get-package-history
commands.summary: List a package's recent versions with their bundle sizes and publish dates, plus major/minor release markers

params.name: api_limit
params.description: Maximum number of versions to return (sent to the site as "limit"; clify's own --limit only shapes the output)

commands.name: get-similar-packages
commands.summary: Find alternative or similar packages in the same category as a given package

commands.name: list-recent-searches
commands.summary: List packages recently searched on Bundlephobia by all users, keyed by package name

params.name: api_limit
params.description: Number of recent packages to return (sent to the site as "limit"; clify's own --limit only shapes the output)

commands.name: compare-trends
commands.summary: Compare download, star and size trends over time for several packages (the data behind the /trends page)

commands.name: get-github-package-json
commands.summary: Fetch the package.json of a GitHub repo (default branch) to list its dependencies for scanning with get-package-size

notes: The Bundlephobia API rate-limits aggressively (HTTP 429), especially trends, history, exports and similar-packages. Space out calls and retry with backoff; do not bulk-scan many packages quickly.
Package arguments accept 'name', 'name@version' and scoped names like '@scope/name'. Without a version, the latest version is used.
get-package-size records the lookup in the public 'recent searches' list (record=true), the same as the website does.
get-package-details reads __NEXT_DATA__ from the package page. On first load of a package not yet built, initialResult may be null; if so, call get-package-size instead.

The response shapes of get-package-exports and compare-trends were only partly captured because of rate limiting. The trends UI also offers metric=downloads|stars|size and groupBy=day|week|month, but those are client-side display options.
Scan workflow: run get-github-package-json, then call get-package-size for each dependency name.
Bundlephobia also exposes an MCP endpoint at https://bundlephobia.com/api/mcp.
about: Bundlephobia shows the bundle-size cost of npm packages.

name: caniuse

params.name: ids

commands.name: compare-browsers
commands.summary: Compare feature support between browser versions; returns the raw comparison result (IDs of features whose support differs between the given versions)

params.name: compare
params.description: Comma-separated list of '<browser> <version>' pairs, e.g. 'chrome 120,firefox 120,safari 17'. Browser keys: chrome, firefox, safari, edge, opera, ios_saf, ie, etc. Versions must exist in caniuse data

params.name: cats
params.description: Comma-separated feature categories to include (CSS, HTML5, JS, JS API, Other, Security, SVG)

commands.name: get-feature-page
commands.summary: Get a feature's detail page summary: title, spec link and status, description and global usage percentages (works for caniuse IDs, wf-* and mdn-* IDs)

commands.name: list-features-index
commands.summary: List all features in the caniuse index (titles and links, grouped by category in page order: CSS, HTML5, ...); the feature ID is the last path segment of href (e.g. 'css-rrggbbaa')

commands.name: list-news
commands.summary: List latest caniuse news / newly added features

commands.name: get-usage-table
commands.summary: Get the browser usage-share table: per browser, the versions with their global usage percentage

commands.name: list-feature-suggestions
commands.summary: List the top suggested features not yet on caniuse, ranked by GitHub votes

notes: Typical flow: search-features or compare-browsers returns feature IDs; pass them (comma-separated) to get-feature-support for full data, or to get-feature-page for global usage percentages.

Support stat codes in get-feature-support: y = supported, a = partial, n = not supported, p = polyfill available, u = unknown, x = needs a prefix, d = disabled by default; '#N' refers to note number N.
The stats object is large (every version of every browser). Request few IDs at a time.
list-feature-suggestions 'row' is the full row text, '<rank>. <title><votes>'. The trailing digits are the vote count. The first row is the table header.
In get-usage-table, versions_usage is the concatenated text '<version>:<pct>%' for each version of that browser.

The /ciu/filter page (category/baseline filters with group and sort) is rendered client-side and has no separate data endpoint, so it is not exposed. Use list-features-index plus get-feature-support (baseline_status) instead.
There is no pagination. Raw data is also published at github.com/Fyrd/caniuse. No login is needed.
about: caniuse.com: browser support tables for web platform features (HTML, CSS, JS APIs).

name: citybik
description: CityBikes (citybik.es) collects open bike-sharing data from around the world. This CLI queries the public CityBikes API (api.citybik.es/v2) for networks, network details and live station availability, and lists the projects showcased as built on CityBikes.

commands.name: list-networks
commands.summary: List all bike-sharing networks worldwide, with id, name, city, country, operating company and API href

params.name: api_fields
params.description: Comma-separated list of network fields to return, which keeps the response small. Available fields: id, name, location, href, company, gbfs_href, system, source (sent to the site as "fields"; clify's own --fields only shapes the output)

commands.name: get-network
commands.summary: Get details of one bike-sharing network by id (name, location, company, GBFS feed, system), without the station list

params.name: network_id
params.description: Network id (slug) as returned by list-networks, e.g. velib, bicing

params.description: Network id (slug) as returned by list-networks, e.g. bicing, velib

commands.summary: List the apps and projects that the CityBikes showcase page lists as built on CityBikes data

notes: All network data comes from the public, unauthenticated CityBikes API at https://api.citybik.es/v2. No login is needed.

list-networks returns every network (several hundred), and the API has no server-side search or pagination. Use --fields (e.g. id,name,location) to shrink the payload, then filter on location.city or location.country client-side to find a network id.

Station data is live. free_bikes is the number of bikes available to rent, and empty_slots is the number of free docks to return a bike. Some stations also carry an 'extra' object (e.g. ebikes, address), which you can request via --fields on the raw output.
The city search box on the homepage map did not load during exploration and sent no API calls, so it has no command. Use list-networks instead.
Analytics calls to stats.citybik.es were skipped.

params.description: Hex image id from the artwork's zoomify/DZI URL in get-artwork data

Filter keys seen: currently_on_view=1, recently_acquired=1, artist_tags (e.g. female), artists, type, culture, medium, credit, gallery, department, collection_mapped, orderby (date_sortable asc|desc). Facet values are the exact display strings shown on artwork pages, e.g. culture=United States, type=Painting.
Use the exact values from the detail page or from suggest-collection. suggest-collection with --filter artists returns artist names suitable for artists=.
info.total in the raw search response gives the total hit count. Page with --skip in steps of 100.
Artwork detail URLs are https://www.clevelandart.org/art/{accession_number}. A printable view is at /print/art/{accession_number}.
Only public, read-only collection data is covered. The ticketing, cart and tracking-pixel endpoints were skipped.
about: Cleveland Museum of Art online collection: search and filter artworks (keyword, artist, culture, type, medium, department, gallery, on view, recent…

name: clinicaltrials
description: ClinicalTrials.gov (NIH/NLM registry of over 600k clinical studies). The CLI searches studies, fetches full study records and their version history, autocompletes conditions, interventions, sponsors and facilities, and returns registry statistics and field metadata, all through the site's internal /api/int endpoints.

commands.name: search-studies
commands.summary: Search or list clinical studies by condition, keyword, intervention, sponsor, location or NCT IDs, with facet filters, sorting and offset paging. Returns compact study hits.

params.name: cond
params.description: Condition or disease search area, e.g. 'breast cancer'. Use suggest --dictionary Condition for canonical terms.

params.name: term
params.description: Other terms: free-text search over NCT ID, acronym, titles, keywords and more. Supports Essie expression syntax (AND/OR/NOT, AREA[Field]value).

params.name: intr
params.description: Intervention or treatment search area, e.g. 'tamoxifen'

params.name: spons
params.description: Sponsor or collaborator name search area

params.name: ids
params.description: Restrict to these NCT IDs, comma-separated, e.g. NCT00001372,NCT04368728

params.name: aggFilters
params.description: Facet filters as comma-separated 'facetId:key key' groups, e.g. 'status:rec not,sex:f'. Facet ids and keys come from the aggFilters block of count-studies (e.g. status keys: not=not yet recruiting, re

params.name: api_fields
params.description: Comma-separated field pieces to return (see get-field-metadata) (sent to the site as "fields"; clify's own --fields only shapes the output)

params.name: api_limit
params.description: Results per page (the UI uses up to 100) (sent to the site as "limit"; clify's own --limit only shapes the output)

commands.name: count-studies
commands.summary: Get the total number of matching studies and per-facet counts (status, sex, phase, study type, …) for a search, without listing studies.

commands.name: get-study
commands.summary: Get the full record of one study by NCT ID: protocol (description, eligibility, arms, outcomes, locations, contacts), results if posted, and derived data. Uses the public REST API v2.

params.name: api_fields
params.description: Comma-separated field pieces or section names to return, e.g. 'NCTId,BriefTitle,EligibilityCriteria' or 'ProtocolSection'. Leave empty for the full record. (Sent to the site as "fields".)

commands.name: suggest
commands.summary: Autocomplete or normalize a condition, intervention, lead sponsor or facility name before searching.

commands.name: get-field-metadata
commands.summary: Get the study data structure: every field with its piece name (used in fields/sort/AREA[] expressions), type, description and rules.

params.name: includeIndexedOnly
params.description: Include fields that are indexed only (searchable but not part of the record)

params.name: includeHistoricOnly
params.description: Include fields that exist only in historic versions of records

commands.name: list-search-areas
commands.summary: List the search areas (term, cond, intr, …), their query param names, and the weighted fields each one searches.

commands.name: get-stats
commands.summary: Get registry statistics: total studies, recruiting and registered counts by location and study type, registrations and results by year, and the last update date.

commands.name: get-api-spec
commands.summary: Get the OpenAPI 3 (YAML) spec of the public ClinicalTrials.gov REST API v2, the reference for query syntax, filters and field names.

notes: robots.txt disallows /search, /expert-search and /api/v2/*, so every command uses the internal /api/int endpoints the web app calls.

search-studies was only recorded with filter.ids (My Saved Studies page). The cond/term/intr/spons/locStr params are inferred from list-search-areas, whose 'param' value gives each area's query name. Check them with count-studies before relying on them.
aggFilters syntax is 'facetId:key1 key2,facetId2:key'. Get the valid facet ids and keys from the aggFilters array returned by count-studies.
Field and sort names are 'piece' names from get-field-metadata (e.g. BriefTitle, OverallStatus, LastUpdatePostDate).
Study IDs look like NCT########. get-study returns large records; the default fields omit resultsSection, so request it explicitly if needed.
Text fields contain HTML entities (e.g. /) and some descriptions are HTML.

Saving studies is stored only in browser localStorage, and the download dialog sent no recorded request, so neither is available as a command. Location autocomplete uses Google Places and is not exposed.
about: ClinicalTrials.gov (NIH/NLM registry of over 600k clinical studies).

name: cocoapods
description: CocoaPods.org is the public registry of Swift/Objective-C libraries (pods). This CLI searches pods by keyword through the site's Algolia index and reads pod detail pages, pod changelogs and owner profiles.

commands.name: search-pods
commands.summary: Search CocoaPods libraries by keyword. Returns name, version, summary, license, platforms, download counts and repo owner. Paginated, 20 per page.

params.name: query
params.description: Search keywords matched against pod name, summary, authors and repo owner. Prefix matching works, e.g. 'alamo' finds Alamofire.

params.name: page
params.description: Zero-based result page. The response field nbPages gives the total number of pages.

commands.name: get-pod
commands.summary: Get one pod's detail page: version, metadata table (tests, language, license, release, SPM), first maintainer, Podfile line, podspec/GitHub links and README text.

params.name: name
params.description: Exact pod name, case-sensitive as published, e.g. Alamofire (use the 'name' field from search-pods).

commands.name: get-pod-changelog
commands.summary: Get a pod's CHANGELOG as rendered text. Some pods only contain a link to their GitHub releases (see first_link).

params.name: name
params.description: Exact pod name, case-sensitive as published, e.g. Alamofire (use the 'name' field from search-pods).

commands.name: list-owner-pods
commands.summary: List all pods maintained by an owner (numeric owner id from get-pod's maintainer_url), with summary, license and language.

params.name: id
params.description: Numeric owner id, e.g. 2662 taken from /owners/2662.

notes: search-pods calls the site's public Algolia index using the read-only search key the web app embeds. Pages are zero-based; nbHits and nbPages in the raw response give the totals.
In search-pods, query is placed inside an Algolia 'params' string. Avoid '&' and '=' in queries; plain words and spaces work.
Pod names are case-sensitive in /pods/{name}. Use the exact 'name' value from search-pods.

get-pod's 'metadata' field is the sidebar table flattened to text (Tests, Language, License, Released, SPM support). 'maintainer' and 'maintainer_url' cover only the first maintainer; 'maintained_by' lists them all as text.
Owner ids appear only in maintainer links (/owners/{id}) on pod pages. Pass the number to list-owner-pods.
podspec_url links to the sharded podspec in the CocoaPods/Specs GitHub repo. Fetch it from GitHub if you need the raw spec.
The site shows a notice that CocoaPods trunk is moving to read-only, so new releases may be rare.
about: CocoaPods.org is the public registry of Swift/Objective-C libraries (pods).

name: collection-sciencemuseumgroup
description: Science Museum Group Collection (collection.sciencemuseumgroup.org.uk), the online catalogue of over 500,000 museum objects and archives. This CLI reads only the public homepage: featured collections, top-level collection categories, and 'on this day' anniversary highlights.

commands.name: list-featured-collections
commands.summary: List the featured collections shown in the homepage 'Explore' carousel (for example BBC Heritage Collection), with title, description and link

commands.name: list-collection-categories
commands.summary: List the top-level collection themes on the homepage (for example Medicine), with their description and subcategory text (for example Pharmacology, Surgery, Asian medicine)

commands.name: list-anniversaries
commands.summary: List the homepage 'anniversary' highlights: collection objects linked to events from N years ago today, with the anniversary text and a link to the object

notes: Only the homepage could be loaded. Every request for keyword search (/search?q=...), category listings (/search/categories/...), object pages (/objects/{id}) and archive documents (/documents/{id}), including their ?ajax=true variants, got a CloudFront 403 'Request blocked' from the site's bot/WAF protection.

No search or detail commands are provided for three reasons: the recorded responses were 403 errors, the site's robots.txt disallows /api/, /iiif/, /mcp and any URL with a query string, and working around the bot block would not be appropriate.
The homepage returns curated, rotating content. Carousel items and anniversary cards change over time.
The 'url' fields point to collection, category or object pages on the site. These are links for a human to open. Fetching them programmatically is expected to be blocked.
For programmatic access to collection data, contact the Science Museum Group about official data or API access instead of scraping.
about: Science Museum Group Collection (collection.sciencemuseumgroup.org.uk), the online catalogue of over 500,000 museum objects and archives.

name: collections-vam
description: V&A Explore the Collections: a JSON CLI over the Victoria and Albert Museum's public collections API. It can search and filter museum objects, fetch object records, IIIF manifests and image info, get facet counts, autocomplete makers, search archives, export results as CSV and browse organisation pages.

commands.name: search-objects
commands.summary: Search V&A collection objects by keyword. Filters: maker, object name, material, place, accession number, category, place/material/technique/person/organisation/collection IDs, has-image and on-displa

params.name: q
params.description: Free-text keyword searched across all fields

params.name: q_actor
params.description: Search only the Artist/maker field (person or organisation name)

params.name: q_object_name
params.description: Search only the title / object type field

params.name: q_material_technique

params.name: q_place_name

params.name: q_accession_number

params.name: images_exist

params.name: kw_location_type
params.description: Location type filter. 'display' = only objects currently on display

params.name: id_place
params.description: Place-of-origin facet ID, e.g. x29523 (Yorkshire), x28980 (London)

params.name: kw_object_type
params.description: Exact object type keyword, e.g. Teapot

commands.summary: Export object search results as CSV text. Takes the same main filters as search-objects.
