commands.name: get-image-info
commands.summary: Get IIIF image info (dimensions, tile sizes, supported formats) for an image asset ID such as _primaryImageId.

params.name: asset_ref
params.description: Image asset reference, e.g. 2007BP1152 (the _primaryImageId field from search results)

commands.name: get-facet-counts
commands.summary: Get facet counts (categories, people, places, materials, techniques, etc.) for an object search.

params.name: cluster_size
params.description: Number of terms returned per facet

commands.name: list-facet-values
commands.summary: List the values and counts of one facet type (e.g. place, material, category) for an object search. Use this to find facet IDs for search-objects.

params.name: q
params.description: Free-text keyword to scope the counts

commands.name: autocomplete-names
commands.summary: Search-as-you-type suggestions for people and organisations (makers), returning their IDs for use in id_person / id_organisation filters.

commands.name: search-archives
commands.summary: Search the V&A archives index (archive collections and records) by keyword.

commands.name: list-suggested-facets
commands.summary: List the site's built-in suggested facets (popular places, etc.) with their system-number IDs.

commands.name: list-organisations

commands.name: get-organisation-objects
commands.summary: Open an organisation profile page and list its featured collection objects.

params.name: org_id

params.name: slug

notes: The API is public and needs no authentication. All JSON endpoints are on api.vam.ac.uk/v2.
Object system numbers look like O151155. get-object and get-object-manifest take only the numeric part (151155). Human-readable page: https://collections.vam.ac.uk/item/O{num}/.
Image URLs follow IIIF: https://framemark.vam.ac.uk/collections/{_primaryImageId}/full/!800,800/0/default.jpg. Images are licensed for non-commercial use only.
To find facet IDs (id_place, id_material, id_category, ...), use list-facet-values, get-facet-counts or list-suggested-facets. Use autocomplete-names for maker IDs (id_person / id_organisation).
search-objects returns info.record_count and info.pages in the raw response. page_size is capped at 100.

Not captured: the 'you may also like' related items (objects/search?search_profile=ymal, the object-identifying parameter was not observed), browse/{cluster_type}/{term}, v1 endpoints and the 'Order this Object' action. The full spec is at https://api.vam.ac.uk/openapi.json.
about: V&A Explore the Collections: a JSON CLI over the Victoria and Albert Museum's public collections API.

commands.name: list-filing-history

commands.summary: Advanced company search. Filter by name include/exclude, registered office address, incorporation and dissolution date ranges, status, SIC code and company type. Returns company names and profile URLs

notes: All pages are server-rendered HTML. No sign-in is needed for any command.
Company numbers are 8 characters with leading zeros or a prefix (00445790, SC123456, NI012345). Get them from the /company/{number} URL in search results.

Officer ids come from /officers/{id}/appointments links in search-officers, search-all or list-company-officers. Disqualified officer ids come from /disqualified-officers/{natural|corporate}/{id} links.
Filing document links look like /company/{n}/filing-history/{transactionId}/document?format=pdf. get-filing-document redirects to a short-lived signed S3 URL that returns the PDF.

The advanced search status, sicCodes and type filters accept multiple values on the website. This CLI sends one value each.
The public REST API (api.company-information.service.gov.uk, documented at developer.companieshouse.gov.uk) needs an API key and is not covered here.

commands.summary: List a project's public deliverables, data management plans and publications, with download links (from the project's Results tab)

params.name: project_id

commands.summary: Get a result/report record as JSON (periodic report summary, work performed, final results, related project), looked up by its RCN

commands.summary: Get a CORDIS article (news, Results in Brief, Ask an expert…) as JSON, including body, keywords and related projects/articles

params.name: id
params.description: Article id with slug as it appears in article URLs, e.g. 467900-can-birds-understand-the-songs-of-other-species

commands.summary: List the latest CORDIS news articles shown on the news hub, by section (Scientific advances, Ask an expert…)

params.name: domain
params.description: Domain slug, e.g. energy, digital-economy, climate-change-and-environment (the lowercase, hyphenated domain name)

commands.name: search-projects-map
commands.summary: Keyword search over EU-funded projects and participating organisations (Projects Map data): returns hit counts plus organisations with address, coordinates and their projects (budget, dates, scheme);

bodyTemplate.query: {query}

commands.name: get-data-extraction-api-spec
commands.summary: Get the OpenAPI spec of the CORDIS Data Extraction Tool API (bulk extractions; using the API needs a personal API key)

notes: robots.txt disallows /search and /programme/id/*, so the site's main keyword search, its filters, sort orders, pagination and framework-programme pages are not exposed. Use search-projects-map for keyword search instead.

search-projects-map returns two fields, 'number' and 'content'. Both are JSON-encoded strings, so parse them a second time. 'number' holds totals and budget/date ranges. 'content' maps organisation IDs to {name, country, city, lat, lon, projects{projectId: {...}}}.
The web app also sent search-projects-map queries such as 'hydrogen&&&2' and 'hydrogen&&&3' to get further result chunks or views. To try these, append '&&&N' to --query.

IDs: projects use the grant agreement ID (e.g. 101070320). Result reports use an RCN (e.g. 1169591), found in a project's relations or on its reporting page. Articles use 'rcn-slug' ids (e.g. 467900-can-birds-understand-the-songs-of-other-species), found in list-news, list-domain-articles or a project's relations.
Project fact sheets can also be exported as XML (?format=xml) and fetched in other languages at /project/id/{id}/{lang} (de, en, es, fr, it, pl).
Bulk datasets of all Horizon Europe and H2020 projects (CSV/JSON/XML) are on data.europa.eu, not on CORDIS itself.
The Data Extraction Tool endpoints (/api/dataextractions/*) need a personal API key from a CORDIS account, so they are not wrapped here.
The SPARQL endpoint (EURIO Knowledge Graph) exists, but no query was recorded, so it is not wrapped.
Not wrapped because the recording did not give enough detail: per-project news (/project/id/{id}/news) and the thematic-packs listing.
get-project-widget is based only on the explorer's summary: its exact parameters and response were not recorded.

get-project and list-domain-articles were not fully verified against the recording. For get-project, only the HTML fact sheet's structure was recorded, so the JSON fields of the export are unknown. For list-domain-articles, the extract selectors come from a truncated page outline.
about: CORDIS (EU research results portal): look up EU-funded research projects and their reports, deliverables, OpenAIRE publications, Results-in-Brief and news…

notes: All commands are public reads and need no login. Write actions (publish, yank, follow, owner changes) need GitHub sign-in or an API token, so they are not covered.

The crates.io data access policy (https://crates.io/data-access) asks clients to send at most 1 request per second and to use a descriptive User-Agent. For bulk data, use the database dump or the sparse index (index.crates.io) instead.

Version-specific commands (get-version, list-dependencies, get-readme, list-source-files, get-docs-status, get-version-downloads) need an exact version string. Get it from get-crate's default_version or from list-versions' num.
To list the crates a user or team owns: call get-user / get-team to get the numeric id, then call search-crates with --user_id / --team_id.
To list the crates in a category or with a keyword: call search-crates with --category <slug> or --keyword <kw>.
list-reverse-dependencies returns the dependent crate versions (crate, num). The raw response also has a 'dependencies' array with each dependent's version requirement, linked by version_id.
get-crate-downloads keys counts by numeric version id. list-versions returns each version's id, which you can use to map ids to version numbers.
list-versions returns at most 100 versions per call. Pagination for longer histories is seek-based (meta.next_page) and is not exposed here.
get-readme returns raw rendered HTML. get-advisories returns the RustSec OSV array (it may be empty or 404 for crates with no advisories).
The full OpenAPI spec is at https://crates.io/api/openapi.json.
about: crates.io, the Rust package registry.

The dataset UUID in data.gov.uk URLs (/dataset/{uuid}/{slug}) is the CKAN package id, and the slug is the CKAN 'name'. Either works with get-dataset.
search-datasets filtering uses Solr fq syntax: organization:<publisher-slug>, res_format:CSV, license_id:uk-ogl. Publisher slugs are in organization.name of search results.

The HTML directory search (/search?query=&publisher=&topic=&format=&sort=recent&open_government_licence_only=on&page=N) also works, but its result markup was not captured. The CKAN API is the reliable route.
Collection topic pages embed chart data in script#chart-<hash>-json, and the hash differs per page. Use download-collection-chart-data to get the series instead.

notes: The search API (search.api.fellesdatakatalog.digdir.no) is public and needs no auth, but it is rate-limited to about 10 requests per minute with a burst of 20. Exceeding the limit returns HTTP 429, so wait and retry.

Pagination is 0-based (page=0 is the first page). The response's 'page' object has totalElements and totalPages, and 'aggregations' has facet counts (orgPath, format, dataTheme, losTheme, accessRights) that you can reuse as filter values.
Filters are optional. Only pass the ones you need. orgPath is a prefix match: /STAT covers all state agencies, and /STAT/972417807/971526920 is SSB specifically.
Multilingual fields are objects keyed by language (nb, nn, no, en). Some records only have one language filled in, so check the other keys if 'nb' is missing.

Search hit 'id' values (UUIDs) are what get-dataset, get-data-service, get-concept and get-resource-rdf take. The web pages are at https://data.norge.no/nb/datasets/{id}, /nb/data-services/{id} and /concepts/{id}.
Sorting by newest exists in the UI (sortfield=FIRST_HARVESTED), but its request body was not recorded. Use lastXDays to find recently published items.

A SPARQL endpoint and a catalog-view API are documented at https://data.norge.no/nb/technical/api, and the search OpenAPI spec is at https://search.api.fellesdatakatalog.digdir.no/swagger-ui/index.html.

params.name: poly
params.description: Polygon as lat,lng:lat,lng:... Use instead of lat/lng.

params.name: date
params.description: Month in YYYY-MM format. Omit for the latest month.

commands.summary: All stop and searches a force reported for one month.

params.name: force

params.name: date
params.description: Month in YYYY-MM format. Omit for the latest month.

commands.name: stops-no-location
commands.summary: Stop and searches a force reported for one month that could not be mapped to a location.

params.name: date
params.description: Month in YYYY-MM format. Omit for the latest month.

commands.name: stops-at-location
commands.summary: Stop and searches at a specific street location id for one month.

params.name: location_id
params.description: Street location id (location.street.id from stops-street or crime results)

params.name: date
params.description: Month in YYYY-MM format. Omit for the latest month.

notes: No login is needed. All /api/ endpoints are public JSON.
Dates are months in YYYY-MM format. Data lags about two months behind today; use get-last-updated or list-dates to find the latest available month (2026-08 at recording time).
Location queries take either lat+lng (1-mile radius) or poly ('lat,lng:lat,lng:...'), not both. A get-neighbourhood-boundary result can be joined into a poly string.
Very large areas or polygons can fail with HTTP 503 when the result would exceed 10,000 crimes. Use a smaller area if that happens.
Locations are anonymised to nearby points. location.street.id is the location_id accepted by crimes-at-location, outcomes-at-location and stops-at-location.
Anti-social behaviour crimes have an empty persistent_id and no outcomes, so get-crime-outcomes cannot look them up.
Text fields such as bio, description, issue and action contain HTML markup.
The API is rate-limited (about 15 requests/second). Not every force publishes stop and search data every month; check list-dates.

generate-csv-download submits a Django form protected by a CSRF token taken from /data/. The recording only shows the include_crime dataset field, and the request was held, not sent, so the response format was not seen.

This CLI searches and reads datasets, APIs (data services), organisations, specifications, concepts and terminologies through the public EntryScape/EntryStore backends (admin.dataportal.se and editera.dataportal.se). No login is needed.

commands.name: search-datasets
commands.summary: Full-text search of public datasets (dcat:Dataset) in the national catalogue, with sorting and offset paging

params.name: q
params.description: A single search word, matched against title, description, keywords and all text. Use * for everything. Do not use spaces; see notes.

params.name: api_limit
params.description: Results per page (sent to the site as "limit"; clify's own --limit only shapes the output)

params.name: offset
params.description: Number of results to skip, used for paging

params.name: sort
params.description: Sort order: relevance, or most recently modified/created first

commands.summary: Full-text search of public APIs / data services (dcat:DataService) in the catalogue

params.name: q
params.description: A single search word. Use * for all data services.

params.name: api_limit
params.description: Results per page (sent to the site as "limit"; clify's own --limit only shapes the output)

commands.name: search-organisations
commands.summary: Search publishing organisations (foaf:Agent / foaf:Organization) by name or text

params.name: q
params.description: A single search word, e.g. part of the organisation name. Use * for all organisations.

params.name: api_limit
params.description: Results per page (sent to the site as "limit"; clify's own --limit only shapes the output)

commands.name: search-catalog-solr
commands.summary: Advanced: run a raw Solr query against the admin.dataportal.se catalogue store (filter by theme, access rights, publisher, type, with optional facets)

params.name: query
params.description: Solr query in EntryStore syntax. Escape colons inside unquoted URIs as \: (e.g. rdfType:http\://www.w3.org/ns/dcat#Dataset). Always include public:true.

params.name: api_limit
params.description: Results per page (sent to the site as "limit"; clify's own --limit only shapes the output)

params.name: sort
params.description: Sort order, e.g. 'score desc' or 'modified desc'

commands.name: get-entry
commands.summary: Get full DCAT metadata for a dataset, data service (API) or organisation by catalog and entry id (site URL ids like 389_8203 = catalog 389, entry 8203)

params.name: catalog
params.description: Catalog (context) id: the part before '_' in the site URL, e.g. 389 in /datasets/389_8203

params.name: entry
params.description: Entry id: the part after '_', e.g. 8203

commands.name: get-catalog-quality
commands.summary: Get the metadata-quality score (MQA percentage, score, rating) for a catalog

commands.name: search-concepts
commands.summary: Search concepts/terms (skos:Concept) in the national terminology store

params.name: api_limit
params.description: Results per page (sent to the site as "limit"; clify's own --limit only shapes the output)

commands.summary: List public terminologies (skos:ConceptScheme) in the terminology store

params.name: api_limit
params.description: Max results (sent to the site as "limit"; clify's own --limit only shapes the output)

commands.summary: Search specifications (information/data models, dx-prof Profiles) in the editera store

params.name: q
params.description: A single search word. Use * for all specifications.

params.name: api_limit
params.description: Results per page (sent to the site as "limit"; clify's own --limit only shapes the output)

commands.name: get-concept
commands.summary: Get a concept, terminology or specification entry from the editera store by catalog and entry id (site ids like /concepts/202_4778 or /terminology/202_1)

commands.name: list-detected-apis
commands.summary: List catalogue entries with an automatically detected OpenAPI definition (definition URL, version, format, CORS)

commands.name: get-theme-stats
commands.summary: Count of datasets per EU data theme (Transport, Economy, ...)

commands.name: get-organisation-stats
commands.summary: Organisations ranked by number of published datasets (labels and counts)

commands.name: get-dataset-history
commands.summary: Monthly history of the total number of datasets in the catalogue

commands.name: get-entity-counts
commands.summary: Total counts of concepts, terminologies and specifications

notes: Site URLs use {catalog}_{entry} ids: /datasets/389_8203, /dataservice/50_6104 and /organisations/827_223 map to get-entry catalog=389 entry=8203 (and so on). Concepts (/concepts/202_4778) and terminologies (/terminology/202_1) map to get-concept.

Search results come from EntryStore. Each child has entryId and info, whose URI contains .../store/{catalog}/entry/{entry}. Its metadata is keyed by resource URI and holds the dcterms:title, dcterms:description and dcat:keyword values.
q in the search commands is put straight into a Solr expression. Use one word or a wildcard (traf*). For multi-word or complex queries, use search-catalog-solr.
Filters in search-catalog-solr:
- Open data: add AND metadata.object.uri:"http://publications.europa.eu/resource/authority/access-right/PUBLIC"
- Transport theme: add AND metadata.object.uri:"http://publications.europa.eu/resource/authority/data-theme/TRAN"
- One publisher's datasets: add AND metadata.object.uri:"http://dataportal.se/organisation/SE2021006297"
- Data services: use rdfType:http\://www.w3.org/ns/dcat#DataService
Paging uses offset. The response field 'results' is the total hit count. The website's s=8 ('Senast ändrad') corresponds to sort='modified desc'.
The organisation and specification rdfType filters were inferred from the DCAT-AP-SE and dx-prof models, not captured exactly in the recording.
about: Sveriges dataportal (dataportal.se), Sweden's national open-data catalogue.

name: dev-to

commands.name: list-articles

notes: There is no keyword search command. /search/feed_content is blocked by robots.txt. To find articles, filter list-articles by tag, tags, username, top or state instead.
Article ids are numeric (id). Comment ids are short strings (id_code). get-comment-reaction-counts returns numeric comment ids, which are not id_codes.
In list responses, tag_list is an array. In single-article responses (get-article, get-article-by-path), tag_list is a comma-separated string.
Comment and article bodies are HTML in body_html. Replies are nested recursively in children.
list-articles filters can be combined. For example, tags + tags_exclude + state=rising + per_page.
Only public, signed-out reads are covered. Writes (reactions, bookmarks, follows, comments) were not captured because the explorer was not logged in.

name: devdocs
description: DevDocs (devdocs.io) is a single site that bundles many API documentation sets. This CLI lists the available docs, fetches a doc's index of entries and categories, and retrieves documentation pages or full offline bundles as static JSON or HTML from documents.devdocs.io.

commands.name: list-docs
commands.summary: List every documentation set on DevDocs with its slug, version, release, mtime and size. Use the slug in the other commands.

commands.name: list-entries
commands.summary: List all entries (name, path, type) in one documentation set's search index. DevDocs search is done on the client against this list, so filter the result by name to search.

params.name: slug
params.description: Documentation slug from list-docs, e.g. git, css, javascript, html, dom, http, python~3.13 (versioned slugs use ~)

commands.name: list-types
commands.summary: List the categories (types) of one documentation set, with entry counts and slugs, e.g. 'Branching and Merging' for git or 'Elements' for html.

params.name: slug
params.description: Documentation slug from list-docs, e.g. git, html, python~3.13

commands.name: get-doc-home
commands.summary: Get the HTML home/overview page of one documentation set.

params.name: slug
params.description: Documentation slug from list-docs, e.g. git, python~3.13

commands.name: get-page
commands.summary: Get the HTML content of one documentation page, using the slug and an entry path from list-entries.

params.name: slug
params.description: Documentation slug from list-docs, e.g. git, css, javascript, python~3.13

params.name: path
params.description: Entry path from list-entries with any '#anchor' removed, e.g. git-merge, properties/flex, global_objects/array/map, library/json

commands.name: download-doc
commands.summary: Download the full offline bundle of one documentation set: a JSON object that maps each page path to its HTML. This can be very large.

params.name: slug
params.description: Documentation slug from list-docs, e.g. git, javascript

notes: DevDocs has no server-side search API. To search, run list-entries for a doc and match entry names on the client side (the site does fuzzy matching).
Entry paths can contain '#anchor' (e.g. library/json#json.dumps). Pass only the part before '#' to get-page; the anchor points to a section inside that page.
Entry paths can contain slashes (e.g. properties/flex). These must be sent unescaped in the URL.
Versioned docs use slugs like python~3.13 or angular~21. Get the slugs from list-docs.
The web app adds ?<mtime> to document URLs only to bust the cache. It is not required.
Nothing requires login, and there is no pagination.
about: DevDocs (devdocs.io) is a single site that bundles many API documentation sets.

name: developer-mozilla
description: MDN Web Docs (developer.mozilla.org) is Mozilla's web developer documentation. This CLI searches the docs, fetches any doc page as structured JSON, lists every doc title/URL for a locale, and looks up browser compatibility data.

commands.name: search-docs
commands.summary: Full-text search of MDN documentation, 10 results per page, optionally limited to one locale

params.name: locale
params.description: Docs locale to search, e.g. en-US, fr, de, es, ja, ko, pt-BR, ru, zh-CN, zh-TW

commands.name: get-doc
commands.summary: Get one MDN doc page as structured JSON: title, summary, body sections (HTML), TOC, parents, translations, and BCD keys

params.name: locale
params.description: Docs locale, e.g. en-US, fr, de, ja

params.name: path
params.description: Doc path after /{locale}/docs/, with slashes kept, e.g. Web/API/Fetch_API or Web/HTML/Reference/Elements. Take it from a search result's mdn_url by removing the '/{locale}/docs/' prefix.

commands.name: list-docs
commands.summary: List every doc in a locale as {title, url}, ordered by popularity (MDN's quick-search index)

params.name: locale
params.description: Docs locale, e.g. en-US, fr, de, ja

commands.name: get-browser-compat
commands.summary: Get browser compatibility data (support per browser/version, status, spec URL) for a BCD feature key such as api.fetch or html.elements.details

params.name: feature
params.description: Dot-separated BCD feature path, e.g. api.fetch, api.Window.fetchLater, html.elements.details, css.properties.display. get-doc lists these keys in its browserCompat field.

notes: search-docs has no sort option. The site's sort=popularity URL parameter is not passed to the API. Each result includes a popularity score you can sort by yourself.
search-docs accepts one locale per call. The site can search several locales at once by repeating locale=; to do that here, run the command once per locale.

To get a doc's path for get-doc, take mdn_url (from search-docs) or url (from list-docs) and drop the leading '/{locale}/docs/'. Example: '/en-US/docs/Web/API/Fetch_API' becomes path 'Web/API/Fetch_API' with locale 'en-US'. The slashes in path must be kept literally.
get-doc body sections are HTML strings in body[].value.content. Category pages such as Web/HTML/Reference/Elements contain their listings as HTML tables inside those sections.
get-doc returns a browserCompat array of BCD keys. Pass those keys to get-browser-compat as the feature argument.
list-docs returns a very large array covering every doc in the locale. Prefer search-docs for targeted lookups.
The HTTP Observatory (/en-US/observatory/analyze?host=) starts each scan with a write request that was not recorded, so no command is provided for it.
The explorer was not signed in, so no signed-in user features were recorded. get-current-user works anonymously and returns null user fields.
about: MDN Web Docs (developer.mozilla.org) is Mozilla's web developer documentation.

notes: A binding is one issue or volume. Use bindingId from search-materials or search-articles with get-binding, get-page-ocr and get-ocr-hits.

OAI-PMH returns at most one batch per call. Follow resumptionToken manually if the response includes one.

notes: All data is public and nothing needs a login. Digitraffic asks clients to send a Digitraffic-User header and to accept gzip compression (Accept-Encoding: gzip).

The road, rail and marine API endpoints come from the explorer summary and the public Swagger docs (tie/rata/meri.digitraffic.fi/swagger). Only the www.digitraffic.fi pages and the status JSON appear in the request digest.

Data is live, so ids in examples can expire. Situation ids for get-traffic-message should be taken from list-traffic-messages. Train composition data only exists for long-distance trains on dates that have been published.
Rail station codes are short codes such as HKI, TPE and TKU; get them from list-rail-stations.
Announcement filtering (traffictype/tag) may run client-side on the static site. If the server ignores the filter, check the trafficType and tag fields in the output.
Announcement texts are in Finnish.
about: Digitraffic (Fintraffic) offers open, real-time Finnish road, rail and marine traffic data.

notes: The HTML pages (home, /toc, /article) are behind Cloudflare, and /search/* is disallowed by robots.txt. Use only the public API, OAI-PMH and the feed.

Search queries are Elasticsearch query_string (Lucene) syntax placed in the URL path. Use JSON dot-notation fields (bibjson.publisher.country:IR, bibjson.apc.has_apc:false, bibjson.year:2021) and combine them with AND/OR. Append .exact for exact match on full field names. Wildcards (*) are rejected.
Forward slashes in queries (e.g. DOIs) are escaped automatically by the API.
Search responses include total, page, pageSize and next/last URLs. The maximum pageSize is 100, and deep paging is limited, so narrow the query instead.
Sorting by bibjson.year on articles returns bad_request. created_date and last_updated work.

OAI-PMH ListRecords returns one batch plus a resumptionToken under OAI-PMH.ListRecords.resumptionToken. Fetching later batches needs /oai?verb=ListRecords&resumptionToken=..., which this CLI does not wrap.
Write endpoints (applications/articles CRUD) need a publisher api_key and are not included.
Full data dumps are available on request (see /docs/public-data-dump/), and a journal CSV export is documented at /docs/journal-csv.
about: DOAJ (Directory of Open Access Journals): search and look up open-access journals and articles through DOAJ's public v4 API, OAI-PMH endpoint and Atom feed.

name: docs-python
description: Official Python documentation (docs.python.org, a static Sphinx site). The CLI fetches the glossary as JSON, the module index, the general index by letter, tables of contents, What's New highlights, doc pages, the API entries on a page, and documentation downloads, for any docs version.

commands.name: get-glossary
commands.summary: Get every Python glossary term with its HTML definition, as a JSON object keyed by term

params.name: version
params.description: Docs version: '3' (latest stable) or a specific version such as '3.12' or '3.13'

commands.name: list-modules
commands.summary: List all standard-library modules from the Python Module Index, with descriptions and doc links

commands.name: get-index-letter
commands.summary: List general index entries (functions, classes, keywords, topics) that start with a given letter, with links to where each is documented

params.name: letter
params.description: Uppercase index letter A-Z, or 'Symbols' or '_'

commands.name: list-toc
commands.summary: List the table of contents (chapters and pages) of a docs section such as the library reference, tutorial, HOWTOs, language reference or What's New

commands.name: get-page
commands.summary: Get a documentation page (module reference, tutorial chapter, HOWTO, What's New) with its title, breadcrumb, source link and full text

params.name: section
params.description: Docs section directory, e.g. library, tutorial, howto, reference, whatsnew, builtins

commands.name: get-api-entries
commands.summary: List the API objects (functions, classes, methods, attributes, exceptions, data) documented on a page, each with signature, anchor and first description paragraph

commands.name: get-release-highlights
commands.summary: Get the 'Summary – Release highlights' bullet points from a Python release's What's New page

params.name: version
params.description: Docs version to read from: '3' (latest) or e.g. '3.12'

commands.name: list-downloads
commands.summary: List downloadable documentation archives (PDF, HTML, plain text, EPUB) for a docs version

notes: Full-text search (search.html) runs in the browser against searchindex.js, so the server returns no results. To find things, use list-modules, get-index-letter (general index by letter), get-glossary or list-toc, then get-page.
The version path param accepts '3' (latest stable, currently 3.15) or a specific version such as '3.12'. Translations use a language prefix in the URL, e.g. /fr/3/ (not exposed as a param).

Links in results are relative to the page, e.g. 'library/json.html#module-json' from the module index, or 'asyncio-task.html#asyncio.Task' from a library page. To call get-page, split the link into section (directory) and page (file name without .html).
get-page returns the full page text in 'content', which can be large. Use get-api-entries for a compact list of the functions and classes on a reference page.
Glossary bodies are HTML fragments, and their links are relative to glossary.html.
about: Official Python documentation (docs.python.org, a static Sphinx site).

notes: docs.rs is public and server-rendered. No login is needed and every command is read-only.
Crate package names can contain dashes (e.g. serde-saphyr). The rustdoc path segment {crate} is the library name with underscores (serde_saphyr). Use resolve-crate or get-crate's docs_url to find it.
version accepts 'latest', an exact version, or a semver requirement such as ^1.2.
search-crates pagination uses an opaque 'paginate' token from the HTML 'Next Page' link. Without it, only the first 30 results are returned; narrow the query or change sort instead.
In-docs search (?search=) and per-platform docs (target-redirect) run client-side or redirect. They are not exposed. Use list-crate-items to find items.
get-source-file returns the file text with line numbers prefixed; list-source-files with dir='' lists the package root, and subfolders need a trailing slash (e.g. src/).
about: docs.rs is the documentation host for Rust crates.

notes: Times in GeoJSON responses (properties.time, properties.updated) are Unix epoch milliseconds in UTC. Coordinates are [longitude, latitude, depth_km].

search-earthquakes paging: offset is 1-based and limit maxes out at 20000. Without starttime, the server defaults to the last 30 days. Use count-earthquakes first for large queries; it returns maxAllowed=20000.
Use either a bounding box (min/max latitude/longitude) or a radius (latitude + longitude + maxradiuskm), not both.
Event ids come from the feature 'id' field in get-feed or search-earthquakes results. Pass them to get-event.

To get product contents, read the product id from get-event: properties.products.<type>[0].id, e.g. oaf for get-aftershock-forecast and shakemap for get-shakemap-contours. Each product's 'contents' map also gives direct URLs for every file (PAGER XML, DYFI GeoJSON, and others).
Summary feeds update about every minute. 'significant' is chosen by the USGS significance score and PAGER alert, not by magnitude.
No authentication is needed. All endpoints are public USGS APIs.

notes: Domain ids are case-sensitive. Group domains (allebi, proteinSequences, genomes, literature, ...) aggregate source domains (uniprot, pdbe, pubmed, ...). Each result's 'source' field gives its source domain; use that for entry and xref lookups.
Valid 'fields', 'facets' and 'sort' values differ per domain. Check get-domain-info first: requesting fields that are not retrievable can cause an error.
Without a 'fields' parameter, search results contain only id, acc and source.
Facet filter syntax is facetId:value, comma-separated (e.g. TAXONOMY:9606,status:Reviewed). Use get-search-facets to discover values.
Sort syntax is field:descending or field:ascending, e.g. sort=publication_date:descending on pubmed.
Paging is offset-based: start=0,15,30... with size up to 100.
UniProt entries accept either the accession (P01308) or the entry name (INS_HUMAN) as the id.
fetch-sequence returns plain text (e.g. FASTA), not JSON.

params.description: Dataset code, e.g. une_rt_m, tps00203, nama_10_gdp

params.name: geo
params.description: Geo code, e.g. DE, FR, EU27_2020 (see get-dataset-dimensions / get-codelist geo)

params.name: age
params.description: Age class code, e.g. TOTAL, Y_LT25, Y25-74, Y15-74

params.name: unit
params.description: Unit code, e.g. PC_ACT, THS_PER, CP_MEUR

params.name: na_item
params.description: National accounts item, e.g. B1GQ (GDP) for nama_10_gdp

params.name: sinceTimePeriod
params.description: Only periods from this one on, e.g. 2020, 2024-01, 2023-Q1

params.name: untilTimePeriod
params.description: Only periods up to this one, e.g. 2025

params.name: lastTimePeriod
params.description: Return only the N most recent periods

commands.name: get-codelist
commands.summary: Get all codes and labels of a Eurostat codelist (e.g. geo = countries/regions/aggregates).

params.name: codelist
params.description: Codelist id (lowercase dimension id), e.g. geo, unit, sex, age, na_item

notes: Typical flow: search-datasets (or list-category-datasets) -> get-dataset-dimensions to learn valid codes -> get-data with those codes as filters.

get-data returns JSON-stat 2.0: 'value' is an object keyed by flat index computed from 'id' / 'size' and each dimension's category.index. Filter narrowly (geo, lastTimePeriod), because unfiltered requests on large datasets can be huge or rejected.
Filter params on get-data are dataset-specific. Only dimensions that exist in the dataset are valid. The API also accepts repeated keys (e.g. geo=DE&geo=FR) for several values.
Timestamps such as lastUpdate, lastDataUpdate and eurobaseLastDataUpdate are Unix epoch milliseconds.
Bulk file downloads (not wrapped as commands): /eurostat/api/dissemination/sdmx/2.1/data/{code}?format=TSV (also SDMX-CSV), plus the ESMS metadata page at /eurostat/cache/metadata/en/{code}_esms.htm.
Dataset view in the browser: https://ec.europa.eu/eurostat/databrowser/view/{code}/default/table
about: Eurostat Data Browser (ec.europa.eu/eurostat/databrowser): search and browse EU statistical datasets, inspect dataset metadata, dimensions, codelists…

name: ecb-europa
description: ECB Data Portal (data.ecb.europa.eu): search European Central Bank statistical series (HICP inflation, exchange rates, SPF forecasts and more), fetch a series' observations as JSON, and pull raw data from the public ECB SDMX REST API.

commands.name: get-series-observations
commands.summary: Get the observations (period, value, unit, trend, status) of one ECB series by its full series key, e.g. HICP.M.U2.N.SERV00.4D0.ANR

params.name: series_key
params.description: Full series key: DATASET.dim1.dim2... For example HICP.M.U2.N.SERV00.4D0.ANR (euro area services inflation), EXR.D.USD.EUR.SP00.A (daily USD/EUR rate) or SPF.Q.U2.HICP.POINT.LT.Q.AVG.

commands.name: search-series
commands.summary: Keyword search for ECB data series, optionally filtered by concept tag; returns links to series detail pages that contain the series keys

params.name: layerType
params.description: Result layer: KL = key series, DL = data layer (all series), AL = all layers

params.name: tag
params.description: Concept/tag filter as shown in the facet list, e.g. 'Services'

params.name: page
params.description: Zero-based page index (0 = first page, 1 = second page)

commands.name: get-sdmx-data
commands.summary: Download series data as CSV from the public ECB SDMX REST API (data-api.ecb.europa.eu); supports wildcard keys and period filters

params.name: dataset
params.description: Dataflow id, e.g. EXR, HICP, SPF

params.name: key
params.description: Series key without the dataset prefix. Dimensions are dot-separated; leave a dimension empty for wildcard and join several values with '+', e.g. M.USD+GBP.EUR.SP00.A

params.name: startPeriod
params.description: Start period: YYYY, YYYY-MM, YYYY-Qn or YYYY-MM-DD

params.name: endPeriod
params.description: End period, same formats as startPeriod

params.name: lastNObservations
params.description: Return only the last N observations of each series

commands.name: list-dataflows
commands.summary: List all ECB dataflows (dataset ids, names and their data structure ids) from the SDMX REST API

commands.name: get-data-structure
commands.summary: Get the SDMX data structure definition (dimensions, concepts and code lists) for a dataset, e.g. ECB_EXR1 for EXR

params.name: dsd_id
params.description: Data structure definition id, as returned by list-dataflows (str:Structure.Ref.@id), e.g. ECB_EXR1 (EXR), ECB_ICP1 (HICP)

notes: All endpoints are public and need no login.

get-series-observations returns a JSON array of observations, newest first. OBS is the rounded display value and OBS_VALUE_AS_IS is the full-precision value. PERIOD is a UTC timestamp of the period start; PERIOD_NAME is human-readable.

Series key pattern for HICP: HICP.{freq M/A}.{area: U2=euro area, DE, FR, IT, ...}.N.{item: 000000=all items, SERV00=services, NRGY00=energy, FOOD00=food, XEF000=core, IGXE00=non-energy industrial goods, 040000=housing...}.4D0.{ANR=annual rate | INX=index}.
Series key pattern for exchange rates: EXR.{D/M/A}.{currency}.EUR.SP00.A, e.g. EXR.D.USD.EUR.SP00.A.
Search results pages are zero-based: page=1 is the second page. Result links have the form /data/datasets/{DATASET}/{SERIES_KEY}; pass the last path segment to get-series-observations.

The SDMX commands (get-sdmx-data, list-dataflows, get-data-structure) use the documented public API at data-api.ecb.europa.eu. Their XML responses are converted to JSON and can be large; prefer detail/lastNObservations to limit size.
Not captured: the geographical-area and dataset filters, the sort order of search results, and the data-cart and currency-converter actions (the converter runs only in the browser).
about: ECB Data Portal (data.ecb.europa.eu): search European Central Bank statistical series (HICP inflation, exchange rates, SPF forecasts and more), fetch…

name: eia
description: U.S. Energy Information Administration (EIA): energy statistics through the public Open Data API v2 (routes, data queries, facets, legacy series IDs), dnav data tables, Today in Energy articles, daily and weekly fuel prices, glossary and FAQs.

commands.name: list-api-datasets
commands.summary: List the top-level EIA Open Data API v2 dataset categories (coal, electricity, natural-gas, petroleum, ...).

commands.name: get-api-route
commands.summary: Get metadata for a top-level API v2 category (e.g. natural-gas, electricity): its child routes.

params.name: route
params.description: Single path segment category id from list-api-datasets, e.g. natural-gas, electricity, petroleum (multi-level paths containing '/' are not supported because the slash gets encoded)

commands.name: list-api-facet-values
commands.summary: List the allowed values (id and name) of one facet of a two-level API v2 dataset, e.g. all stateid codes for electricity/retail-sales.

params.name: dataset
params.description: Leaf dataset id under the category (single segment), e.g. retail-sales

params.name: facet
params.description: Facet id from the route metadata, e.g. stateid, sectorid

commands.name: get-data-table
commands.summary: Read a dnav summary data table (e.g. U.S. or state natural gas prices): one row per series with the latest values and a link to its history.

params.name: table
params.description: Table id. The area and frequency are encoded in it, e.g. NG_PRI_SUM_DCU_NUS_M (U.S., monthly), ng_pri_sum_dcu_STX_m (Texas, monthly), ng_pri_sum_dcu_STX_a (Texas, annual)

commands.name: get-series-history-table
commands.summary: Read the full-history table of a dnav series, one row per decade (e.g. Texas natural gas wellhead price, annual).

params.name: series
params.description: History page id from get-data-table historyUrl (without ./hist/ and .htm), e.g. na1140_stx_3a, n3010tx3m

commands.name: list-recent-articles
commands.summary: List the latest Today in Energy articles with type, date, title, link and tags.

commands.name: get-article
commands.summary: Get the full text of a Today in Energy article by id.

commands.name: list-articles-by-tag
commands.summary: List all Today in Energy articles that carry a tag (e.g. electricity, natural gas, solar).

params.name: tag
params.description: Tag name as listed by list-article-tags, e.g. electricity, natural gas, liquid fuels

commands.name: list-article-tags
commands.summary: List every Today in Energy article tag.

commands.name: list-article-archive
commands.summary: List Today in Energy articles for one year from the archive, grouped by month in the page.

params.name: year
params.description: Year to list, e.g. 2025. Omit for the current year.

commands.name: get-daily-prices
commands.summary: Get Today in Energy daily prices: wholesale spot petroleum, natural gas and electricity, retail fuel, prompt-month futures and financial indicators.

commands.name: get-gasoline-diesel-prices
commands.summary: Get the weekly U.S., regional and state retail prices for regular gasoline and on-highway diesel (Gasoline and Diesel Fuel Update).

commands.name: list-glossary-terms
commands.summary: List EIA glossary terms and definitions for a fuel topic or a starting letter.

params.name: topic
params.description: Fuel topic or a single letter A-Z

commands.name: get-faq
commands.summary: Get an EIA FAQ answer and the related FAQs on the same topic.

params.name: t
params.description: FAQ topic id (from related FAQ links), e.g. 9 = Diesel

notes: API v2 commands use EIA's public key, the one the site's API browser uses. API values come back as strings. A data query returns at most 5000 rows; page with offset/length.

Discover datasets top-down: list-api-datasets → get-api-route (route='natural-gas', then 'natural-gas/pri', and so on) → list-api-facet-values → query-api-data. Route paths contain slashes, e.g. 'electricity/retail-sales'.
query-api-data exposes common facets (stateid, sectorid, series, duoarea, process, product). Use only the facets the route's metadata lists.

dnav table ids encode area and frequency, e.g. ng_pri_sum_dcu_{AREA}_{m|a} with AREA like NUS (U.S.) or STX (Texas). get-data-table's historyUrl gives the id for get-series-history-table. The 'values' and 'row' fields hold the whole row text.
Article urls are relative (detail.php?id=N). Pass N to get-article.
search-glossary is a POST search form. It was not sent during exploration, so its result layout is assumed to match list-glossary-terms.
Site search goes to search.usa.gov and is not covered. The RSS XML feeds were blocked during recording.
about: U.S. Energy Information Administration (EIA): energy statistics through the public Open Data API v2 (routes, data queries, facets, legacy series IDs), dnav…

name: endoflife
description: endoflife.date is a public catalog of end-of-life dates and support lifecycles for software products. This CLI wraps its public JSON API v1 and Atom feeds to list products, categories, tags and identifiers, and to look up release cycles and EOL dates.

commands.name: list-products
commands.summary: List all tracked products (slug, label, category, tags, aliases)

commands.name: export-products-full
commands.summary: Dump all products with full details including every release cycle (large response)

commands.name: get-product
commands.summary: Get a product's metadata: label, category, tags, aliases, identifiers, version command, links

params.name: product
params.description: Product slug as returned by list-products 'name', e.g. python, nodejs, alpine-linux

commands.name: list-releases
commands.summary: List all release cycles of a product with release, LTS, end-of-active-support and EOL dates

commands.name: get-latest-release
commands.summary: Get the latest release cycle of a product with its support and EOL dates

commands.name: get-release
commands.summary: Get one release cycle of a product (e.g. python 3.12) with its support and EOL status and dates

params.name: release
params.description: Release cycle name as in list-releases 'name', e.g. 3.12 for python or 22 for nodejs

commands.name: list-categories
commands.summary: List product categories (e.g. framework, server-app, database, lang, os, service)

commands.name: list-products-by-category
commands.summary: List products in a category

params.name: category
params.description: Category name from list-categories, e.g. database, lang, os, framework, server-app, service

commands.name: list-tags
commands.summary: List all product tags (e.g. amazon, linux-distribution, java-distribution)

commands.name: list-products-by-tag
commands.summary: List products that have a given tag

params.name: tag
params.description: Tag name from list-tags, e.g. amazon, database, linux-distribution

commands.name: list-identifier-types
commands.summary: List supported product identifier types (purl, cpe, ...)

commands.name: list-identifiers
commands.summary: List all identifiers of a given type (e.g. CPE or purl strings) mapped to product slugs; use it to resolve a CPE/purl to a product

params.name: type
params.description: Identifier type from list-identifier-types, e.g. cpe or purl

commands.name: list-new-products
commands.summary: Recently added products, newest first (Atom feed)

commands.name: list-product-events
commands.summary: Timeline of a product's release and end-of-life events (Atom feed)

notes: The site is public and read-only. No login is needed and no command changes data.

Product slugs are the 'name' field from list-products (e.g. python, nodejs, alpine-linux). Aliases such as 'alma' or 'adonis' are listed there but may not resolve as API paths, so use the canonical name.

Dates are ISO YYYY-MM-DD strings. Fields such as eolFrom, eoasFrom and ltsFrom can be null when a date is unknown or does not apply. isEol, isEoas and isMaintained are computed as of the API's generated_at time.
eoas means end of active support and eoes means end of extended support. The product 'labels' object (shown by get-product) gives the product-specific names for these phases.
Release cycle names are product-specific strings, e.g. '3.12' for python or '22' for nodejs. Use list-releases to find valid values for get-release.

The API has no server-side search or pagination. To find a product by name, filter the output of list-products by name, label or aliases. export-products-full returns every product with every release, so the response is large.
Site search runs in the browser over the static index /assets/js/search-data.json, which has no query support. It is not exposed as a command.
Each product has an iCalendar file at /calendar/{product}.ics. It was observed only as a file download, not as a recorded request, so no command covers it.
about: endoflife.date is a public catalog of end-of-life dates and support lifecycles for software products.

name: ensembl
description: Ensembl (ensembl.org) genome browser: search thousands of genome assemblies, read genome metadata and stats, look up genes, transcripts, proteins, homologues, external references and variants (with predicted consequences), and fetch reference sequence through Ensembl's public JSON and GraphQL APIs.

commands.name: search-genomes
commands.summary: Search genome assemblies by name. Can list every assembly of one species by taxonomy id, and can sort (e.g. by contig N50) and paginate.

params.name: query
params.description: Free-text search: common name, scientific name or assembly name/accession

params.name: species_taxonomy_id
params.description: NCBI species taxonomy id. Restricts results to all assemblies of that species (e.g. 9606 = human, 10090 = mouse)

params.name: sort
params.description: Field to sort by, e.g. contig_n50. Omit for relevance ranking

commands.name: export-genomes-csv
commands.summary: Download genome search results as CSV text, matching search-genomes for the same query.

params.name: species_taxonomy_id
params.description: NCBI species taxonomy id that restricts the export to one species' assemblies

commands.name: get-genome
commands.summary: Get metadata for one genome by its UUID: assembly, providers, annotation version/date, release and reference status.

commands.name: get-genome-stats
commands.summary: Get statistics for a genome: assembly (N50, length, GC%), coding, non-coding, pseudogene and variation counts.

commands.name: get-genome-example-objects
commands.summary: Get example gene, location and variant ids for a genome. These are handy starting points for gene and variant lookups.

commands.name: list-popular-species
commands.summary: List popular species with their taxonomy id and number of available genomes.

commands.name: list-genome-groups
commands.summary: List genome group categories, such as external projects like VGP and BGE, with genome counts.

commands.name: get-genome-counts
commands.summary: Get the total number of genomes in Ensembl and the count per taxonomic group (Animals, Archaea, …).

commands.name: list-releases
commands.summary: List Ensembl data releases (name, type integrated/partial, is_current).

commands.name: search-genes
commands.summary: Search genes by symbol, name or stable id within one genome. Returns stable ids, biotype and location.

params.name: query
params.description: Gene symbol, name or Ensembl stable id

params.name: genome_id
params.description: Genome UUID to search in (default: Human GRCh38.p14)

bodyTemplate.query: {query}

commands.name: search-variants
commands.summary: Search variants (e.g. by rsID) within one genome.

bodyTemplate.query: {query}

commands.name: get-gene-summary
commands.summary: Get a gene's versioned stable id, symbol, chromosome location, strand and biotype.

params.name: geneId
params.description: Ensembl gene stable id (unversioned ok), e.g. ENSG00000139618

bodyTemplate.query: query GeneSummary($genomeId: String!, $geneId: String!) { gene(by_id: { genome_id: $genomeId, stable_id: $geneId }) { stable_id unversioned_stable_id symbol slice { location { start end } strand { code } region { name } } metadata { biotype { label } } } }

commands.name: get-gene-overview
commands.summary: Get a gene's full name, alternative symbols (synonyms), HGNC accession and biotype.

bodyTemplate.query: query GeneOverview($genomeId: String!, $geneId: String!) { gene(by_id: { genome_id: $genomeId, stable_id: $geneId }) { alternative_symbols name stable_id symbol metadata { name { accession_id url } biotype { value } } } }

commands.name: get-gene-structure
commands.summary: Get a gene's transcripts with exon layout, CDS coordinates, protein product ids and canonical/MANE flags. This is what the feature explorer gene view draws.

bodyTemplate.query: query DefaultEntityViewerGene($genomeId: String!, $geneId: String!) { gene(by_id: { genome_id: $genomeId, stable_id: $geneId }) { stable_id symbol unversioned_stable_id version slice { location { start end length } strand { code } } transcripts_page(page: 1, per_page: 100) { transcripts { stable_id unversioned_stable_id slice { location { start end length } region { name } strand { code } } relative_location { start end } spliced_exons { relative_location { start end } exon { stable_id slice { location { length } } } } product_generating_contexts { product_type cds { relative_start relative_end } cdna { length } product { stable_id unversioned_stable_id length } } metadata { biotype { value } canonical { value label } mane { value label } } } } } }

commands.name: list-gene-transcripts
commands.summary: List all transcripts of a gene with biotype, length, canonical/MANE status and protein length. Also returns the gene location and region checksum.

bodyTemplate.query: query GeneForVariantTranscriptConsequences($genomeId: String!, $geneId: String!) { gene(by_id: { genome_id: $genomeId, stable_id: $geneId }) { stable_id unversioned_stable_id symbol slice { location { start end length } region { sequence { checksum } length } strand { code } } transcripts { stable_id unversioned_stable_id slice { location { length } } metadata { biotype { value } canonical { value label definition } mane { value label definition } } product_generating_contexts { product_type product { length } } } } }

commands.name: get-gene-external-references
commands.summary: Get cross-references (NCBI Gene, HGNC, OMIM, GeneCards, UniProt, RefSeq, …) for a gene and for each of its transcripts and proteins.

bodyTemplate.query: query GeneExternalReferences($geneId: String!, $genomeId: String!) { gene(by_id: { stable_id: $geneId, genome_id: $genomeId }) { stable_id symbol external_references { accession_id name description url source { id name } } transcripts_page(page: 1, per_page: 100) { transcripts { ...transcriptFields } } } } fragment transcriptFields on Transcript { stable_id slice { location { length } } external_references { accession_id name description url source { id name } } product_generating_contexts { product_type product { external_references { accession_id name description url source { id name } } } } metadata { canonical { value } mane { value } biotype { value } } }

commands.name: get-gene-homologies
commands.summary: List homologues/orthologues of a gene in other species, with homology type and percent identity/coverage.

params.name: geneId
params.description: Versioned Ensembl gene stable id, e.g. ENSG00000139618.19 (use stable_id from get-gene-summary)

bodyTemplate.query: query EntityViewerGeneHomologies($genomeId: String!, $geneId: String!) { homologies(genome_id: $genomeId, gene_stable_id: $geneId) { target_genome { genome_id common_name scientific_name assembly { accession_id name } } target_gene { stable_id symbol version unversioned_stable_id } query_genome { genome_id common_name scientific_name assembly { accession_id name } } query_gene { stable_id symbol version unversioned_stable_id } subtype { accession_id label value definition } stats { query_percent_id query_percent_coverage target_percent_id target_percent_coverage } } }

commands.name: get-transcript
commands.summary: Get one transcript's location, exons, CDS coordinates and protein product (id, length, sequence checksum).

params.name: transcriptId
params.description: Versioned Ensembl transcript stable id, e.g. ENST00000366667.6

bodyTemplate.query: query TranscriptForVariantTranscriptConsequences($genomeId: String!, $transcriptId: String!) { transcript(by_id: { genome_id: $genomeId, stable_id: $transcriptId }) { slice { location { start end length } } relative_location { start end length } spliced_exons { index relative_location { start end length } } product_generating_contexts { cds { relative_start relative_end nucleotide_length } product { stable_id length sequence { checksum } } } } }

commands.name: get-protein-domains
commands.summary: Get a protein's length and its domain/family matches (Pfam, PANTHER, InterPro, …) with positions.

params.name: productId
params.description: Versioned Ensembl protein stable id, e.g. ENSP00000369497.3

bodyTemplate.query: query ProteinDomains($genomeId: String!, $productId: String!) { product(by_id: { genome_id: $genomeId, stable_id: $productId }) { length family_matches { relative_location { start end } sequence_family { name description url source { name } } via { accession_id description url source { name } } } } }

commands.name: get-protein-structure-stats
commands.summary: Get PDBe summary counts for a UniProt accession: number of PDB structures, ligands, interaction partners and similar proteins.

commands.name: get-variant
commands.summary: Get variant details: location, alleles, allele type, dbSNP source, VEP prediction, citation count, phenotype assertions and population allele frequencies.

params.name: variantId
params.description: Variant id in the form {chromosome}:{position}:{rsID}, e.g. 1:230710048:rs699

bodyTemplate.query: query VariantDetails($genomeId: String!, $variantId: String!) { variant(by_id: { genome_id: $genomeId, variant_id: $variantId }) { name alternative_names { name url } slice { location { start end length } region { name } } allele_type { value } primary_source { url source { name release } } prediction_results { score result analysis_method { tool } } ensembl_website_display_data { count_citations } alleles { name allele_type { value } slice { location { start end } strand { code } } allele_sequence reference_sequence phenotype_assertions { feature } prediction_results { score result analysis_method { tool } } population_frequencies { is_minor_allele is_hpmaf allele_frequency } ensembl_website_display_data { count_transcript_consequences count_overlapped_genes count_regulatory_consequences count_variant_phenotypes count_gene_phenotypes representative_population_allele_frequency } } } }

commands.name: get-variant-consequences
commands.summary: Get the predicted molecular consequences of each allele of a variant on overlapping transcripts: consequence terms plus cDNA, CDS and protein positions with ref/alt.

bodyTemplate.query: query VariantPredictedMolecularConsequences($genomeId: String!, $variantId: String!) { variant(by_id: { genome_id: $genomeId, variant_id: $variantId }) { alleles { predicted_molecular_consequences { stable_id gene_stable_id gene_symbol cdna_location { ...RelativeLocationFields } cds_location { ...RelativeLocationFields } protein_location { ...RelativeLocationFields } consequences { value } } } } } fragment RelativeLocationFields on VariantRelativeLocation { start end length ref_sequence alt_sequence }

commands.name: get-region
commands.summary: Get a chromosome/region's length, topology and sequence checksum. Use the checksum with get-sequence.

bodyTemplate.query: query RegionChecksum($genomeId: String!, $regionName: String!) { region(by_name: { genome_id: $genomeId, name: $regionName }) { name length topology sequence { checksum } } }

commands.name: get-sequence
commands.summary: Fetch raw DNA or protein sequence (plain text) for a sequence checksum over a coordinate range, via refget. Uses 0-based start and exclusive end.

params.name: checksum
params.description: Sequence checksum: a region checksum from get-region, or a protein sequence checksum from get-transcript

params.name: start
params.description: 0-based start coordinate (inclusive). For a 1-based genomic position P, use P-1. Example: 230710027 for a variant flank

params.name: end
params.description: End coordinate (exclusive, 0-based). Equals the 1-based inclusive end. Length returned = end - start

notes: Most gene/variant commands take a genomeId (genome UUID). It defaults to Human GRCh38.p14 (59871324-7803-4234-856e-2a2bd96d7b3c). For other species, find the genome_id with search-genomes (use species_taxonomy_id to list all assemblies of one species).

Typical flow: search-genes → stable_id → get-gene-summary / get-gene-structure / list-gene-transcripts / get-gene-external-references / get-gene-homologies (homologies needs the versioned id, e.g. ENSG00000139618.19).

Variant ids use the form {chromosome}:{position}:{rsID} (e.g. 1:230710048:rs699). search-variants did not resolve rsIDs in the recording (0 hits), so build the id from a known position or from get-genome-example-objects.

Protein ids for get-protein-domains come from product.stable_id in get-gene-structure or get-transcript. UniProt accessions for get-protein-structure-stats (PDBe host) come from get-gene-external-references.
get-sequence returns plain text. Pass a region checksum (get-region) with genomic start/end, or a protein sequence checksum (get-transcript product.sequence.checksum) with protein coordinates.
export-genomes-csv was described by the explorer but not captured as a request; its parameters mirror search-genomes.
The GraphQL TranscriptSearch operation returned no hits for gene symbols or rsIDs, so it was left out; use search-genes instead.
The genome browser and BLAST are blocked by robots.txt and are not covered.
about: Ensembl (ensembl.org) genome browser: search thousands of genome assemblies, read genome metadata and stats, look up genes, transcripts, proteins, homologues…

name: fec
description: FEC.gov campaign finance data (via the public OpenFEC API at api.open.fec.gov/v1). The CLI covers candidate and committee lookups, fundraising and spending totals, itemized receipts and disbursements, outside spending, filings, elections, calendars and advisory opinions.

commands.name: search-candidate-names
commands.summary: Autocomplete or search candidates by name and get their FEC candidate IDs

params.name: q
params.description: Candidate name or part of it

params.name: api_key
params.description: api.data.gov API key. DEMO_KEY works but is heavily rate-limited; a free key is available at api.data.gov/signup

commands.name: search-committee-names
commands.summary: Autocomplete or search committees (campaigns, PACs, parties) by name and get their FEC committee IDs

params.name: q
params.description: Committee name or part of it

name: finlex
description: Finlex, the Finnish government's free legal database (statutes, Statute Book, translations and Supreme Court case law). This CLI searches all datasets, lists Statute Book entries and Supreme Court precedents, and fetches statute, translation and precedent detail pages and translation PDFs.

commands.summary: Keyword search across all Finlex data (legislation, government proposals, treaties, case law, officials). Returns hit count, category counts and hits as a Next.js server-action text stream.

commands.summary: Get a statute by number and year, e.g. 55/2001 (Employment Contracts Act). Returns the title and statute text.

params.name: number
params.description: Statute number within the year, e.g. 55. Some numbers have a suffix, e.g. 39-001 for the Criminal Code (1889).

commands.name: get-statute-translation
commands.summary: Get the English translation page of a statute by year and number, including the translation PDF link.

params.name: number
params.description: Statute number within the year, e.g. 55

commands.summary: List the Supreme Court material collections (precedents, rulings other than precedents, etc.) with last-update dates.

commands.name: list-latest-precedents
commands.summary: List the latest Supreme Court precedents (KKO).

commands.name: get-precedent
commands.summary: Get the full text of a Supreme Court precedent by year and number, e.g. KKO 2026:74.

params.name: number
params.description: Precedent number within the year, e.g. 74

notes: The 'search' command calls a Next.js server action identified by the next-action header. The id was recorded from the current build and may change when Finlex redeploys; if the call fails, take the new id from the search page's POST request.

The 'search' response is a React Server Components text stream, not plain JSON. The line starting '1:' holds an Elasticsearch-style JSON object: hits.total.value, hits.hits and aggregations.category.buckets.

Only limit=0 was recorded; it returned just the total and the per-category counts (GOVERNMENT_PROPOSALS, LEGISLATION, TREATIES, OFFICIALS, CASE_LAW), with an empty hits.hits. Non-zero limits are expected to return hits but were not observed.
Sort is only carried in the search page URL, not in the action body, so it may not affect action results.
Statute titles are often in Finnish or Swedish even on the /en pages. English texts exist only for statutes that have a translation (get-statute-translation).
Statutes and precedents are addressed as number/year, e.g. statute 55/2001 → year=2001 number=55. Some statute numbers have suffixes like '39-001'.
Find translation PDF ids in the links on the translation page. The recorded '?timestamp=' query parameter is only cache-busting and can be omitted.

Finlex began returning HTTP errors (likely rate limiting) after many rapid requests, so space out calls. Because of this, the Statute Book collection detail, amendments, open-data and government-proposals pages were not recorded.
The amendment-history tab (/en/legislation/{year}/{number}/amendment-history/{id}) was also not captured with enough detail to define a command.
Listing extractors use generic 'section#content li' selectors because the result markup was not fully visible in the recording, so fields may need light post-processing.
about: Finlex, the Finnish government's free legal database (statutes, Statute Book, translations and Supreme Court case law).

Record ids look like '<source>.<local id>', e.g. helmet.1830976 or museovirasto.2588B7F548C8DB31DF7968B845EB1520. The human-readable page is https://www.finna.fi/Record/{id}.

The get-authority example id was not seen in the recording. Take real ids from search-authorities.

Saving an opportunity requires signing in with Login.gov. The explorer was not logged in, so no save request was captured and no save command exists.
The 'Download all' attachments action on detail pages closed the browser page, so no request was captured for it.

RSS feed URLs from list-rss-feeds may redirect to page-not-found. GG_NewOppByCategory.xml did when tried.

Release dependencies are in the 'requirements' object of get-release. It is keyed by dependency name, and each entry has 'requirement' and 'optional'.
Security advisories and retirements appear in get-package (security_advisories, retirements) and in get-release (security_advisories, retirement).
get-release-file returns raw text. Use CHANGELOG.md or LICENSE as --path for changelogs and licenses. Not every package ships these files. Nested paths contain '/', e.g. lib/phoenix.ex.
Docs tarballs are binary at https://repo.hex.pm/docs/{name}-{version}.tar.gz. Hosted docs are at the docs_html_url returned by get-package and get-release.

The version diff page (/diff/{name}/{a}..{b}) is disallowed by robots.txt and is not covered. The package audit-log page (/packages/{name}/audit-logs) is not covered either, because its item structure was not visible.
The API search returns up to 100 packages per page. Increment --page until an empty array comes back.

notes: *.data endpoints are Remix single-fetch (turbo-stream) responses. They come back as one flat JSON array, not nested objects. Objects appear as {"_K": V}: K is the array index of the key-name string and V is the array index of the value. Negative numbers are sentinels: -5 means undefined and -7 means null. To read a value, follow the indices. Strings such as descriptions, tag names, digests and pull counts appear inline right after their key names, so scanning the array is often enough.
Global search (/search?q=) is behind a Cloudflare bot check. Use search-category-images (call list-categories first for the slugs) or list-publisher-repositories instead.
Official images use the 'library' namespace: /_/{image} on the site, and namespace=library for get-image-layers and get-organization. In Scout, repoName is the bare name (nginx).
Digest format differs by command: the tag list and Scout use sha256:<hex>, while get-image-layers needs sha256-<hex> (colon replaced by a dash).
The Scout GraphQL repoFeatures query returns 403 when not logged in. Whether imageSummariesByDigest works anonymously was not confirmed: only the repoFeatures 403 response was captured.
Sort values 'updated_at' and the badges/type values other than 'verified_publisher'/'image' come from the UI options; only pull_count, verified_publisher and image were confirmed in the recording.

list-repository-tags, get-official-image and get-repository use the matching Remix .data routes for pages that were recorded as HTML documents (/r/grafana/grafana, /_/nginx). Those exact .data URLs were not captured.

notes: The recording captured nothing useful. A Cloudflare bot check blocked every www.inaturalist.org page, and the only recorded request was a 307 on /observations. None of these commands were observed in the recording. They target iNaturalist's documented public read-only API (https://api.inaturalist.org/v1), which the iNaturalist web app calls. They should be verified, especially the example ids (observation 10000000 is an unverified guess).
All commands are anonymous reads. Nothing here needs login, and no write endpoints are included.
Responses share the envelope {total_results, page, per_page, results:[...]}. Detail endpoints (get-observation, get-taxon, get-user) also return a one-element results array.
iNaturalist asks API clients to stay around 60 requests per minute or less (roughly 1 per second) and to keep total volume low. Bulk downloads should use their export tools or GBIF instead.
Use search-places or search-taxa first to resolve names into place_id and taxon_id, then pass those to search-observations, list-species-counts or list-top-observers.
Taxon 47851 is the genus Quercus (oaks), and place 14 is California. Both are used in the examples.

notes: TAP (/TAP/sync) is the main data interface. It takes ADQL: SELECT <cols> FROM <table> WHERE <constraints>. Use 'select top N' or maxrec to limit rows. There is no paginated listing.

Useful tables: pscomppars (one row per confirmed planet, composite parameters), ps (all parameter sets; filter default_flag=1 for defaults), toi (TESS candidates), cumulative (Kepler KOIs), stellarhosts.
Common columns: pl_name, hostname, pl_orbper (days), pl_rade (Earth radii), pl_bmasse (Earth masses), pl_eqt (K), discoverymethod, disc_year, sy_dist (pc). Use get-table-columns to discover more.
Use plain ADQL WHERE clauses. Cloudflare's WAF blocked queries using contains(point(...),circle(...)) cone searches.
String literals in ADQL use single quotes. Name filters in list-host-planets are exact matches; use run-tap-query with "hostname like 'Kepler-%'" for wildcard matches.
robots.txt disallows /cgi-bin/TblView/nph-tblView, /cgi-bin/ExoOverview, /cgi-bin/nstedAPI and /cgi-bin/Lookup/nph-aliaslookup.py. The legacy nstedAPI is retired in favour of TAP.
No login is needed; all commands are public reads.

notes: No login is needed. All data comes from jsDelivr's public data API (data.jsdelivr.com/v1, OpenAPI spec at /v1/spec.yaml) and a public Algolia search key.
The 'name' param for gh packages is 'user/repo' (e.g. twbs/bootstrap). Scoped npm packages look like '@scope/pkg'. The slash must reach the server unencoded.
search-packages builds an Algolia 'params' query string, so query and filters values must be URL-encoded. The search page param is 0-based; the data.jsdelivr.com page params are 1-based.

Period values: day, week, month, quarter or year (rolling windows ending yesterday); s-month, s-quarter or s-year (last complete calendar period); or explicit periods such as 2026-09 or 2026-Q3 (see list-stats-periods). Browser and platform stats need s-* or explicit periods.
Stats responses include large per-day 'dates' maps. Use defaultFields totals unless you need the daily breakdown.

Workflow: search-packages → list-package-versions (get a version) → list-package-files / get-package-entrypoints / get-package-file-stats. The CDN file URL is https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/{type}/{name}@{version}/{file}.

Commands that take a version need an exact version. Get it from get-package (latestVersion), list-package-versions or get-package-meta.
Registry URLs on jsr.io (meta.json, {version}_meta.json, source files) return the HTML viewer if Accept is text/html, so these commands send Accept: application/json.

search-packages-by-runtime uses JSR's public Algolia search key. Runtime filter syntax is 'runtimeCompat.<runtime>:true' with runtime one of deno, node, bun, browser, workerd. Its page is 0-based, while the api.jsr.io commands use 1-based pages.
The api.jsr.io endpoints are JSR's documented public management API (see jsr.io/docs/api). No authentication is needed for reads.
Runtime compatibility values: true means it works, false means it does not, and a missing key means unknown.

notes: All commands scrape server-rendered HTML. robots.txt disallows the official JSON API (/api/*), so the CLI does not use it. Its schema is documented at https://lichess.org/openapi.yaml.

Cloudflare bot checks block the homepage, user profiles (/@/{user}), broadcast round pages, team search and some calendar months, so the CLI has no commands for them. Profile and broadcast urls in results are for reference only.
Other months of the broadcast calendar live at /broadcast/calendar/{year}/{month} (e.g. /broadcast/calendar/2026/9), but some of those pages are behind Cloudflare.
FIDE player urls look like /fide/{id}/{slug}. Split the url returned by search-fide-players to get both parts for get-fide-player and list-fide-player-broadcasts.
The rating columns are read by position (classical, rapid, blitz, age). A player with no rating in one category may have an empty cell.
get-tournament returns only the static header (format, start time, winner). Live standings are rendered client-side and are not included.
In get-top-players, limit is the {n} segment of /player/top/{n}/{perf}. It was seen only in the explorer's summary; the recorded URL was /player/top/blitz.
The explorer was not logged in, so every command is a public read.

An intermittent bot check (/__meb_verify, a 'Verifying your browser' page) blocked release detail (/release/{id}), artist tabs (/artist/{id}/releases) and label pages (/label/{id}). Those commands are omitted. If any command returns a page titled 'Verifying your browser', wait and retry.

HTML table rows for instrument tabs, release-group releases and country statistics return a 'row' field holding the whole row's text, because the columns cannot be targeted individually.

params.name: station
params.description: NDBC station ID, e.g. 44013 or 42001. C-MAN IDs are uppercase here, e.g. BZBM3. Some stations, such as 41001, return 404.

commands.summary: Get the last 5 days of standard meteorological data for a station (newest first) as a whitespace-delimited text table: WDIR, WSPD/GST in m/s, WVHT in m, PRES in hPa, temps in degC; 'MM' means missing

params.name: station
params.description: NDBC station ID, e.g. 44013 or 42001. C-MAN IDs are uppercase, e.g. BZBM3.

commands.name: list-latest-observations
commands.summary: Get the latest observation for every reporting station in one whitespace-delimited text table (columns include STN, LAT, LON, WDIR, WSPD, GST, WVHT, PRES, ATMP, WTMP; m/s, m, hPa, degC; 'MM' means mis

commands.name: get-station-table
commands.summary: Get the full station metadata table (ID, owner, type, hull, name, payload, location, timezone, forecast, note) as pipe-delimited text

notes: CloudFront blocks the HTML/PHP pages on www.ndbc.noaa.gov with 403. This includes station_page.php, the search pages and directory listings. Only the static data files used here are reachable.
The .spec and .ocean realtime files, historical stdmet files and the radial station search also return 403, so they are not included.
Text tables use two header lines starting with '#' (column names, then units). Missing values are written as 'MM'. Times are UTC.
Common columns: WDIR (deg), WSPD/GST (m/s), WVHT (m), DPD/APD (s), PRES (hPa), ATMP/WTMP/DEWP (degC), VIS (nmi), TIDE (ft).
Use list-active-stations or get-station-table to find station IDs. Not every active station has a realtime2 file; for example, 41001 returns 404.
The description field in get-latest-observation is an HTML fragment containing the observation time, location and measured values.
