name: news-ycombinator
description: Hacker News (news.ycombinator.com): read front page, new, past, Ask, Show and jobs listings, stories with comment trees, comment feeds, user profiles, submissions, comments and favorites, and post comments. Every command parses the server-rendered HTML.

commands.name: list-stories
commands.summary: List ranked stories from a Hacker News feed: front page (news), Ask HN, Show HN, best, or most active. Page-numbered.

params.name: feed
params.description: Which feed to list: news = front page, ask = Ask HN, show = Show HN, best = highest-voted recent stories, active = most active discussions

params.name: h
params.description: Only for feed=best: look-back window in hours

commands.name: list-new-stories
commands.summary: List the newest submissions, newest Ask HN, newest Show HN, or job postings, in chronological order.

params.name: feed
params.description: newest = all new links, asknew = new Ask HN, shownew = new Show HN, jobs = job postings

params.name: next
params.description: Pagination cursor: the item id from the page's 'More' link (normally the id of the last item shown). Omit for the first page.

params.name: n
params.description: Rank number for the first item on the next page (e.g. 31). Use together with next.

commands.name: list-front-page-by-day
commands.summary: List the stories that were on the Hacker News front page on a given past day.

commands.name: list-site-stories
commands.summary: List Hacker News submissions from a given domain or site path (e.g. github.com/antirez).

params.name: site
params.description: Domain or site path as HN shows it next to titles, e.g. nytimes.com or github.com/antirez

params.name: next
params.description: Pagination cursor: the item id from the 'More' link

params.name: n
params.description: Rank number of the first item on the next page, e.g. 31

commands.name: get-item
commands.summary: Get one story, Ask/Show post or comment by id: title, link, points, author, age, comment count and body text.

params.name: id
params.description: Hacker News item id (story or comment)

commands.name: list-item-comments
commands.summary: List the comment tree of a story or comment (flattened in thread order, with indent depth).

params.name: id
params.description: Hacker News item id whose comments to list

params.name: p
params.description: Page of comments, for very large threads

commands.name: list-new-comments
commands.summary: List the newest comments across Hacker News, with the story each one is on.

params.name: next
params.description: Pagination cursor: the comment id from the page's 'More' link

commands.name: list-best-comments
commands.summary: List the most-upvoted comments of the last N hours (48 by default).

params.name: h
params.description: Look-back window in hours. The site uses 48 when this is omitted.

commands.name: get-user
commands.summary: Get a Hacker News user's profile: username, account creation date, karma and about text, as label/value rows.

commands.name: list-user-submissions
commands.summary: List the stories a user has submitted, newest first.

params.name: next
params.description: Pagination cursor: the item id from the 'More' link

params.name: n
params.description: Rank number of the first item on the next page, e.g. 31

commands.name: list-user-comments
commands.summary: List a user's recent comments, with the story each one is on.

params.name: next
params.description: Pagination cursor: the comment id from the page's 'More' link

commands.name: list-leaders
commands.summary: List the top 100 Hacker News users by karma, in rank order.

commands.name: list-lists
commands.summary: List Hacker News's special listing pages (front, best, active, leaders, etc.) with descriptions.

notes: All data comes from server-rendered HTML. In story listings, points, author, age and comment count sit in a sibling row that cannot be reached from the item, so list commands return id, title, url and site. Run get-item with the id for points, author and comment count.
Story and comment ids are the numeric HN item ids. Pass them to get-item / list-item-comments, or build the link https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=<id>.

Pagination: news, ask, show, best, active, front, bestcomments and favorites use ?p=N. newest, asknew, shownew, jobs, from, submitted, threads and newcomments use the 'More' link cursor ?next=<id>&n=<rank>. In practice, next is the id of the last item on the current page.
get-user returns label/value rows (user, created, karma, about, ...).
add-comment needs a logged-in HN session. The hmac token is read from the reply form on item?id=<parent>. Comments are public and posted immediately.
Keyword search is not on this host: HN search is https://hn.algolia.com (API: https://hn.algolia.com/api/v1/search?query=...), which was not recorded.
Upvoting (vote?id=&how=up&auth=...) was not recorded and needs a per-item auth token on a logged-in page, so it is not included.
HN rate-limits rapid scraping. Keep request rates modest.
The list-user-favorites example (fagnerbrack) showed no items in the recording, so it may return an empty list.
about: Hacker News (news.ycombinator.com): read front page, new, past, Ask, Show and jobs listings, stories with comment trees, comment feeds, user profiles…

name: nhl
description: NHL stats (nhl.com/stats) via the NHL public JSON APIs (api.nhle.com/stats/rest and api-web.nhle.com). Covers league leaders, skater, goalie and team stat reports, player search, profiles and game logs, game details, standings, scores and schedules.

commands.name: get-skater-leaders

params.name: cayenneExp
params.description: Cayenne filter expression. Season is an 8-digit id like 20262027; gameType 2=regular season, 3=playoffs. You can append "and isRookie = 'Y'" or "and player.positionCode = 'D'".

commands.name: get-goalie-leaders
commands.summary: Top-10 goalie leaders by goals-against average, save percentage or shutouts in a season

params.name: cayenneExp
params.description: Cayenne filter expression, e.g. season=20262027 and gameType=2 and gamesPlayed >= 2

params.name: cayenneExp
params.description: Cayenne filter. Season range: gameTypeId=2 and seasonId<=20262027 and seasonId>=20262027. Prefix 'franchiseId=5 and ' to filter by franchise (ids from list-franchises). Add 'and skaterFullName likeIgn

params.name: api_limit

params.example: franchiseId=5 and gameTypeId=2 and seasonId<=20252026 and seasonId>=20252026

example.cayenneExp: franchiseId=5 and gameTypeId=2 and seasonId<=20252026 and seasonId>=20252026

params.name: cayenneExp
params.description: Cayenne filter, e.g. gameTypeId=2 and seasonId<=20262027 and seasonId>=20262027 (prefix franchiseId=N and ... to filter by franchise)

params.name: sort

params.name: api_limit

commands.summary: Find players by (partial) name to get their player id

params.name: playerId

commands.summary: Player game-by-game log for a season and game type (regular season or playoffs)

commands.name: get-game-boxscore

commands.name: get-game-play-by-play

commands.name: get-game-recap-stories

commands.name: get-standings
commands.summary: League standings as of a date (division, conference and wild-card ordering, records, points)

commands.name: list-standings-seasons
commands.summary: Seasons that have standings, with their date ranges and rules (ties, wild card, etc.)

commands.name: get-scores
commands.summary: All games and scores for a date (state, teams, score, goals)

commands.name: get-schedule
commands.summary: League schedule for the week starting on a date (games per day, teams, start times, broadcasts)

commands.name: get-schedule-calendar
commands.summary: Schedule calendar window for a date: start/end dates, previous/next week, and the list of teams

commands.name: list-seasons
commands.summary: All NHL seasons, newest first, with ids, dates, number of games and rules

commands.name: get-current-season
commands.summary: The season and game type the stats site currently defaults to

commands.name: list-franchises
commands.summary: All NHL franchises with ids (for franchiseId filters) and first/last seasons

commands.name: list-countries
commands.summary: Countries (and their states/provinces) usable as player nationality or birthplace filters

commands.name: list-drafts
commands.summary: NHL entry draft years and number of rounds

commands.name: get-glossary
commands.summary: Stats glossary: abbreviation, full name and definition of every stat

notes: Seasons are 8-digit ids like 20262027 (the 2026-27 season). gameType/gameTypeId: 2=regular season, 3=playoffs (1=preseason).

Stats reports (list-*-stats) filter with a Cayenne expression in cayenneExp, e.g. 'franchiseId=5 and gameTypeId=2 and seasonId<=20252026 and seasonId>=20252026'. Franchise ids come from list-franchises.
Name filter on stats reports: add 'and skaterFullName likeIgnoreCase "%Crosby%"' (use goalieFullName for goalies). To find a player id, use search-players.
sort is a JSON array of {property, direction}. Add a unique tiebreaker such as playerId (or teamId/franchiseId) so paging stays stable. Page with start (offset) and limit.
All-time or multi-season totals: widen the seasonId range and set isAggregate=true. Game-by-game rows: set isGame=true and filter on gameDate ("YYYY-MM-DD").
Date-based api-web endpoints (standings, score, schedule, schedule-calendar) accept 'now'. It answers with a 307 redirect to today's date.
Game ids are 10 digits: season start year + game type (02) + game number, e.g. 2026020119.
Ad and telemetry endpoints were skipped (rubicon, sodar, maze, blaze, satis), along with i18n bundles and the site config.

name: nhtsa-dot

commands.name: decode-vin
commands.summary: Decode a full or partial VIN (use * as a wildcard) into a flat record with make, model, year, body, engine, safety equipment, plant and more

params.name: vin
params.description: 17-character VIN or partial VIN; use * for unknown positions, e.g. 5UXWX7C5*BA

params.name: modelyear
params.description: Model year. Recommended for partial VINs; when set it overrides the year decoded from the VIN

commands.name: decode-wmi
commands.summary: Decode a World Manufacturer Identifier (the first 3 or 6 VIN characters) into its manufacturer, make and vehicle type

commands.name: list-models-for-make-year

commands.name: get-manufacturer-details
commands.summary: Look up manufacturers by full or partial name (or numeric manufacturer ID) and get address, country and vehicle types

params.name: manufacturer
params.description: Manufacturer name (partial match) or numeric Mfr_ID, e.g. tesla or 955

commands.name: list-wmis-for-manufacturer
commands.summary: List the WMI codes assigned to a manufacturer, matched by full or partial name or ID

params.name: manufacturer
params.description: Manufacturer name (partial match) or ID, e.g. hon

commands.name: list-canadian-spec-makes
commands.summary: List the makes that have Canadian Vehicle Specifications data for a model year

commands.name: list-canadian-spec-models
commands.summary: List the Canadian Vehicle Specifications model names for a year, optionally limited to one make

params.name: make
params.description: Make name in upper case as returned by list-canadian-spec-makes, e.g. FORD; empty for all makes

commands.name: get-canadian-specs
commands.summary: Get Canadian Vehicle Specifications dimensions (length, width, height, wheelbase, curb weight, track, weight distribution) for a year and make, optionally one model

params.name: make
params.description: Make in upper case, e.g. HONDA

params.name: model
params.description: Exact model name from list-canadian-spec-models, e.g. ACCORD 2DR COUPE LX-G/EX-L; empty for all models of the make

params.name: search
params.description: Keyword filter applied across all columns

commands.summary: Get a manufacturer's MID profile by manufacturer ID: contacts, address, makes and models, WMIs, manufacturer types and Part 565/566 filings

params.name: id

commands.name: get-modifier
commands.summary: Get a registered adapted-vehicle modifier's details (DBAs, address, phone, contact) by modifier ID

notes: The /api/vehicles/* endpoints are NHTSA's documented public REST API. They need no auth, and results are always under 'Results'. The API docs ask clients to rate-limit themselves (no hammering).
decode-vin accepts partial VINs with * wildcards. For partial VINs, pass modelyear. Check ErrorText or ErrorCode in the result ('0' means a clean decode).
Canadian spec make and model values are upper case and must match exactly. Get them from list-canadian-spec-makes and list-canadian-spec-models.

The MID manufacturer search (POST /mid/ then AjaxHandler565TopLevel/566TopLevel) and the modifier search (POST /mid/home/ModifierSearch then AjaxHandler595TopLevel) keep their search criteria in the server session behind an anti-forgery token, so they are not exposed as standalone commands. Use get-manufacturer-details or list-wmis-for-manufacturer to find manufacturer IDs, then get-mid-manufacturer.
MID manufacturer IDs are the same numbers as the API's Mfr_ID, e.g. 955 = Tesla, 988 = American Honda.
CSV exports (/mid/Export/ExportToCSV565, ExportToCSV566, ExportToCSV595, ExportAllToCSV595, ExportReplicaToCSV) are browser file downloads tied to the session's last search, so they are not included.

name: nominatim-openstreetmap
description: Nominatim (OpenStreetMap geocoder): search places by free text or structured address, reverse-geocode coordinates, fetch full place details by OSM id, and check server/data status.

commands.name: search-places
commands.summary: Free-text geocoding search for places, addresses or POIs by name. Returns matching OSM objects with coordinates.

params.name: q
params.description: Free-text query, e.g. a place name, address or landmark

params.name: api_limit
params.description: Maximum number of results (1-40, server default 10) (sent to the site as "limit"; clify's own --limit only shapes the output)

params.name: countrycodes
params.description: Comma-separated ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country codes to restrict results to, e.g. us or de,at

params.name: accept_language
params.description: Preferred language(s) for result names, e.g. en or de,en

params.name: layer
params.description: Restrict results to a thematic layer (comma-separated allowed)

params.name: exclude_place_ids
params.description: Comma-separated places already shown, to get the next page of results. Format: OSM type letter plus OSM id (N/W/R + osm_id), e.g. W518071791,R126326

params.name: addressdetails
params.description: Include a broken-down address object (house_number, road, city, postcode, country...) per result

params.name: polygon_geojson
params.description: Include the full GeoJSON outline of each result. This can be very large.

commands.name: search-structured
commands.summary: Structured address/POI search using separate fields (amenity, street, city, county, state, country, postalcode). Can be restricted to a bounding box.

params.name: amenity
params.description: Name or type of POI, e.g. cafe

params.name: street
params.description: House number and street name, e.g. 10 Downing Street

params.name: viewbox
params.description: Preferred search area as lon1,lat1,lon2,lat2 (two corners), e.g. 2.33,48.86,2.37,48.84

params.name: bounded
params.description: With viewbox: only return results inside the box

params.name: dedupe
params.description: Merge duplicate results such as multiple segments of the same street. Server default is true. Set to false to keep all.

params.name: polygon_threshold
params.description: Simplification tolerance in degrees for returned polygons, e.g. 0.01

params.name: api_limit
params.description: Maximum number of results (1-40) (sent to the site as "limit"; clify's own --limit only shapes the output)

params.name: countrycodes
params.description: Comma-separated ISO country codes to restrict results

params.name: accept_language
params.description: Preferred language(s) for names, e.g. en

params.name: exclude_place_ids
params.description: Comma-separated places already shown (N/W/R + osm_id), for the next page

params.name: addressdetails
params.description: Include a broken-down address object per result

commands.name: get-place-details
commands.summary: Get full details of an OSM place by type and id: names, extratags (wikidata, population, website), address hierarchy, linked places, centroid. Optionally includes child places or search keywords.

params.name: osmtype
params.description: OSM object type: N=node, W=way, R=relation

params.name: osmid
params.description: OSM object id (osm_id from search results)

params.name: class
params.description: OSM class/category to pick when an object has several (category from search results), e.g. boundary

params.name: hierarchy
params.description: Include child places that have this place as parent

params.name: keywords
params.description: Include the name and address search keywords indexed for this place

params.name: polygon_geojson
params.description: Include the full geometry as GeoJSON (can be large)

commands.name: reverse-geocode
commands.summary: Reverse geocode a latitude/longitude to the nearest OSM object and its address, at a chosen detail level (zoom).

params.name: accept_language
params.description: Preferred language(s) for names, e.g. en

params.name: polygon_geojson
params.description: Include the GeoJSON outline of the result (can be large)

commands.name: get-status
commands.summary: Check Nominatim server status, software/database version and when the OSM data was last updated.

notes: Public OSM Nominatim usage policy: no more than 1 request per second. Do not bulk-geocode. Results are under ODbL (© OpenStreetMap contributors).

Search results give osm_type as a word ('node', 'way', 'relation'). get-place-details and exclude_place_ids need the letter form instead: N, W or R. Pass search 'category' as get-place-details --class.

Paging search results: there is no page number. Instead, re-run the same search with exclude_place_ids set to a comma-separated list of the places already returned (e.g. W518071791,R126326), and keep adding to the list on each page.
search-structured cannot be combined with q. Give at least one structured field. viewbox is lon1,lat1,lon2,lat2.
polygon_geojson can make responses very large. Only enable it when geometry is needed.
Not covered: /lookup (batch lookup by OSM ids) was not recorded.

commands.summary: Get the latest observed conditions (temperature, wind, etc.) from an NWS weather station

params.name: station
params.description: NWS station id, e.g. LTHC1 (Lost Horse, Joshua Tree)

notes: Park codes are lowercase 4-letter codes such as jotr and yose. search-parks-by-name returns them in uppercase, so lowercase them before passing them to get-park, get-park-alerts or get-park-facilities.
Filter ids for search-parks (activities, topics, states) come from list-park-filters. Comma-separate multiple values.

For a location search, the flow is geocode-suggest, then geocode-location. Pass candidates[0].location.y as lat and location.x as lng to search-parks with sort='distance asc'. Alternatively, search-parks-by-name returns geometry.coordinates as [lng, lat].

Park coordinates for weather lookups are in get-park (containsPlace[].geo) and in search-parks geometry. Round them to 4 decimals for get-weather-point, then use gridId/gridX/gridY with get-weather-forecast.
The /solr/ endpoints return Solr JSON (the web app used JSONP, which is dropped here). In search-multimedia, filter by park using the full park name in Parks_Item.
Multimedia pagination via start was not confirmed during exploration and may be ignored by the server.
Site-wide keyword search is blocked by robots.txt. Event calendars did not load data while exploring, so no event commands are provided.
The apikeys in the central.nps.gov URLs are the public keys embedded in the nps.gov web app.
The api.weather.gov endpoints are third-party (the National Weather Service) and are used by the park conditions pages.
about: National Park Service (nps.gov): find parks by state, activity, topic or location; read park details, alerts, parking and conditions; search articles…

name: nrk
description: NRK (Norwegian Broadcasting) news, sport, culture, TV and radio: the CLI reads news collections and articles, tag, author and review listings, TV/radio broadcast schedules, playback metadata and manifests, radio/podcast catalogs and NRK TV page plugs.

commands.name: get-content
commands.summary: Get an nrk.no content item (article teaser, news collection or stream such as 'Krigen i Ukraina' or the sports news stream) by its 1.<id>, including its latest related items

params.name: id
params.description: NRK content id in the form 1.<number>, taken from legacy article/collection URLs (…-1.11480927)

params.name: api_limit
params.description: How many related items (relations) to include (sent to the site as "limit"; clify's own --limit only shapes the output)

commands.name: list-topic-articles
commands.summary: List articles on an nrk.no topic/tag page (e.g. /atomkraft/, /sverige/) by topic id, newest first, with cursor paging

params.name: cursor
params.description: Paging cursor from the previous page. It is base64 JSON {timestamp, contentId} of the last item seen.

commands.name: list-author-articles
commands.summary: List articles written by an NRK journalist (author profile /forfatter/<slug>-<id>) by author id, with cursor paging

params.name: authorId
params.description: Numeric author id (the trailing number in /forfatter/<slug>-<id>)

params.name: cursor
params.description: Paging cursor from the previous page (base64 JSON {timestamp, contentId} of the last item)

commands.name: list-reviews
commands.summary: List NRK reviews (anmeldelser) of a given category, e.g. books, with score and cursor paging

params.name: reviewType
params.description: Review category key. 'literature' is books (Bøker). Other categories presumably use similar English keys.

params.name: cursor
params.description: Paging cursor from the previous page (base64 JSON {timestamp, contentId} of the last item)

commands.name: list-related-articles
commands.summary: List articles topically related to a given (newer-format /artikkel/<slug>-<id>) article id

params.name: articleId
params.description: Numeric article id (the trailing number in /artikkel/<slug>-<id>)

commands.name: get-epg
commands.summary: Get the broadcast schedule (EPG) for one or more NRK TV/radio channels on a given date

commands.name: get-playback-metadata
commands.summary: Get playback metadata (title, duration, availability, geoblocking, manifest link) for a video clip, TV/radio program, podcast episode or live channel

params.name: id
params.description: Media id. Clips use a UUID, programs ids like MNAN12004326, podcast episodes l_<uuid>, channels ids like nrktv8.

commands.name: get-playback-manifest
commands.summary: Get the playback manifest (stream URLs such as HLS, plus subtitles) for a playable clip, program, podcast episode or channel

commands.name: get-radio-catalog
commands.summary: Get an NRK radio series or podcast catalog entry, including its seasons (months) and links

params.name: slug
params.description: Series/podcast slug, e.g. dagsnytt-atten, politisk-kvarter, kjapt_oppdatert, bakrommet

commands.name: get-podcast-episode
commands.summary: Get details of a single NRK podcast episode (title, date, duration, contributors, playback link)

commands.name: get-latest-episode
commands.summary: Get the latest (or next upcoming) episode of an NRK TV series, e.g. dagsrevyen or nyheter

params.name: seriesId
params.description: TV series slug, e.g. dagsrevyen, nyheter, rykter

commands.name: get-tv-page
commands.summary: Get an NRK TV page (e.g. the front page) with its sections and plug references

commands.name: get-tv-plug
commands.summary: Resolve an NRK TV plug reference (from get-tv-page plugRefs) to its series/program title, description, images and ids

commands.name: list-clip-collections
commands.summary: List the related video collections shown alongside an nrk.no video clip

notes: Keyword search is not available: /sok is disallowed and no search request was captured.
The legacy article/collection ids look like '1.18057825'. Pass them as-is to get-content. The 'relations' array lists child item ids, which you can also fetch with get-content.

Paging on plugs.json (topic, author and reviews) uses an opaque cursor: base64 JSON {timestamp, contentId} of the last item on the previous page. Pass it back via --cursor. The cursor field name in the response was not recorded.
Topic ids, author ids and review category keys are not exposed as listings. Take them from page URLs (/forfatter/<slug>-<id>) or from earlier results.
Many video clips and TV programs are geoblocked outside Norway (nonPlayable.messageType 'ProgramIsGeoblocked'). Radio and podcast content is usually playable everywhere.
The video person/collection load-more (video/api/v1/loadmore) and regional load-more (serum/api/render/<id> with offset params) are not exposed because their parameters were not fully recorded.
get-epg dates are YYYY-MM-DD in Norwegian local time. Today and tomorrow were confirmed to work.
about: NRK (Norwegian Broadcasting) news, sport, culture, TV and radio: the CLI reads news collections and articles, tag, author and review listings, TV/radio…

name: nuget
description: nuget.org, the public .NET package gallery. This CLI searches packages, reads package and version metadata, licenses, owner profiles, and download statistics, and lists NuGet client tool downloads, all without logging in.

commands.name: search-packages
commands.summary: Search the NuGet gallery by keyword or tag (q=Tags:"bson"), with sort, framework, package-type and prerelease filters, 20 results per page

params.name: q
params.description: Search text. Supports field syntax such as Tags:"bson", id:Newtonsoft, owner:jamesnk

params.name: sortby
params.description: Sort order. 'relevance' is the default ranking

params.name: frameworks
params.description: Comma-separated framework generations to filter by, e.g. net, netcoreapp, netstandard, netframework

params.name: tfms
params.description: Comma-separated specific target framework monikers, e.g. net8.0,netstandard2.0

params.name: frameworkFilterMode
params.description: Whether packages must match ALL or ANY of the selected frameworks

params.name: includeComputedFrameworks
params.description: Also match frameworks that are computed as compatible, not only frameworks targeted explicitly

params.name: packagetype
params.description: Restrict results to one package type

commands.name: search-packages-v2
commands.summary: Search packages through the OData v2 API, which returns structured metadata (id, version, downloads, description) with offset paging

params.name: query
params.description: Search term, placed inside single quotes in the OData URL

params.name: skip
params.description: Number of results to skip, for paging

commands.name: get-package
commands.summary: Get the gallery page for the latest version of a package: title, version, target frameworks, install command and README text

commands.name: get-package-version
commands.summary: Get metadata for one package version through the OData v2 API: dependencies, downloads, hash, size, dates, project URL

commands.name: list-package-versions
commands.summary: List all versions of a package with their per-version download counts and publish dates (OData v2 FindPackagesById)

params.name: id
params.description: Package id, placed inside single quotes in the OData URL

params.name: skip
params.description: Number of versions to skip, for paging (the server returns at most 100 per page)

commands.name: get-package-feed
commands.summary: Get the Atom feed of a package's versions, newest first, with update times and links

commands.name: get-package-license
commands.summary: Get the license text of a specific package version

commands.name: get-package-download-stats
commands.summary: Get download counts for a package, broken down by version, client name or client version

params.name: groupby
params.description: Dimension to group download counts by

commands.name: get-package-version-download-stats
commands.summary: Get download counts for one package version, broken down by client name or client version

params.name: groupby
params.description: Dimension to group download counts by

commands.name: get-gallery-totals
commands.summary: Get gallery-wide totals: total downloads, unique packages, total package versions, last update time

commands.name: get-stats-overview
commands.summary: Get the statistics overview: top 10 packages, top 10 package versions, and NuGet client usage over the last 6 weeks

commands.name: list-top-packages
commands.summary: List the top 100 most downloaded packages over the last 6 weeks (all packages, followed by community-only rows)

commands.name: list-top-package-versions
commands.summary: List the most downloaded package versions over the last 6 weeks

commands.name: get-owner-profile
commands.summary: Get a NuGet user or organization profile: package count, total downloads, and the packages they own

commands.name: list-client-downloads
commands.summary: List downloadable NuGet client tools (nuget.exe, VS VSIX, and others) with their versions, URLs and release dates

notes: All commands are public reads. Signing in is only needed for uploading and managing packages, which this CLI does not cover.

Raw .nupkg files can be downloaded directly from https://www.nuget.org/api/v2/package/{id}/{version}. The response is a binary zip, so there is no command for it. The URL also appears in content.@src of the OData results.

OData v2 commands (search-packages-v2, list-package-versions, get-package-version) return Atom XML converted to JSON. Property keys are prefixed 'd:', and typed values live under '#text'. For example, m:properties.d:VersionDownloadCount.#text holds the download count.
d:DownloadCount is capped at 2147483647 (Int32 max) for very popular packages. Use d:VersionDownloadCount, or get-package-download-stats, for real numbers.

In the gallery search, use q=Tags:"name" to search by tag. Package ids in gallery HTML output can contain stray spaces after dots because of <wbr> line-break hints. Remove them before passing an id to other commands.
The stats report endpoints accept repeated groupby values in the web app. This CLI sends a single groupby dimension.
list-top-packages returns the 'all packages' table followed by the community-only table. The 'row' field contains rank, name and downloads together.
about: nuget.org, the public .NET package gallery.

name: ons
description: Office for National Statistics (ons.gov.uk), the UK's official statistics site. This CLI searches publications and data, reads time series values and metadata, bulletins, datasets and the release calendar, and downloads CSV data. It is read-only and needs no login.

commands.name: search
commands.summary: Site-wide keyword search over ONS publications, bulletins, time series and datasets, with content-type and census topic filters, sorting and paging

params.name: filter
params.description: Content type filter. Examples: publications, bulletin, time_series, datasets, user_requested_data. The UI repeats this param when several are chosen.

commands.name: search-timeseries
commands.summary: Search the time series explorer (58k+ series) by keyword and/or topic path; each result shows the series ID (CDID) and dataset ID

params.name: topic
params.description: Restrict to a topic's time series, e.g. /economy/inflationandpriceindices/timeseries

commands.name: get-timeseries
commands.summary: Get time series metadata and its latest value (title, CDID, unit, latest period and value, release dates, source dataset) from the ONS content API

params.name: topic
params.description: Topic path without leading/trailing slash, e.g. economy/inflationandpriceindices or employmentandlabourmarket/peoplenotinwork/unemployment. Take it from a search-timeseries result URL.

params.name: series_id
params.description: Series ID (CDID), lowercase, e.g. l55o, d7g7, mgsx

params.name: dataset
params.description: Source dataset ID, lowercase, e.g. mm23, lms

commands.name: get-timeseries-data
commands.summary: Get the monthly observations of a time series as a list of {date, value} (for quarterly or annual-only series use download-timeseries-csv)

params.name: topic
params.description: Topic path without leading/trailing slash, e.g. economy/inflationandpriceindices

commands.name: download-timeseries-csv
commands.summary: Download a time series as CSV with all frequencies (annual, quarterly, monthly) plus metadata rows; also works for a previous version

params.name: uri
params.description: Time series URI path, e.g. /economy/inflationandpriceindices/timeseries/l55o/mm23. Append /previous/vN for a superseded version.

commands.name: list-timeseries-versions
commands.summary: List previous (superseded) versions of a time series with update date, label/reason and version uri (pass uri to download-timeseries-csv)

commands.name: get-bulletin
commands.summary: Get a statistical bulletin edition: title, summary, release and next-release dates, and its sections

params.name: edition
params.description: Edition slug, e.g. august2026 (take it from list-bulletin-releases)

commands.name: list-bulletin-releases
commands.summary: List all past editions of a bulletin series, newest first

commands.name: list-bulletin-related-data
commands.summary: List the datasets and data related to a bulletin edition

commands.name: get-dataset
commands.summary: Get a dataset page: title, description, release info, any correction notice and the current edition's file download link

commands.name: list-topic-data
commands.summary: List all published data (time series, datasets, user-requested data) for a topic, with keyword filter, sorting and paging

commands.name: list-topic-publications
commands.summary: List all publications (bulletins, articles and so on) for a topic, with keyword filter, sorting and paging

commands.name: list-topic-headline-series
commands.summary: List a topic page's headline (spotlight) time series uris, e.g. CPIH/CPI/RPI for inflation

commands.name: list-releases
commands.summary: List the release calendar (published, upcoming or cancelled releases) with keyword search, sorting and paging, read from the RSS feed

params.name: api_limit
params.description: Results per page (sent to the site as "limit"; clify's own --limit only shapes the output)

commands.name: get-release
commands.summary: Get a release calendar entry: title, release date and time, publication status and summary

params.name: slug
params.description: Release slug, i.e. the last path segment of a release calendar link

notes: No login or API key is needed, and every command is read-only.

ONS content lives under a topic path, e.g. economy/inflationandpriceindices or employmentandlabourmarket/peoplenotinwork/unemployment. Pass it as the 'topic' arg without leading or trailing slashes. The slashes must stay literal in the URL. Search results return full URLs from which you can read the topic, series ID and dataset.
Time series are identified by a lowercase CDID (series_id, e.g. l55o = CPIH annual rate, d7g7 = CPI annual rate, chaw = RPI index, mgsx = unemployment rate) plus a source dataset ID (e.g. mm23, lms).

get-timeseries-data returns only the series' default frequency. For annual, quarterly and monthly values together, use download-timeseries-csv. The CSV starts with metadata rows (Title, CDID, Unit, Release date, ...) followed by period,value rows.
The bulletin edition slug can be 'latest'. The legacy bulletin /data JSON was retired on 02/02/2026, so bulletins are read from HTML.

A public JSON API also exists at https://api.beta.ons.gov.uk/v1 (search, /search/releases, datasets, filters, code-lists, topics). It is documented at developer.ons.gov.uk but was not exercised in this recording.
about: Office for National Statistics (ons.gov.uk), the UK's official statistics site.

name: opam-ocaml
description: opam.ocaml.org is the official OCaml package repository site. This CLI lists all opam packages (by name or by last update), and fetches package and version details, dependencies and reverse dependencies, from the server-rendered HTML.

commands.name: list-packages
commands.summary: List every opam package alphabetically by name, with latest version and description. The full list comes back in one response; filter it yourself to search.

commands.name: list-recent-packages
commands.summary: List opam packages sorted by their most recent publish date, newest first, with latest version and description.

commands.name: get-package
commands.summary: Get details of the latest version of an opam package: synopsis, description, author, license and latest version.

commands.name: list-package-versions
commands.summary: List all published versions of an opam package, with links to each version's detail page.

commands.name: get-package-version
commands.summary: Get details of a specific version of an opam package: synopsis, description, author, license, source URL/checksums and other metadata.

commands.name: get-package-dependencies
commands.summary: List the dependency formula entries (dependencies, optional deps and conflicts) of a specific opam package version, with version constraints.

commands.name: list-package-dependents
commands.summary: List the packages that require a given opam package (reverse dependencies, 'Required by'), with their version constraints.

notes: The site is fully static HTML with no API, no pagination and no login. All data is scraped from server-rendered pages.
Search on the site only filters the full list on the client. To search, run list-packages and filter by name or description locally.
Package detail URLs need a trailing slash (/packages/{name}/). Without it the server returns a 308 redirect.
Version detail pages use the form /packages/{name}/{name}.{version}/, e.g. /packages/dune/dune.3.24.2/. Use list-package-versions to find valid versions.
The 'published' field in list results is the row title attribute, e.g. 'Published: Oct 17, 2026'.
Dependency entries can contain nested 'any of' / 'all of' formulas. The 'text' field holds the full formula when package/constraint only show the first match.
Documentation for a package lives at https://ocaml.org/p/{name}/{version|latest}/doc/index.html.
about: opam.ocaml.org is the official OCaml package repository site.

name: open-meteo
description: Open-Meteo: free, keyless weather APIs. The CLI provides forecasts, historical reanalysis, archived and previous model runs, ensembles, seasonal and climate projections, marine, air quality, satellite radiation, flood, elevation, geocoding and CSV export.

commands.name: search-locations
commands.summary: Find places by name or postal code and get their coordinates, timezone, country and population. Use this first to turn a city name into latitude/longitude.

params.name: name
params.description: Location name or postal code. You can narrow it with ', <country or admin1>', e.g. 'Paris, Texas'. Two characters must match exactly; three or more are prefix-matched.

params.name: language
params.description: Language for the returned names, as an ISO 639-1 code (en, fr, de, ...)

params.name: countryCode
params.description: Return only results in this ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country, e.g. US, GB, DE

commands.name: get-forecast
commands.summary: Weather forecast for one or more coordinates: current conditions plus hourly and daily variables, up to 16 days ahead and 92 past days, with an optional national model (e.g. DWD ICON).

params.name: latitude
params.description: Latitude in WGS84 decimal degrees. Comma-separate values for several locations, e.g. 52.52,48.85

params.name: longitude
params.description: Longitude in decimal degrees. For several locations, comma-separate in the same order as latitude

params.name: daily
params.description: Comma-separated daily variables, e.g. temperature_2m_max,temperature_2m_min,precipitation_sum,sunrise,sunset,weather_code. Needs timezone.

params.name: timezone
params.description: IANA timezone for timestamps and daily aggregation, e.g. Europe/Paris, or 'auto' for the location's timezone. Defaults to GMT.

params.name: forecast_days
params.description: Number of forecast days (0-16). Defaults to 7.

params.name: past_days
params.description: Number of past days to include (0-92)

params.name: start_date
params.description: Explicit start date (yyyy-mm-dd). Use together with end_date instead of forecast_days/past_days.

params.name: models
params.description: Weather model(s), comma-separated, e.g. dwd_icon_seamless, ecmwf_ifs025, gfs_seamless, meteofrance_seamless, ukmo_seamless, jma_seamless. Defaults to best_match.

params.name: timeformat
params.description: Timestamp format: ISO8601 local strings, or unix seconds

commands.name: export-forecast-csv
commands.summary: Download a weather forecast as CSV text (the docs page's CSV export), for spreadsheets or bulk processing.

params.name: latitude
params.description: Latitude in decimal degrees; comma-separate for several locations

params.name: longitude
params.description: Longitude in decimal degrees; comma-separate for several locations

commands.name: get-historical-weather
commands.summary: Historical observed-like weather (ERA5 reanalysis, 1940 to a few days ago) for coordinates over a date range, as hourly and/or daily variables.

params.name: latitude
params.description: Latitude in decimal degrees; comma-separate for several locations

params.name: longitude
params.description: Longitude in decimal degrees; comma-separate for several locations

params.name: timezone
params.description: IANA timezone or 'auto'. Needed for daily values.

params.name: models
params.description: Reanalysis model, e.g. era5, era5_land, era5_seamless, cerra, ecmwf_ifs

commands.name: export-historical-csv
commands.summary: Download historical (ERA5) weather for a date range as CSV text.

commands.name: get-historical-forecast
commands.summary: Archived high-resolution model forecasts (from 2022 onward) for coordinates and a date range, with the same variables and models as the forecast API.

params.name: latitude
params.description: Latitude in decimal degrees; comma-separate for several locations

params.name: models
params.description: Weather model(s), e.g. dwd_icon_seamless, ecmwf_ifs025, gfs_seamless

commands.name: get-previous-runs
commands.summary: Compare forecasts from earlier model runs at fixed lead times by requesting <variable>_previous_dayN variables alongside the current run.

params.name: hourly
params.description: Comma-separated hourly variables; append _previous_day1 ... _previous_day7 to get the forecast issued N days earlier, e.g. temperature_2m,temperature_2m_previous_day1

params.name: past_days
params.description: Past days to include (0-92). Do not combine with start_date/end_date.

params.name: forecast_days
params.description: Forecast days to include (0-16). Do not combine with start_date/end_date.

params.name: start_date
params.description: Explicit start date yyyy-mm-dd (data from Jan 2024; some models from March 2021). Use with end_date instead of past_days/forecast_days.

params.name: models
params.description: Weather model(s), e.g. ecmwf_ifs025, gfs_seamless, dwd_icon_seamless

commands.name: get-single-run
commands.summary: Full forecast horizon of one specific model run, identified by its initialisation time.

params.name: run
params.description: Model initialisation time in UTC, yyyy-mm-ddThh:mm, e.g. 2026-10-17T00:00

params.name: forecast_days
params.description: Number of days of the run to return. Defaults to 7.

commands.name: get-ensemble-forecast
commands.summary: Ensemble forecast with every perturbed member (variable_memberNN), or ensemble mean/spread when you pass a *_ensemble_mean_* model.

params.name: models
params.description: Ensemble model(s), e.g. icon_seamless, icon_global, gfs_seamless, ecmwf_ifs025. For means use dwd_icon_eps_ensemble_mean_seamless or ncep_gefs_ensemble_mean_seamless.

params.name: forecast_days
params.description: Forecast days (default 7, up to 35 depending on model)

commands.name: get-seasonal-forecast
commands.summary: Long-range seasonal and sub-seasonal forecast (ECMWF SEAS5 / EC46, about 6-7 months) with ensemble members.

commands.name: get-climate-projection
commands.summary: Downscaled daily climate-change projections from CMIP6 models for 1950-2050 at a location.

params.name: models
params.description: Climate model(s), comma-separated: CMCC_CM2_VHR4, FGOALS_f3_H, HiRAM_SIT_HR, MRI_AGCM3_2_S, EC_Earth3P_HR, MPI_ESM1_2_XR, NICAM16_8S

commands.name: get-marine-forecast
commands.summary: Marine forecast for a sea location: wave height, direction and period, swell, and ocean currents.

params.name: latitude
params.description: Latitude in decimal degrees (must be over sea)

commands.name: get-air-quality
commands.summary: Air quality forecast: pollutants (PM10, PM2.5, ozone, NO2, ...), pollen, and European/US AQI, both hourly and current.

commands.name: get-satellite-radiation
commands.summary: Satellite-derived solar irradiance (GHI, direct, diffuse, DNI) for a location, near-real-time and archive.

params.name: temporal_resolution
params.description: 'native' returns the satellite's native interval (e.g. 10 min); 'hourly' aggregates to hours

commands.name: get-flood-forecast
commands.summary: Simulated river discharge (GloFAS) near a location, for flood forecasting: 1984 up to about 7 months ahead.

params.name: latitude
params.description: Latitude in decimal degrees (snaps to the nearest river)

params.name: daily
params.description: Comma-separated daily variables: river_discharge, river_discharge_mean, river_discharge_median, river_discharge_max, river_discharge_min, river_discharge_p25, river_discharge_p75

commands.name: get-elevation
commands.summary: Terrain elevation in meters (Copernicus DEM, 90 m) for one or more coordinates.

params.name: longitude
params.description: Longitude(s), comma-separated in the same order

notes: No API key or login is needed. The free tier is for non-commercial use and has rate limits (about 10k calls/day).
All weather endpoints take coordinates. Use search-locations to turn a place name into latitude/longitude (and timezone).
Multiple locations: pass comma-separated latitude and longitude in the same order. The response is then a JSON array with one object per location.
Responses hold parallel arrays: hourly.time[i] belongs to hourly.<variable>[i]. Units are in hourly_units, daily_units and current_units.
Daily variables need a timezone (use timezone=auto). Without one, timestamps are in GMT.
timeformat defaults to iso8601 here for readability (the web docs use unixtime). With unixtime, add utc_offset_seconds to get local time.
weather_code values are WMO codes: 0 clear, 1-3 partly cloudy to overcast, 45/48 fog, 51-57 drizzle, 61-67 rain, 71-77 snow, 80-82 showers, 95-99 thunderstorm.
Ensemble and seasonal responses repeat each variable per member (temperature_2m_member01..memberNN), so they can be large. Request few variables and days.
The CSV export commands return raw text. The xlsx format is also available on the API, but it is binary and not exposed here.
about: Open-Meteo: free, keyless weather APIs.

name: open-smk
description: SMK Open, the art collection of Statens Museum for Kunst (the National Gallery of Denmark). The CLI searches and filters artworks through the public SMK API and fetches artwork details, similar works, enrichment data, curated themes and IIIF image metadata.

commands.name: search-artworks
commands.summary: Search the SMK collection by keyword, with optional facet filters, a date or geo range, language and offset pagination.

params.name: query
params.description: Free-text search keywords. Use * to match all artworks.

params.name: filters
params.description: Comma-separated filters, each written [field:value]. Fields include artist, creator, object_names, colors, content_person, has_image and public_domain.

params.name: range
params.description: Range filter on a date or geo field. Use * for an open end.

params.name: offset
params.description: Index of the first result to return (0-based).

commands.name: list-search-facets

params.name: query

params.name: facets

params.name: filters

commands.name: get-artworks

params.name: object_number

commands.name: get-similar-artworks
commands.summary: Get the object numbers of artworks that are visually similar to an artwork.

commands.name: get-artwork-enrichment
commands.summary: Get enrichment records for an artwork, such as visual feature extraction (brightness, contrast, saturation, colour temperature) and similar-image data.

commands.name: list-themes
commands.summary: List curated themes (e.g. '10 Highlights', 'Animals') with their Danish and English titles and the object numbers of their artworks.

params.name: id
params.description: Theme id, as returned by list-themes.

commands.name: get-iiif-manifest
commands.summary: Get the IIIF Presentation 3 manifest for an artwork: label, rights, attribution, metadata, and canvases with image size and image service URLs.

commands.name: get-iiif-image-info
commands.summary: Get IIIF Image API info.json for an artwork image: full width and height, available sizes, tiles and supported formats, for building zoom or crop URLs.

params.name: image_id
params.description: IIIF image identifier: the last path segment of the service id in the manifest's thumbnail or canvas, e.g. 5x21tg258_KMS6658.tif.jp2.

notes: All data is public; no login is needed.

Artworks are identified by object_number (e.g. KMS6658, KMS1). Matching is case-insensitive. get-artworks accepts several numbers separated by commas; this is also how saved and shared lists (/shared-list?list=IDs) are resolved.

Filters syntax in search-artworks: [field:value] items separated by commas, e.g. [artist:Vilhelm Hammershøi],[has_image:true]. To find the related works of an artist or a portrayed person, filter by artist or content_person.
Values for filters can be discovered with list-search-facets. The facet values come back in the chosen language.

The web app sends an authorization header to similar.api.smk.dk and to enrichment.api.smk.dk/api/themes. If get-similar-artworks, list-themes or get-theme fail with 401/403, that header is required and cannot be replayed.
To build an image URL from a IIIF image service, use https://iip.smk.dk/iiif/jp2/{image_id}/full/!1024,/0/default.jpg (IIIF Image API 2, level 2).
Search pages hold 24 results by default; paginate with offset in steps of rows.
about: SMK Open, the art collection of Statens Museum for Kunst (the National Gallery of Denmark).

name: open-vsx
description: Open VSX Registry (open-vsx.org), the open-source VS Code extension marketplace. This CLI searches extensions and reads extension details, versions, README/CHANGELOG files, reviews, publisher namespaces and the registry change feed through its public JSON API.

commands.name: search-extensions
commands.summary: Search Open VSX extensions by keyword, with optional category filter, sorting and offset paging

params.name: query
params.description: Free-text search term. Omit it to list all extensions, for example the most downloaded or most recently updated.

params.name: category

params.name: extension
params.description: Extension name, i.e. the part after the dot in the extension id

commands.name: get-extension-version
commands.summary: Get metadata of one specific version of an extension. The version can also be 'latest' or 'pre-release'.

commands.name: get-extension-file

params.name: fileName
params.description: File name as listed in the extension's files map. It is case-sensitive, e.g. README.md, readme.md or CHANGELOG.md.

commands.name: list-extension-reviews
commands.summary: List user ratings and review comments for an extension

commands.name: list-extension-versions
commands.summary: List published versions of an extension, newest first, as a version-to-URL map with offset paging

params.name: size
params.description: Number of versions per page (server default 18)

commands.name: query-extensions
commands.summary: Query extension metadata by id (namespace.name), with optional version and all-versions flag; returns one entry per target platform (e.g. linux-x64, alpine-arm64, universal)

params.name: namespaceName
params.description: Return extensions of this namespace only

params.name: extensionName
params.description: Extension name, used together with namespaceName

params.name: includeAllVersions
params.description: Return one entry per version instead of only the latest

commands.name: get-namespace-details
commands.summary: Get a publisher namespace's profile (display name, description, website, social links) and its extensions with stats

commands.name: list-namespace-extensions
commands.summary: List the names of all extensions in a namespace (a map of name to API URL) and whether the namespace is verified

commands.name: list-version-changes
commands.summary: Page through the registry-wide feed of extension version changes (publish/state updates), oldest first, using a cursor

params.name: cursor
params.description: Opaque nextCursor value from the previous page

commands.name: get-registry-version
commands.summary: Get the Open VSX server version and limits, such as the maximum extension size

notes: Extension ids are 'namespace.name' (e.g. redhat.java). Path-based commands take them split into namespace and extension.

Version-specific file URLs (README, CHANGELOG, .vsix, icon) are listed in the 'files' object of get-extension / get-extension-version. File names are case-sensitive (redhat/java uses readme.md, ms-python/python uses README.md).
get-extension-file returns raw text and follows a 302 redirect to openvsx.eclipsecontent.org. Binary files such as .vsix should be downloaded from files.download instead of being read as text.
search-extensions uses offset paging: the step equals size (30 by default). totalSize gives the total number of matches.
The cursor parameter name for list-version-changes was inferred and not seen in the recording. Pass the nextCursor value from the previous response; hasMore=false marks the end.
All commands are anonymous reads. Publishing, reviewing and deleting need an Open VSX access token and are not covered. The full OpenAPI spec is at /v3/api-docs/registry.
about: Open VSX Registry (open-vsx.org), the open-source VS Code extension marketplace.

name: openligadb

commands.name: list-leagues

commands.name: list-leagues-by-season

commands.name: get-current-matchday
commands.summary: Get the current matchday (group) of a league

commands.summary: List all matches (fixtures and results) of one matchday in a league season

commands.summary: List a league season's matches for teams whose name contains the given text

params.name: team

commands.summary: Get full details of one match by matchID: teams, results, goals, location and viewers

commands.summary: List all recorded matches between two teams, identified by teamId

commands.summary: List a team's matches in a time window around today, given as weeks in the past and weeks in the future

commands.name: get-next-match
commands.summary: Get the next upcoming match of a league

commands.summary: Get the most recently played match of a league

commands.summary: Get the league table (standings) for a league season

commands.summary: Get the goal scorers ranking for a league season

commands.name: get-last-change
commands.summary: Get the timestamp of the last data change for one matchday; a cheap poll before refetching match data

notes: The API at api.openligadb.de is public: no login and no API key. It allows 60 requests per minute per IP. Poll get-last-change and only refetch match data when the timestamp changes. Finished seasons never change.

Leagues are identified by a shortcut (bl1 = 1. Bundesliga, bl2, bl3, …). Seasons are identified by their start year (2025 = 2025/2026). Use list-leagues or list-leagues-by-season to find shortcuts. In list-leagues-by-season, resultsUrl has the form /Matches/{shortcut}/{season}.
The website itself is a Blazor/SignalR app (_blazor/negotiate, _blazor/initializers). Match pages render client-side, so match data comes from the API, not the HTML.
search-team-matches and list-matchday-matches share the same URL shape. A numeric third segment is read as a matchday, and text is read as a team-name filter.

Team ids: 40 = FC Bayern München and 7 = Borussia Dortmund were used as examples. Get others from list-teams. The get-match example id (66924) was not in the recording and may need replacing with a matchID from list-matchday-matches.
getgrouptable (group-stage tables, e.g. ucl/2025) returned 404 and is not included.
Data is licensed under ODbL 1.0.
about: OpenLigaDB: a free community sports-results database for the Bundesliga and many other leagues.

name: openstreetmap
description: OpenStreetMap (openstreetmap.org), the free editable world map. This CLI searches places, reads map elements, their history and raw data, gets routes, exports map data for a bounding box, and reads changesets, user profiles, diaries and communities.

commands.name: search-places

params.name: api_limit
params.description: Maximum number of results (1-40) (sent to the site as "limit"; clify's own --limit only shapes the output)

params.name: viewbox
params.description: Preferred area as minlon,minlat,maxlon,maxlat. Results inside it are ranked higher.

params.name: exclude_place_ids
params.description: Comma-separated place_ids to exclude. Use it to get more results after a first page.

commands.name: get-element
commands.summary: Get the detail page of an OSM node, way or relation: name, current version, last editor, changeset, edit comment and tags (as text).

params.name: id

commands.name: get-element-history
commands.summary: List every version of an OSM node, way or relation, with version number, editor, timestamp, changeset and comment.

params.name: json

commands.name: list-area-changesets

params.name: before

commands.name: list-user-changesets
commands.summary: List a user's changesets (edits), newest first. Use --before for older ones.

params.name: before
params.description: Only changesets with id lower than this (pagination cursor)

commands.name: get-user

commands.name: get-user-contributions

params.name: before

params.name: language

params.name: before

commands.name: get-diary-entry

commands.name: list-communities
commands.summary: List the official OpenStreetMap Local Chapters (country or regional organisations) with their websites.

notes: Everything here is a public read and works without logging in.
Typical flow: search-places gives osm_type/osm_id and lat/lon. Feed osm_type/osm_id to get-element, get-element-history or get-element-full, and lat/lon to get-route.
Coordinate order: OSRM paths and bbox strings use lon,lat (minlon,minlat,maxlon,maxlat). Valhalla's JSON uses lat/lon keys.
export-map-data only works for small areas; large bounding boxes return HTTP 400. For big areas use Overpass API, Geofabrik or Planet OSM.
Nominatim and the FOSSGIS routing servers are volunteer-run. Keep to about 1 request per second and avoid bulk use.
robots.txt disallows /api/0.6/* JSON reads, /traces and /note/{id}. get-element-full and export-map-data still returned data in the recording, but use them sparingly.
Diary and changeset listings are cursor-paged with --before=<id>. Pass the smallest entry or changeset id seen on the previous page.
The recording did not capture changeset detail pages (/changeset/{id}), so there is no command for them. Changeset ids are returned by get-element and the list-*-changesets commands.

params.name: page_size

params.name: url
params.description: Openverse image page URL in the form https://openverse.org/image/<id>, where <id> is the image UUID from search-images

commands.name: list-image-sources
commands.summary: List all image content sources (e.g. flickr, wikimedia) with their media counts

commands.name: search-audio
commands.summary: Search openly licensed audio by keyword, with filters for category, length, file extension, license and source

params.name: page_size
params.description: Results per page. Anonymous requests are capped at 20.

params.name: extension
params.description: File extension, e.g. mp3, ogg, flac, wav

params.name: license_type
params.description: Comma-separated usage permissions the license must allow

params.name: source

commands.summary: List all audio content sources (e.g. freesound, jamendo) with their media counts

commands.name: get-rate-limit
commands.summary: Show the current API rate-limit status for this client (requests used and remaining)

notes: All commands call the public API at api.openverse.org/v1, not the openverse.org frontend. The frontend sits behind a Cloudflare bot check, and robots.txt disallows /search/. The only recorded request was a 307 on the openverse.org homepage (E1). These commands are built from the explorer's description of the documented API at api.openverse.org/v1/.

The example IDs for get-image, get-related-images, get-image-oembed, get-audio, get-related-audio and get-audio-waveform are placeholders, because no real UUID was captured. Run search-images or search-audio first and pass a result's id field. These examples will fail verification until real IDs are substituted.
The search-images and search-audio examples ('cat', 'piano') are common keywords, not queries copied from the recording.
Anonymous limits are 20 requests per minute and 200 per day. Use get-rate-limit to check the remaining quota, and keep page_size at 20 or below.

Combining a narrow filter with page 2 can return an empty results array. In the recording this happened with filtered image and audio queries, and also on page 2 of a plain image search. Check the result_count and page_count fields in the raw response before paging further.
Sort order was not tested, so no sort parameter is exposed. No search-suggestion (as-you-type) endpoint was found. All commands are read-only, and none need login.
about: Openverse (openverse.org) is a search engine for openly licensed images and audio.

params.name: type
params.description: Package type filter, e.g. library, symfony-bundle, composer-plugin

commands.summary: Get Packagist-wide totals: packages registered, versions available, and total package installs since 2012.

fields.packages_installed: dl.dl-horizontal dd + dt + dd + dt + dd

notes: Package names are vendor/package. Commands that take them as path params need 'vendor' and 'package' separately, e.g. monolog and monolog.
search-packages (search.json) and list-popular-packages use 1-based 'page'. search-packages-faceted (Algolia) uses 0-based 'page'.

In search-packages-faceted, 'filters' is an Algolia filter expression on the facets 'type' and 'tags', e.g. type:library or tags:logging. URL-encode spaces (%20) because the value goes inside an Algolia params string. The Algolia API key in the URL is the site's public search-only key.
Numbers in HTML-extracted results (downloads, stars, statistics) use spaces as thousands separators, e.g. '598 232 593'.
Stats endpoints return {labels: [...dates], values: {series: [...numbers]}, average}. The last data point is partial.
list-security-advisories returns an object keyed by package name, each holding an array of advisories.
In browse-explore, the 'name' text also contains the version string for New Releases items, e.g. 'imagewize/winespringv1.7.2'.
Not available: the vendor transparency log needs login; repo.packagist.org/p2/ Composer metadata is blocked by robots.txt. Use get-package for the same data.
Packagist asks API users to send a User-Agent with contact info and to avoid scheduling jobs exactly on the hour.
No write commands are included: the only recorded POSTs were the /api/event pageview analytics, which was skipped, and the Algolia search requests, which are reads.

params.name: filter

params.name: token
params.description: Page token from the previous response's symbols.nextPageToken

commands.name: list-importers

params.name: path
params.description: Package import path, slashes kept, e.g. github.com/gorilla/mux

params.name: filter

params.name: token
params.description: Page token from the previous response's importedBy.nextPageToken

commands.name: list-vulns
commands.summary: List known Go vulnerabilities (from the Go vuln DB) affecting a module at a given version (latest by default)

params.name: path
params.description: Module path, slashes kept, e.g. golang.org/x/net

params.name: version

params.name: token

commands.name: get-package-doc
commands.summary: Fetch the rendered documentation page of a package (README, doc text, repo link), optionally at a version (path@version) and GOOS

params.name: path
params.description: Import path, slashes kept, optionally suffixed with @version, e.g. github.com/gorilla/mux, github.com/gorilla/mux@v1.7.0, net/http

params.name: GOOS
params.description: Build context to render docs for, e.g. windows, linux, darwin, js

commands.name: list-std-packages
commands.summary: List the Go standard library packages with links and synopses

commands.name: list-subrepos
commands.summary: List the official Go sub-repositories (golang.org/x/...) with short descriptions

notes: The JSON API at https://pkg.go.dev/v1 is the documented public API (spec at /v1/openapi.yaml). It is rate-limited to about 45 QPS per client and answers 429 when exceeded.
Path params are import or module paths that contain slashes (e.g. github.com/gorilla/mux). Pass them as-is: do not URL-encode the slashes.

Pagination is cursor-based. Pass the nextPageToken from the previous response as --token. Invented tokens return 400. As long as nextPageToken is non-empty there may be more results, even if the current page is short.

Filters are Go-like expressions: ==, !=, <, >, &&, ||, !, plus the functions contains(s,sub), hasPrefix(s,pre), hasSuffix(s,suf) and matches(s,re). The variables are the fields of each list item, e.g. name, kind, path, importedByCounts.packages.
Standard-library versions use the module-style form v1.27.2 (go1.27.2 → v1.27.2). go1.x.y returns 404 on API routes.
list-importers may report total -1 when the count has not been computed yet.
list-vulns returns {items:null,total:0} when a module has no known vulnerabilities. The recorded example golang.org/x/net returned empty at its latest version.
The HTML /search page is disallowed by robots.txt. Use search-packages (the JSON API) instead.

The package page tabs (?tab=imports, licenses, versions, importedby) exist in HTML but were not mapped to extract fields. Use list-versions and list-importers for the equivalent data. A package's own import list is only available on the HTML imports tab.
list-module-packages with path=std likely returns the standard library packages via JSON as an alternative to list-std-packages, but this was not recorded.
about: pkg.go.dev is the Go package and module index.

name: pub
description: pub.dev is the official registry for Dart and Flutter packages. This CLI searches packages and reads package metadata, versions, scores, metrics, docs status, publishers, topics and the atom feeds through pub.dev's public JSON API.

params.name: page

commands.summary: List packages owned by a publisher, with likes, pub points, downloads, latest version and description (scraped from the publisher's packages page).

params.name: publisher
params.description: Publisher ID (a verified domain), e.g. dart.dev

commands.name: list-recent-packages
commands.summary: Get the site-wide Atom feed of the most recently published package versions on pub.dev.

commands.name: list-package-names

commands.name: list-topics

commands.name: list-search-qualifiers
commands.summary: List the search qualifiers (is:, has:, license:, platform:, sdk:, topic:, etc.) and the allowed values for each, for building search-packages queries.

notes: search-packages returns only package names, 10 per page. Use get-package, get-package-score or get-package-metrics to get details for each name.

Search qualifiers can be combined in q, for example 'topic:http platform:web', 'dependency:dio' (packages that depend on dio) or 'publisher:dart.dev'. Use list-search-qualifiers for the valid qualifier values and list-topics for topic names.
The HTML search page (/packages?q=...) is blocked by robots.txt, so always use the JSON search API.
get-package and list-package-versions both call /api/packages/{name}. get-package returns the latest version and list-package-versions returns the full version history.
Package archives can be downloaded from the archive_url field (https://pub.dev/api/archives/{name}-{version}.tar.gz).
Liking a package requires a signed-in Google session. It was not recorded, so it is not exposed.
about: pub.dev is the official registry for Dart and Flutter packages.

params.description: Sort order as 'field,dir'. Examples: relevancescore,desc; cid,asc; complexity,desc; mw,asc; mw,desc; annothitcnt,desc

params.name: start

params.name: api_limit

commands.summary: Keyword search of PubChem bioassays (AIDs)

params.name: api_limit

params.name: api_limit
params.description: Maximum suggestions per dictionary (sent to the site as "limit"; clify's own --limit only shapes the output)

commands.name: get-compound
commands.summary: Full PubChem compound summary record (names, identifiers, properties, safety, pharmacology, etc.) by CID

params.name: heading
params.description: Optional TOC heading that limits the record to one section, e.g. 'Melting Point' or 'IUPAC Name'

commands.name: get-gene
commands.summary: PubChem gene target record by NCBI Gene ID

commands.name: get-bioassay

params.name: record_type

commands.summary: Download a compound's 2D or 3D structure as SDF (MOL) text by CID

commands.name: list-elements
commands.summary: Periodic table: every element with symbol, mass, electron configuration, electronegativity, state, melting/boiling point, etc.

commands.name: list-classifications
commands.summary: List the classification hierarchies in the PubChem Classification Browser (MeSH, ChEBI, ATC, Compound TOC, ...) with their HIDs

commands.name: list-sources
commands.summary: List all PubChem data sources (depositors) with substance/assay counts, category, organization, URL and license

commands.name: list-news
commands.summary: Recent PubChem news and announcements

notes: PubChem's usage policy asks for no more than 5 requests per second. Heavy use is throttled automatically.
The search-* commands embed the keyword inside a JSON query string, so do not put double quotes or backslashes in q.
Paging for search-* uses the 1-based 'start' offset: next page = start + limit.

structure-search returns only hitcount and cachekey. The PubChem web app then lists the hits through sphinxql.cgi using where {"ands":[{"input":{"type":"netcachekey","idtype":"cid","key":"<cachekey>"}}]}. Cache keys expire.
list-elements and list-sources return Table.Row[].Cell arrays. Column names are in Table.Columns.Column, in the same order (e.g. AtomicNumber, Symbol, Name, AtomicMass, ...).
get-* records are PUG View documents: nested Section[] with TOCHeading and Information[].Value (StringWithMarkup / Number / Boolean). Use get-compound --heading to fetch one section only.
robots.txt disallows /rest/pug/... name/property URLs, so this CLI uses the /interactive/rest/pug paths the web app itself calls.
No login or user-specific features exist. The result-list 'Download data' export was not captured.
