name: pubmed-ncbi
description: PubMed (NCBI biomedical literature database): search articles by keyword, author or field-tagged query, with filters, sorting and pagination, and fetch full abstract records, MEDLINE text exports and PMID lists. All commands read the server-rendered search page.

commands.name: search-articles
commands.summary: Search PubMed articles by keyword or field-tagged query with optional filters, sort, author ID and pagination; returns summary results (PMID, title, authors, citation, snippet)

params.name: term
params.description: Search query. Accepts plain keywords and PubMed field tags, e.g. 'crispr', 'Hryhorowicz M', '"Nature"[jour] AND crispr', '31727474[pmid] OR 36163606[pmid]'

params.name: sort
params.description: Sort order. relevance=Best match (the default when omitted), date=Most recent, pubdate=Publication date, fauth=First author, jour=Journal

params.name: filter
params.description: Result filter. Examples: datesearch.y_1, datesearch.y_5, datesearch.y_10 (last 1/5/10 years); years.2020-2025 (custom year range); simsearch1.fha (has abstract); simsearch2.ffrft (free full text); pub

params.name: filter2
params.description: Second filter to combine with the first. Same values as --filter

params.name: filter3
params.description: Third filter to combine with the others. Same values as --filter

params.name: cauthor_id
params.description: Computed author ID. Use it with an author-name term to restrict results to one disambiguated author, e.g. term='Hryhorowicz M' cauthor_id=27699445

commands.name: get-articles
commands.summary: Get full article records (title, authors, affiliations, PMID/PMCID/DOI, journal, abstract, full-text links) for a query, typically a list of PMIDs; this replaces the blocked article detail pages

params.name: term
params.description: Query whose results are shown as full records. For specific articles join PMIDs with OR, e.g. '31727474[pmid] OR 36163606[pmid]'. Any search query also works

params.name: sort
params.description: Sort order: relevance, date (most recent), pubdate, fauth (first author), jour (journal)

params.name: filter
params.description: Optional result filter, e.g. simsearch2.ffrft, pubt.review, datesearch.y_5, years.2020-2025

commands.name: export-medline
commands.summary: Export search results as plain-text MEDLINE/PubMed records (all tagged fields: PMID, TI, AB, AU, AD, MH, DP, etc.)

params.name: term
params.description: Search query or PMID list, e.g. 'crispr' or '31727474[pmid] OR 36163606[pmid]'

params.name: sort
params.description: Sort order: relevance, date, pubdate, fauth, jour

params.name: filter
params.description: Optional result filter, e.g. simsearch2.ffrft, pubt.review, datesearch.y_5

commands.name: list-pmids
commands.summary: Get only the PMIDs that match a search query, as a plain list (up to 200 per page); a cheap way to collect IDs for get-articles

params.name: term
params.description: Search query, e.g. 'crispr' or '"Nature"[jour] AND crispr'

params.name: sort
params.description: Sort order: relevance, date, pubdate, fauth, jour

params.name: filter
params.description: Optional result filter, e.g. simsearch2.ffrft, pubt.review, datesearch.y_5, years.2020-2025

params.name: filter2
params.description: Second filter to combine with the first. Same values as --filter

notes: Every command reads the server-rendered search page https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/?term=...; the format parameter (summary/abstract/pubmed/pmid) picks the output. No login is needed.
Article detail pages (/{pmid}/), cited-by listings, /{pmid}/citations/ and /suggestions/ return 403 for this client. Use get-articles with PMID field tags instead.

A query that matches exactly one article (e.g. a single PMID) makes PubMed redirect to the blocked detail page. To fetch one article, OR its PMID with another, or use export-medline. Some single-hit queries may still fail.
Field tags work inside term: [pmid], [jour], [au], [ti], [tiab], [dp], [mh]. Combine them with AND/OR/NOT.
To combine filters, pass --filter, --filter2 and --filter3; each one is sent as its own repeated 'filter' query parameter.
To search one disambiguated author, set term to the author name and add cauthor_id (e.g. 'Hryhorowicz M' and 27699445). Sorting by date is typical.
export-medline and list-pmids return the text block shown on the page. Split the MEDLINE output on blank lines between records and the PMID list on newlines.
The alerts.json endpoint on cdn.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov only carries site banner notices and is not exposed as a command.
about: PubMed (NCBI biomedical literature database): search articles by keyword, author or field-tagged query, with filters, sorting and pagination, and fetch full…

name: pxdata-stat
description: Statistics Finland's PxWeb statistical databases (StatFin, Paavo postal-code data, etc.). The CLI uses the public PxWeb API v1 to browse databases, subject areas and tables, search tables, read table metadata and query table data.

commands.name: list-databases
commands.summary: List all databases on the server (StatFin, Postinumeroalueittainen_avoin_tieto, Hyvinvointialueet, ...)

commands.name: list-subject-areas
commands.summary: List the top-level subject areas (folders) of a database, e.g. StatFin subject areas like vaerak (population structure)

commands.name: list-tables
commands.summary: List the tables (type 't') or sub-levels (type 'l') inside a subject area of a database

params.name: area
params.description: Subject area id from list-subject-areas, e.g. vaerak, kuol, matk (for Paavo: uusin or arkisto)

commands.name: search-tables
commands.summary: Search a database's tables by free text, title words or variable value codes; query=* with filter=* lists every table with publish dates

params.name: lang
params.description: Language of texts and of the search index

params.name: query
params.description: Search text, a value code (e.g. KU091 municipality code), or * for all tables

params.name: filter
params.description: Restrict where to match: title = table titles only, codes = variable value codes, * = everything (use with query=* to list all tables). Omit for default full-text search.

commands.name: get-table-metadata
commands.summary: Get a table's title and variables, with each variable's code, value codes and value texts (needed before querying data)

params.name: area
params.description: Subject area id. This is the search result 'path' without the leading slash, e.g. vaerak

params.name: table
params.description: Table id including the .px suffix, e.g. 11rc.px

commands.name: get-table-data
commands.summary: Query a table's data values, selecting on one variable (e.g. latest N years with filter=top on timeperiod_y); all other variables return all values

params.name: code
params.description: Variable code to select on (from get-table-metadata variables[].code). StatFin tables use timeperiod_y for years.

params.name: filter
params.description: Selection type: item = a specific value code, top = latest N values (value is N), all = every value (value *)

params.name: value
params.description: Value code for filter=item (e.g. 2024, SSS), a count for filter=top (e.g. 5), or * for filter=all

params.name: format
params.description: Response format. json gives columns plus data[{key:[codes], values:[...]}]; json-stat2 is the compact JSON-stat format

commands.name: get-api-limits
commands.summary: Get the API's usage limits: max cells/values per query, max calls per time window, CORS

notes: Rate limits: at most 40 calls per 60 seconds and 120000 cells per data query. Space out calls and narrow your selections.
Typical workflow: search-tables (or list-subject-areas, then list-tables) to find a table; get-table-metadata for its variable codes; then get-table-data.
Search results return 'path' like '/vaerak'. Strip the leading slash and pass it as --area. Table ids keep the .px suffix (e.g. 11rb.px).
In list-subject-areas and list-tables, type 'l' is a folder/level you can open with list-tables, and type 't' is a table.

get-table-data was not captured in the recording. It follows the documented PxWeb API v1 POST query format, selects on one variable and returns all values of every other variable. Large tables (e.g. 11rc with age) can exceed the 120000-cell limit unless you narrow with filter=item or filter=top.
Variable codes and value codes are the same in every language; only the texts change with --lang. StatFin uses timeperiod_y for years and SSS for 'Total' in sex variables.
Human web page for a table: https://pxdata.stat.fi/PxWeb/pxweb/{lang}/StatFin/StatFin__{area}/{table}/
API documentation: https://pxdata.stat.fi/api1.html
about: Statistics Finland's PxWeb statistical databases (StatFin, Paavo postal-code data, etc.).

notes: Keyword search (/search/) is blocked by robots.txt and the JSON API (/pypi/{name}/json) is disallowed, so there is no search command. To find a package, use its exact name with get-package, or browse list-newest-packages / list-latest-updates.

PyPI sometimes answers HTML pages with a bot 'Client Challenge' page instead of content. This happened for /project/httpx/0.27.0/ and /user/{name}/ profile pages. If get-package or get-package-version returns empty fields, retry later or use the RSS commands.
User profile pages and /rss/user/{name}/packages.xml were not usable (challenge page / 404), so there is no user command.
list-package-releases uses the RSS feed, which only carries the most recent releases. Use get-package-version for a specific older version.

get-github-repo and search-github-issues call api.github.com directly. Unauthenticated requests are rate-limited (about 60 per hour for the REST API and 10 per minute for search). Get owner/repo from the 'Source' link in the get-package sidebar.
The first row of list-top-projects-by-size is the 'All of PyPI' total, not a project.
about: PyPI (Python Package Index): look up Python packages and specific versions, read release, update and new-package RSS feeds, see top projects by size…

notes: All data comes from the public, no-login JSON API at de1.api.radio-browser.info. Other mirrors work the same way (see api.radio-browser.info).

play-station and vote-station are plain GET requests, but they have side effects. play-station counts a click and vote-station adds a public vote. Do not call either one just to read data. Use get-station to see url/url_resolved without counting a click.
During exploration, two unintended votes were sent: one on the jazz search page and one for France Info (1cfb151d-a341-11e9-a787-52543be04c81). The API has no way to undo a vote.
Station search booleans (hidebroken, reverse) are sent as the strings 'true'/'false', exactly as the web app sends them.
The stationuuid returned by search-stations is the uuid that get-station, get-station-checks, get-station-clicks, get-station-history, get-check-steps, play-station and vote-station take.
The list-* commands use the empty path filter by default, which lists everything. Pass --filter for type-ahead suggestions, as the search box does with limit=5.

The site also offers exports of the same station search at /{csv|xml|json|m3u|pls|xspf|ttl}/stations/search on the API host. These were not recorded as separate requests, so no command was made for them.
The geo map request returned an empty body and the add-station form was never submitted, so neither has a command. /json/config is app config and was skipped.

params.name: queryId
params.description: Entity ID (4HHB_2) when from=PDB_ENTITY, or chain instance ID (4HHB.B) when from=PDB_INSTANCE

params.name: queryId

bodyTemplate.query:
query QueryAnnotations(
    $queryId: String!,
    $reference: SequenceReference!,
    $sources:[AnnotationReference!]!,
    $range:[Int!],
    $filters: [AnnotationFilterInput!]
){
    annotations(
        queryId:$queryId
        reference:$reference
        sources:$sources
        range:$range
        filters:$filters
    ){
        source
        target_id
        target_identifiers{
            target_id
            entry_id
            assembly_id
            entity_id
            asym_id
            interface_id
            interface_partner_index
        }
        features {
            type
            provenance_source
            description
            feature_id
            name
            value
            feature_positions {
                beg_seq_id
                end_seq_id
                beg_ori_id
                end_ori_id
                range_id
                open_begin
                open_end
                value
                values
            }
        }
    }
}

notes: Search commands return result_set items. 'identifier' is the PDB ID (or PDBID-assemblyId for assembly searches). The full response also has total_count. Paginate with start in steps of rows (25).
To get the newest entries first, use sort_by=rcsb_accession_info.initial_release_date and direction=desc.

ID formats: entry = 4HHB; polymer entity = 4HHB_1 (entry_entityNumber); chain instance = 4HHB.A (entry.labelAsymId). Use get-structure-chains or get-entry-instances to find valid entity and chain IDs.
search-by-attribute sends value as a string. Numeric range filters (such as resolution) were not captured in the recording and may need the public Search API (search.rcsb.org) instead.
Only experimental entries are returned by default. Ligand and polymer-entity result tabs were not captured, so searches return entries (or assemblies for 3D similarity).
get-entry-file with part=view and format=cif/pdb returns full coordinate files, which can be very large. Prefer part=header for metadata.

Data API (data.rcsb.org/graphql) and Sequence Coordinates API are public and need no auth. The GraphQL bodies used by the web app are replayed here verbatim. The pdbx_struct_assembly_gen selection in get-entry-instances was reconstructed because the recorded query was truncated.
robots.txt disallows /search/browse and /groups/summary, so they are not exposed.

Slugs for get-document, get-member, get-webtv-video and get-calendar-event come from the URLs in search results. A document slug ends in _<dok_id lowercased>, e.g. _hd023408 for motion 2025/26:3408.
Some slugs contain non-ASCII characters (e.g. militara-fragor_ha01föu4). Pass them unencoded.
Search parti uses uppercase codes (V, S, MP…). list-members parti uses lowercase codes (s, mp…).

The member activity filter (by type) and the calendar day/week views use query parameters that were not fully captured. Use get-page with the full site path, e.g. /sv/ledamoter-och-partier/ledamot/<slug>/?doktyp=mot.

For bulk or structured data (documents, votes, speeches, members), Riksdagen also offers the open REST API at https://data.riksdagen.se/ (dokumentlista, voteringlista, anforandelista, personlista; JSON/XML/CSV). It was not exercised here.

params.description: Optional Semantic Scholar API key; reduces 429 rate limiting

params.name: apiKey
params.description: Optional Semantic Scholar API key; reduces 429 rate limiting

params.description: Partial query text, typically the start of a paper title

notes: The web app's own data endpoints are protected. POST /api/1/search (E8) always returned 202 with an empty body. Paper and author pages (E9, E11, E12) returned an AWS WAF bot challenge. /search and the api-docs page are disallowed by robots.txt. These were deliberately not turned into commands, and the CLI does not attempt the WAF challenge (E2/E4/E6). Paper, author, citation and recommendation data instead come from Semantic Scholar's official public API at api.semanticscholar.org, which is the sanctioned way to access the data programmatically.

None of the api.semanticscholar.org commands were verified in this recording. The explorer's unauthenticated calls to /graph/v1/paper/search and /graph/v1/paper/<id> returned 429 Too Many Requests, because unauthenticated traffic shares one rate-limited pool. Pass --apiKey (sent as the x-api-key header; free key from https://www.semanticscholar.org/product/api) and/or retry with backoff. Keyed access is typically limited to about 1 request per second.
Paper IDs are 40-char hex S2 IDs (the last path segment of /paper/<slug>/<id> URLs). Graph API commands also accept prefixed IDs: DOI:, ARXIV:, CorpusId:, PMID:, PMCID:, ACL:, MAG:, URL:.
Author IDs are the numeric last path segment of /author/<slug>/<id> URLs, e.g. 40348417 for Ashish Vaswani.

search-papers pagination: offset + limit must stay below 1000. If you change --limit, step --offset by the same amount. The response's 'next' field gives the next offset and 'total' gives the match count.
Use --fields to request extra data, e.g. abstract, tldr, externalIds, publicationDate, s2FieldsOfStudy, embedding. Nested author fields use dot syntax, e.g. authors.name.

autocomplete-papers (E3) is the only command that returned 200 in the recording, but its suggestions array was empty for 'transformer attention'. It depends on the internal web API (x-s2-client header) and may start being challenged like /api/1/search.
No logged-in or write capabilities were observed: the explorer was signed out, and the only writes were WAF, consent and analytics calls, which were skipped.
about: Semantic Scholar, an AI-powered search engine for scientific literature.

Wsymb2 / wSymb2 is SMHI's weather-symbol code: 1 = clear sky, 2 = nearly clear, and so on up to 27 (snow and thunder). Units: wind (ws, gust) in m/s, wind direction (wd) in degrees, humidity (r) in %, pressure (msl) in hPa, visibility (vis) in km, precipitation in mm. A value of '-' means not available.
Times are UTC ISO strings. In the forecast, localDate is local time, written with a Z suffix.
Metobs open API timestamps (date, from, to, updated) are epoch milliseconds. Quality codes: G = checked and approved, Y = suspect or aggregated, O = unchecked.
Metobs parameter 1 = air temperature (hourly instant value). Other parameter ids exist in the SMHI metobs API (https://opendata-download-metobs.smhi.se/api/version/latest.json).
Warning levels: MESSAGE (advisory), YELLOW, ORANGE, RED. NONE means no warning.
Knowledge-bank articles nested more than two levels deep (e.g. /kunskapsbanken/meteorologi/aska/olika-typer-av-aska) cannot be fetched with get-knowledge-article's topic/slug params.

get-today-times and list-popular-today return JSON whose values are HTML fragments (e.g. 'grid' holds <li class="ht-card"> cards). Parse the text from them.
The public API at api.sunrise-sunset.org/v2 is the cleanest source of exact times. Pass either date or date_start+date_end. Its response shape was not captured in detail, so no resultPath is set.
The monthly calendar's 'show moon phases' option was used, but its query parameter was not captured, so it is not exposed.
Saving to 'My places' and all settings are stored in browser localStorage only. No server write endpoint exists, so there is no write command.
The site's main keyword search appeared blocked during exploration. Use search-cities (autocomplete) or slugs instead.
HTML extract selectors were chosen without a page outline (generic h1/meta/a/table tr). Results may include navigation links, so filter by URL pattern.
about: sunrise-sunset.org gives sunrise, sunset and twilight times for any city.

params.name: slug

Teaser 'url' values are site-relative paths such as /nyheter/utrikes/<slug>. Split the path into category/section/slug for get-article, or pass it unchanged as 'path' to get-related-trailers.
Local articles have four path segments (/nyheter/lokalt/<region>/<slug>), so they do not fit get-article's template. Use get-related-trailers with the full path for those.
list-tag-articles: the first 10 items of a tag page come from the server-rendered page. If cursor "0" fails, start at "10" and follow the returned cursor.
Videos with rights.geoBlockedSweden=true have metadata available everywhere, but the streams only play from Swedish IPs.
In Text-TV responses, subPages[].altText is the readable text. gifAsBase64 is a large image and is left out of the default fields.

Several capabilities seen in the recording are not exposed as commands. The RootQuery and AutoFeedPaginationQuery operations behind section 'load more', weather forecasts (/vader/prognos/<place>) and the sport TV schedule (/sport/tabla, scheduleCategory/date params) were recorded with truncated persisted-query hashes, so they cannot be replayed reliably.
Also not exposed: Målservice live scores come from enetscores with encrypted payloads, and the live blog streams through Firestore listen channels.

params.name: query

params.name: page

commands.name: get-package

commands.name: get-package-readme

commands.name: get-package-releases

commands.name: get-package-builds

params.name: version

commands.name: get-documentation-page

params.name: version
params.description: Package version tag (e.g. 2.104.0), branch name, or '~' for the default documentation version

params.name: path
params.description: Lowercase documentation path after /documentation/, e.g. a module name 'nio' or a symbol path such as 'nioconcurrencyhelpers/atomic' (taken from get-documentation-index paths)

commands.name: get-package-score

notes: Packages are identified by owner/repo, the GitHub path, e.g. apple/swift-nio. Search and listing results return this as 'identifier' and as the relative 'url'.
Search filters go inside the query string itself, e.g. 'networking stars:>500 platform:ios,linux last_activity:>2025-01-01 product:library'. See /faq#search-filters.

get-package-builds rows are grouped by Swift version, newest first (6.4, 6.3, 6.2, ...), with one row per platform in each group. The 'results' text lists the stable result first and the default-branch result second. Pass the build UUID from a /builds/{id} link to get-build.
Build logs returned by get-build can be very large.
Documentation paths are lowercase. Use get-documentation-index to discover paths, then pass the part after '/documentation/' to get-documentation-page.
list-author-packages returns GitHub repository URLs. Strip 'https://github.com/' and '.git' to get the owner/repo for the other commands.
The badge API is disallowed by robots.txt and is not exposed. The site has no login, so every command is read-only and public.

name: swpc-noaa
description: NOAA Space Weather Prediction Center (SWPC): a CLI for live space-weather data. It reads the NOAA R/S/G scales, the planetary K-index, solar wind and F10.7 summaries, GOES X-ray, proton and electron feeds, alerts, text forecasts and the HAPI time-series API.

commands.name: get-noaa-scales
commands.summary: Current NOAA space weather scales and forecast probabilities: R (radio blackout), S (solar radiation) and G (geomagnetic storm). Key -1 is yesterday, 0 is now, 1-3 are forecast days.

commands.name: get-planetary-k-index
commands.summary: Observed 3-hourly planetary Kp index for the last ~7 days, with running a-index and station count.

commands.name: get-kp-forecast
commands.summary: Planetary K-index observations plus the 3-day forecast (observed, estimated and predicted Kp per 3-hour slot).

commands.name: get-summary
commands.summary: Latest single-value summary: solar wind speed, solar wind magnetic field (Bt/Bz) or the 10.7cm radio flux.

commands.name: get-goes-feed
commands.summary: GOES satellite particle/X-ray time series (flux per energy band) for a satellite slot, instrument and time range.

params.name: instrument
params.description: Feed type, e.g. xrays, integral-protons, integral-electrons, magnetometers (see the /json/goes/primary/ directory listing)

commands.name: list-alerts
commands.summary: Active and recent SWPC space weather alerts, watches and warnings with their full message text.

commands.name: get-text-product

params.name: product
params.description: Bulletin name (file name under services.swpc.noaa.gov/text/ without .txt)

commands.name: list-hapi-datasets
commands.summary: Catalog of the roughly 85 HAPI time-series datasets (ACE/DSCOVR/active mag and plasma, Kp, etc.) with ids for get-hapi-info and get-hapi-data.

commands.name: get-hapi-info
commands.summary: Metadata for one HAPI dataset: available parameters, units, cadence and start/stop dates.

params.name: id
params.description: HAPI dataset id from list-hapi-datasets, e.g. kp-pt1h, active-plasma-pt1m, active-mag-pt1m

commands.name: get-hapi-data
commands.summary: Download a HAPI dataset as CSV (time_tag plus the chosen parameters) over a time range: solar wind speed/density, IMF Bt/Bz, Kp/ap, etc.

params.name: id
params.description: HAPI dataset id, e.g. kp-pt1h, active-plasma-pt1m, active-mag-pt1m

params.name: parameters
params.description: Comma-separated parameter names from get-hapi-info, e.g. kp,ap or speed,density,temperature or bt,bz_gsm. Omit for all.

notes: All data is public and needs no login. Most commands hit services.swpc.noaa.gov or the HAPI server at tlv-swpc.woc.noaa.gov, not the www site.
The site has no keyword search, filters or sorting. Pick data by command and path parameters instead.
get-noaa-scales returns an object keyed by day offset. "-1" is the previous day, "0" is current conditions, and "1"-"3" are forecast days with R MinorProb/MajorProb, S Prob and the G scale.
get-goes-feed responses can be large (one row per minute per energy band). Use range 6-hour or 1-day for recent values. Field 'electron_contaminaton' is misspelled as in the source.
get-hapi-data returns CSV text whose first line is the header. Keep time ranges short for 1-minute datasets (pt1m). Fill value is -1e30.
get-kp-forecast, list-alerts and get-text-product use feeds the explorer named in its summary; their exact URLs did not appear in the endpoint list.

News articles (/news-archive?page=N, /news/{slug}) and product pages (/products/{slug}) are server-rendered HTML that redirect (301) to spaceweather.gov. They are not covered because no page structure was recorded.
about: NOAA Space Weather Prediction Center (SWPC): a CLI for live space-weather data.

search-site: pageIndex is 0-based and only pages within a single documentType. sortBy=relevance returned 0 results, so results are always sorted newest first (dateTime_dt desc).

The site is behind AWS WAF bot protection. Requests may get 403 or an empty challenge response, especially POST /discover/movie (filters), which is not exposed. discover-movies uses POST /discover/movie/items, which worked during exploration.

notes: The JSON API commands use the free public key 123 (/api/v1/json/123/...). On the free tier some endpoints are limited. The docs say searchteams.php only works for 'Arsenal', and list results may be truncated (e.g. all_leagues and lookup_all_players returned 10 items). For other teams, use search-site to find the team id/slug, then get-team, list-team-last-events or list-team-players.

Ids chain across commands: idTeam comes from search-teams, search-site URLs (/team/{id}-{slug}) or league tables. idLeague comes from list-leagues (4328 = English Premier League). idEvent comes from fixtures lists.
HTML detail commands take id-slug path values exactly as they appear in site URLs (e.g. 133604-arsenal). The plain numeric id usually works too.
list-season-events: the site's own links append filters to the path as '&t=133604-arsenal' or '&r=07'. Passing them as query params (?t=, ?r=) is expected to work but was not verified.
The league table HTML (/table.php?l=&s=&sort=<col>&dir=asc|desc) only adds server-side sorting. Use get-league-table and sort client-side instead.
All times are UTC unless a field says local (strTimeLocal, dateEventLocal). Numeric values in the API come back as strings.

name: tidesandcurrents-noaa
description: NOAA Tides & Currents (CO-OPS): find tide, current and observation stations and fetch tide predictions, water levels, weather, current predictions, datums, harmonic constituents, sea level trends and storm surge alerts through NOAA's public metadata and data APIs.

params.name: expand

commands.summary: Get metadata for one station by ID (name, location, timezone, flags) with optional expanded products, datums, details, notices, benchmarks

params.name: expand

commands.summary: Get tidal datums for a station (MLLW, MHHW, MSL, NAVD88 etc.) plus LAT/HAT and record min/max

commands.name: get-harmonic-constituents
commands.summary: Get tidal harmonic constituents (M2, S2, K1...) for a station: amplitude, phase, speed

commands.name: get-nearby-stations
commands.summary: List the stations nearest to a given station, with distance and station type

commands.name: get-tide-prediction-offsets
commands.summary: Get tide prediction offsets for a station (reference vs. subordinate, time/height offsets to its reference station)

commands.name: get-tide-predictions
commands.summary: Get tide predictions for a station: high/low times and heights or a regular time series, for a date or date range

params.name: date
params.description: Relative date: today, latest or recent. Use this OR begin_date/end_date OR range.

params.name: range
params.description: Number of hours (used with begin_date or end_date, or alone for the last N hours)

params.name: interval
params.description: hilo = high/low tides only; h = hourly; or minutes

params.name: time_zone

commands.name: get-observations
commands.summary: Get observed data for a station: water levels, air/water temperature, wind, air pressure, humidity, visibility, conductivity, salinity, air gap

params.name: product
params.description: Data product. Not every station offers every product; check get-station-sensors or get-data-inventory first.

params.name: date
params.description: Relative date: today, latest or recent (last 72h). Use this OR begin_date/end_date OR range.

params.name: range
params.description: Number of hours (with begin_date/end_date, or alone for the last N hours)

params.name: datum
params.description: Vertical datum (required for water level products, ignored otherwise)

params.name: interval
params.description: Set to h for hourly met data (default is 6-minute)

params.name: station
params.description: Current prediction station ID (find via list-stations --type currentpredictions)

params.name: date
params.description: Relative date: today, latest or recent. Use this OR begin_date/end_date OR range.

params.name: interval
params.description: MAX_SLACK = max flood/ebb and slack events only; or minutes for a time series

params.name: bin
params.description: Depth bin number (omit for the station's default bin)

commands.name: list-tide-prediction-regions
commands.summary: Browse tide prediction geographic groups: top-level regions (lvl=4), states (lvl=5), or children of a parent group

params.name: parent
params.description: Parent geoGroupId to list its sub-groups (e.g. 1743 = U.S. West Coast)

commands.name: list-tide-prediction-group-stations
commands.summary: List the sub-areas and tide prediction stations inside a geographic group (e.g. a state such as 1403 = Massachusetts)

commands.name: list-current-prediction-groups
commands.summary: Get the full hierarchy of current prediction regions and their stations (coast > state > area > station with bin)

commands.name: list-ports-stations

commands.name: get-data-inventory
commands.summary: Get a station's data inventory: which parameters it has measured and over what date ranges

commands.name: list-sea-level-trends
commands.summary: List relative sea level trends (inches/decade, period of record) for all US or global stations, or one station

commands.name: export-sea-level-trend-csv

commands.name: list-storm-surge-events
commands.summary: List active storm surge / coastal inundation events (storm name, type, analysis, links)

commands.name: list-news
commands.summary: List recent NOAA Tides & Currents news posts

notes: No login needed; all endpoints are public NOAA APIs (metadata API mdapi/prod, data API api/prod/datagetter).

Station IDs are 7-digit strings for water level/tide stations (e.g. 9447130 Seattle, 8518750 The Battery); tide-prediction-only subordinate stations may look like 'TPT2705'; current stations look like 'cb0102' or 'PUG1515'.

For datagetter commands (get-tide-predictions, get-observations, get-current-predictions) give exactly one time spec: --date (today/latest/recent), or --begin_date + --end_date, or --range. Max span is about 31 days for 6-minute data and predictions, 1 year for hourly data.
Water level products need a datum (default MLLW); Great Lakes stations use IGLD or LWD.

Errors from datagetter come back as HTTP 200 with {"error":{"message":...}}, e.g. when a station doesn't have the requested product. Check get-station --expand products or list-stations --type to see what a station offers.
Use list-stations --type currentpredictions to find current prediction station IDs and bins. The site's current-station name search is just a client-side filter over that list.
list-stations without --expand returns a compact list; with expand, waterlevels and currentpredictions can return thousands of large entries.
about: NOAA Tides & Currents (CO-OPS): find tide, current and observation stations and fetch tide predictions, water levels, weather, current predictions, datums…

The API is rate-limited to roughly 20 calls per 10 seconds per IP. An HTTP 429 means wait and retry.
IDs: the show ID appears in website URLs as /shows/{id}/slug (Breaking Bad = 169), the person ID as /people/{id}/slug, and the episode ID as /episodes/{id}/slug.
Season IDs are not season numbers. Get them from list-show-seasons, then pass one to list-season-episodes.
Embedded data appears under _embedded. Credit links to characters and shows appear under _links.*.href, and their trailing number is the ID.
A 404 means no match. For example, lookup-show or single-search-show return 404 when nothing is found.
list-shows pages are blocks of 250 show IDs. Paging past the last page returns 404.
The summary fields contain HTML markup.

params.name: query

commands.summary: List occupational fields (ammattialat) with their info page paths

commands.summary: Read an occupation info page (job description, education, outlook) by slug

notes: search-jobs: leave out the optional filters (municipality, publishedAfter) when they are not needed. The web app omits a filter key entirely when it is unused.
search-jobs paging is zero-based. Pages are counted from 0, the response's lastPage is the highest page index, and totalElements is the hit count.

Other job search filters were seen in the UI but their request body keys were not captured: occupation group (ISCO code, e.g. 3), working time (TYÖAIKA code, e.g. 01 = full-time) and application deadline. Use list-codes or list-isco-occupations to interpret the codes in results.
Job posting fields such as workTime, employmentRelationship, continuityOfWork and municipality values are KOPA codes. Resolve them with list-codes (TYÖAIKA, PALVELUSSUHDE, TYÖN_JATKUVUUS, KUNTA).

Training data comes in three levels. A training or course (get-training) belongs to a serviceOffering, which belongs to a service. Use get-service with serviceOffering.service.token to read the general service description.
Most text fields are multilingual objects keyed fi/sv/en, or arrays of {language, value}.
Favorites, saved searches and profile features require a Suomi.fi login and are not available.
about: Työmarkkinatori (tyomarkkinatori.fi), the Finnish public employment services portal.

name: uniprot

commands.summary: List the valid result field names (for --fields) and the sortable fields of a UniProt database

commands.summary: List the query field terms usable in UniProtKB queries (e.g. accession, gene, organism_id, reviewed), with examples

params.name: query
params.description: Name text (e.g. 'mouse') or field query such as 'parent:9606' or 'ancestor:9605'

params.name: api_fields
params.description: Comma-separated result fields (sent to the site as "fields"; clify's own --fields only shapes the output)

commands.name: get-taxonomy
commands.summary: Get a taxonomy node by NCBI taxon id: names, rank, parent, full lineage, links and protein/proteome counts

params.name: taxonId
params.description: NCBI taxonomy id, e.g. 9606 for human

commands.name: search-keywords
commands.summary: Search UniProt controlled keywords (KW-xxxx) by name

params.name: api_fields
params.description: Comma-separated result fields (sent to the site as "fields"; clify's own --fields only shapes the output)

commands.name: get-keyword
commands.summary: Get a UniProt keyword: definition, synonyms, parent hierarchy, category and protein counts

commands.name: search-diseases
commands.summary: Search UniProt human disease entries (DI-xxxxx) by name

params.name: api_fields
params.description: Comma-separated result fields (sent to the site as "fields"; clify's own --fields only shapes the output)

commands.name: get-disease
commands.summary: Get a disease entry: definition, alternative names, cross-references (MIM, MedGen, etc.), keywords and protein counts

commands.name: search-uniref
commands.summary: Search UniRef sequence clusters (100%, 90% and 50% identity); filter identity in the query, e.g. 'hemoglobin AND identity:0.9'

params.name: query
params.description: UniRef query; add 'AND identity:1.0|0.9|0.5' to restrict the cluster level

params.name: api_fields
params.description: Comma-separated result fields (sent to the site as "fields"; clify's own --fields only shapes the output)

commands.name: search-proteomes
commands.summary: Search proteomes by organism name; filter in the query, e.g. 'human AND proteome_type:1' for reference proteomes

params.name: api_fields
params.description: Comma-separated result fields (sent to the site as "fields"; clify's own --fields only shapes the output)

commands.name: get-proteome
commands.summary: Get a proteome by UPID: description, taxonomy, type, and components (chromosomes) with protein counts

params.name: upid
params.description: Proteome id, e.g. UP000005640 (human reference proteome)

commands.name: get-alphafold-prediction
commands.summary: Get the AlphaFold predicted structure for a UniProt accession: confidence (pLDDT) and download URLs for PDB, CIF and PAE files

notes: Everything is a public read-only API at rest.uniprot.org. No login is needed.

Website facet filters become query clauses. Examples: reviewed:true (Swiss-Prot), model_organism:9606, organism_id:10090, existence:1, annotation_score:5, length:[100 TO 500]. Combine them with AND, e.g. '(hemoglobin) AND (reviewed:true)'.
Sort syntax for the REST API is '<field> asc|desc', e.g. 'length desc'. The website URL form sort=length&dir=descend does not work against the API.
Pagination is cursor-based. The next-page URL is returned in the HTTP 'Link' response header, not in the JSON body. Use --size (max 500) and narrow the query rather than paging.
Use list-result-fields to find valid --fields names and list-protein-search-fields to find query terms. Use suggest-terms to resolve keyword, organism or taxonomy names to ids.

Ids chain between commands: search-proteins primaryAccession → get-protein, download-protein, list-protein-publications, get-protein-history, get-alphafold-prediction. The organism.taxonId field → get-taxonomy. search-uniref id → get-uniref-cluster and list-uniref-members. search-proteomes id → get-proteome.
BLAST, ID mapping and basket features were not recorded, so they are not covered.
about: UniProt, the Universal Protein Resource.

Agency, PositionScheduleTypeCode, JobCategoryCode, Page, SortField and SortDirection follow the same envelope but their key names are inferred from the UI URL params (a, ws, j, p, s/sd).

Bare city names can resolve to the wrong place: 'Denver' resolved to 'Denver, Arkansas' and returned 0 jobs. Pass 'City, State' or use suggest-locations first. ResolvedLocations in the raw response shows how the location was interpreted.
The recording did not show a remote-only filter (UI param rmi=true) in the search body, so the command does not expose one. Facet counts, including remote, are in the raw response under 'f'.
Use the DocumentID (or the number at the end of PositionURI) from search-jobs as the id for get-job. get-job reads the schema.org JobPosting JSON-LD embedded in the announcement page.
Applying and saving jobs require a login.gov-authenticated USAJOBS session. save-job without a session redirects (302) to sign-in. Applying was not recorded and is not supported.
list-events returns the first 10 events. The event list's pagination parameter was not recorded.

get-continuous-data accepts either time_series_id, or monitoring_location_id plus parameter_code. Give at least one of these.
find-monitoring-locations-by-number is a read-only CQL2 JSON search sent as a POST; it does not modify data.

params.description: Text to search for in labels and aliases

params.name: uselang
params.description: Language for the returned labels and descriptions

params.name: api_limit
params.description: Maximum results per page (max 50) (sent to the site as "limit"; clify's own --limit only shapes the output)

params.description: Offset for the next page; use the 'search-continue' value from the previous response

commands.summary: Get the full JSON of one entity by ID: an item (Q42), property (P31), lexeme (L7) or other entity type. Includes labels, descriptions, aliases, claims, sitelinks, and lexeme forms/senses. Optionally f

params.name: id
params.description: Entity ID, e.g. Q42 (item), P31 (property), L7 (lexeme)

params.name: revision
params.description: Specific revision ID to fetch (the entity's lastrevid by default)

commands.summary: Batch-fetch one or more entities by ID through wbgetentities, limited to the chosen parts (claims, labels, descriptions, aliases, sitelinks, info) and languages.

params.name: props
params.description: Pipe-separated parts to return: info, sitelinks, sitelinks/urls, aliases, labels, descriptions, claims, datatype

params.name: languages
params.description: Pipe-separated language codes to filter labels and descriptions, e.g. en|de

commands.summary: Export one entity as RDF, in Turtle (ttl) or N-Triples (nt).

commands.summary: Run Wikidata property constraint checks on an entity. Returns violations, warnings and suggestions per statement.

params.name: id
params.description: Pipe-separated entity IDs to check, e.g. Q42 or P31

params.name: status
params.description: Pipe-separated result statuses to include: violation, warning, suggestion, bad-parameters, compliance, exception, todo, not-in-scope, deprecated

commands.name: parse-value
commands.summary: Parse user-typed text (a date, quantity, coordinate, etc.) into a Wikibase datavalue JSON for a given datatype, the same way the statement editor does.

params.name: datatype
params.description: Property datatype, e.g. time, quantity, string, globe-coordinate, wikibase-item, url, external-id, monolingualtext

params.name: values
params.description: Pipe-separated raw input strings to parse, e.g. '1952' or '11 March 1952'

params.name: validate
params.description: Also validate the parsed values against the datatype

params.name: uselang
params.description: Language the input is written in

commands.name: format-value
commands.summary: Render a Wikibase datavalue JSON as human-readable text or HTML, e.g. resolve an item ID to its label.

params.name: datatype
params.description: Property datatype of the value, e.g. wikibase-item, time, string

params.name: uselang
params.description: Language for labels in the output

notes: Entity ID prefixes: Q = item, P = property, L = lexeme. Lexeme forms and senses use IDs like L7-F4 and L7-S1. The 'entities' object in get-entity and get-entities is keyed by entity ID.
Full-text search (Special:Search), RecentChanges, WhatLinksHere and /w/index.php pages are blocked by robots.txt. Use search-entities, which matches labels and aliases only.
search-entities pagination: pass the 'search-continue' value from the response as --continue.
Use a statement's 'id' from get-entity claims to edit it with set-claim. Pass the entity's lastrevid as --baserevid to avoid overwriting concurrent edits.
set-claim makes a real, public edit to Wikidata. Without a logged-in session the edit is attributed to your IP address (the anonymous CSRF token is '+\'). Follow Wikidata's editing and bot policies.
For complex queries (filtering or joining many entities), use the Wikidata Query Service SPARQL endpoint at https://query.wikidata.org/sparql. It is outside this recording.

Times are ISO 8601 in the location's local time zone; temperatures °C, wind m/s, precipitation mm, tide/water level cm.
get-forecast returns daily intervals; the raw forecast response also contains finer-grained interval arrays (hourly) if you need them.
Warning results include large GeoJSON polygons (areasFeatureCollection); filter by county client-side using meta.areas / region names from list-regions.
Mountain pass list has 61 routes; filter by the 'collection' field (fjell-sor = southern Norway, fjell-nord = northern Norway). Location ids in get-mountain-pass can be passed to get-forecast.
Meteorologist posts come from a Sanity GROQ API; the keyword match uses wildcards around q. Text is Norwegian.

Saving locations to 'Mine steder' requires an NRK login and is not exposed. Service announcements (/api/v0/serviceannouncements/web) usually return {message:null} and are omitted. Raw data for heavy use should come from the official api.met.no (see developer.yr.no).
